proposals.user_asks: When you tell me to do something important, prepare it, show me the exact target and expected result on my pendant, and only carry it out if I confirm before the plan expires; if the page, file, or person changed meanwhile, stop and ask again.
proposals.why_useful: Prevents a stale judgement from changing the wrong account, document, recipient, or GUI state. It is genuinely hive-native: perception on the Mac/browser supplies a fresh target proof, judgement creates the plan, the relay holds the lease while the owner is away, and the pendant is the final confirmation and failure channel.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for plan compilation and target-diff summaries; use realtime only for the spoken confirmation and terse result. No model should decide whether a proof hash matches; that is deterministic code.
proposals.latency_budget: Prepare in 1–3 seconds; confirmation feedback under 500 ms when relay/Mac are online; after confirmation, execute within 10 seconds or report lease expiry. A disconnected pendant leaves the lease queued durably rather than executing silently.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per invocation when a compact deterministic diff is used; dominant cost is one small judgement/summary call, not realtime audio. Screenshots or large page extracts should be hashed locally and sent only when needed.
proposals.security_concerns: The lease must contain target identity, surface/session/tab, normalized precondition hash, expected postcondition, expiry, privacy class, reversibility, and confirmation nonce. Never transmit page secrets in the pendant prompt; display redacted recipient/domain and change summary. Irreversible actions require explicit press-and-hold or two presses; cancellation and expiry must be idempotent. Send only hashes and minimum evidence to relay; retain full evidence locally with bounded TTL.
missing: Typed ActionProof/ActionLease schema shared by judgement, perception, Mac/browser executors, relay, and pendant
Deterministic precondition/postcondition verifier that runs after execution and returns VERIFIED, FAILED, or UNKNOWN
Relay durable lease queue with expiry, nonce replay protection, and pendant delivery/ack receipts
Pendant UI/firmware affordance for redacted diff plus confirm/cancel/expired states
Executor gate that refuses execution when the proof is stale or target affinity is lost
Fresh post-action perception request tied to the same target and attempt ID

proposals.user_asks: When I press and hold the pendant as I leave my desk, put my digital workspace into privacy mode: lock the Mac, pause screen sharing and recording, close or blur sensitive browser tabs, stop any pending computer-use loop, and tell me on the pendant exactly what was secured. When I return and press again, restore only the approved workspace—not passwords, submitted forms, or private tabs that were intentionally closed.
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a physical, dependable privacy boundary without finding the Mac or speaking aloud in a public place. It uniquely combines the pendant's physical presence and offline button, the always-awake relay's intent and audit trail, the Mac's lock/screen controls, and the browser's authenticated tab/session reach. No single node can provide that boundary safely.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic policy and OS/browser APIs for locking, pausing, and tab handling; use a cheap background model only to classify currently open surfaces into sensitive/non-sensitive when the owner has enabled that policy. Realtime is unnecessary except for an optional spoken confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Physical press acknowledgement under 300 ms locally; Mac privacy actions within 2 seconds; relay records completion within 5 seconds. If disconnected, the pendant still enters local 'privacy requested' state and retries; it must never claim the Mac is secured until receipt arrives.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for configured app/domain rules; under $0.01 only when semantic classification of an unfamiliar tab is needed. Main cost is implementation and OS/browser integration, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: The action must fail closed: uncertain sensitive classification means leave the tab open but lock the Mac and report it. Never transmit page contents or credentials to the relay. Require a deliberate long press, bind restore to the same device/session identity, maintain an append-only local audit receipt, and never auto-reopen authenticated pages or undo irreversible user actions. Screen recording must be explicitly stopped through approved APIs, with a visible report if permission is unavailable.
missing: Pendant firmware state machine for offline privacy-mode trigger and retry/result indication
Authenticated relay endpoint for privacy-mode intents, receipts, and replay-resistant device identity
Mac privileged-but-minimal privacy controller for lock, screen-sharing/recording pause, and stopping active automation loops
Browser bridge commands to classify, blur, suspend, or close tabs with an owner-defined restore policy
A policy store mapping apps/domains to sensitive, suspendable, closeable, or never-touch categories
Cross-node completion receipt that distinguishes secured, partially secured, and unable-to-secure states

proposals.user_asks: “If a website needs me to sign in, approve a device, or solve a CAPTCHA while you’re doing the task, pause there, tell me exactly what to do, and continue automatically when I’m back in.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an otherwise correct cross-device job fails or risks exposing credentials when a private site presents 2FA, passkey approval, CAPTCHA, or a re-auth screen. The browser is the only surface with the session; the pendant is the only surface guaranteed to reach the owner. A bounded handoff lets the owner satisfy the challenge without dictating secrets, then resumes the exact task with evidence and no duplicate submission.
surfaces: relay-realtime detects a typed auth-challenge event and gives a short pendant prompt with a one-time task code
browser-extension pauses the bound tab/session before mutation, records challenge type and URL/origin, and waits for completion
mac-planner owns the durable job/checkpoint and resumes only when the same tab/session reports authenticated continuity
faculty-action executes the remaining typed steps and emits a receipt; pendant button can cancel and trigger cleanup
dashboard shows challenge history, expiry, and whether the job resumed or was abandoned
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background planner/state machine for detection, checkpointing, and resume; realtime only for the concise pendant prompt and owner reply. No model should be given passwords, OTPs, or page secrets.
proposals.latency_budget: Challenge detection under 1 second; pendant prompt under 2 seconds; after owner completes the challenge, resume within 3 seconds. Challenge leases expire after 5 minutes by default and require a new prompt.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per job, usually zero extra model calls; cost is dominated by durable browser polling and receipt storage, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Never transmit credentials, OTP values, passkeys, or CAPTCHA contents to the relay/model. Verify origin, tab/session binding, and a nonce; reject unexpected navigation and stale completion signals. Require explicit owner button press to resume, and require a fresh approval at the final irreversible step. On timeout/cancel, clear sensitive form fields where possible and leave an auditable receipt.
missing: Typed browser auth_challenge and auth_resolved events with origin, tab/session id, nonce, and expiry
Durable checkpoint/resume state machine with idempotency keys and duplicate-submit protection
Browser extension UI to show a local-only challenge banner and report completion without contents
Pendant prompt/button protocol for challenge handoff and cancel
Planner/action adapters for passkey/device approval, OTP entered locally, CAPTCHA, and re-auth flows

proposals.user_asks: “When you reach a login checkpoint during a task, hand it to me privately, then continue from exactly where you stopped without asking me to reveal the code or start over.”
proposals.why_useful: A private-site task should not fail merely because the site requires a passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, or re-authentication. The browser is the only place holding the session, while the pendant is the only surface guaranteed to reach the owner. This gives the owner a secure local handoff and preserves the task's progress without leaking credentials to the model.
surfaces: browser-extension detects and freezes at an authentication challenge, bound to the exact origin, tab, and session
relay-realtime sends a redacted challenge prompt to the pendant only
pendant displays the challenge kind and offers signed continue/cancel button actions; secrets remain local to the browser
mac-planner persists the checkpoint and resumes the same job only after matching nonce/origin/session resolution
faculty-action executes the remaining steps and writes a receipt; dashboard shows expiry, resume, abort, and cleanup state
proposals.model_tier: A cheap deterministic state machine handles challenge detection, checkpointing, nonce validation, and resume. Realtime is used only for the short pendant prompt; no model receives the secret or challenge contents.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect and notify within 2 seconds; resume within 3 seconds after the owner completes the local challenge. Expire the handoff after 5 minutes or any unexpected navigation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per task, generally no additional inference; durable browser polling and event/receipt storage dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: OTP, passkey, password, and CAPTCHA contents must never leave the browser or be placed in model context. Bind the handoff to origin, tab/session, job, nonce, and expiry; require an explicit pendant action to continue; use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate submission; cancel and clear sensitive fields on timeout where possible; require separate approval for the final irreversible step.
missing: A typed auth_challenge/auth_resolved protocol across browser bridge, relay, Mac runner, and pendant
Durable checkpoint/resume state machine with idempotent continuation and cleanup
Browser-local challenge banner and completion signal that carries no secret contents
Pendant signed continue/cancel interaction and local challenge status display
End-to-end tests for passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, re-auth, timeout, navigation, and duplicate-submit cases

proposals.user_asks: Start this task here, keep working while I move around, and come back to me only when you need a decision or can prove it is finished.
proposals.why_useful: Today a task begun in conversation is either tied to one surface or becomes an opaque background job. The owner should be able to leave the Mac, receive a concise interruption on the pendant when execution encounters a real fork, answer naturally, and then get a proof-oriented completion report. This is a handoff between the worn conversational surface, always-awake relay, Mac executor, and private browser—not a Mac-only automation.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the short interruption and answer exchange on the pendant. Use a cheaper background model for decomposition, polling, summarization, and receipt generation; deterministic local code handles execution and state transitions.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement on the pendant (<2 seconds). Normal background steps may take minutes. A decision request should surface within 5 seconds of a blocked step, and resume within 2 seconds after the owner's answer reaches the relay.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.10 per task depending on duration and private-page extraction; realtime audio turns dominate, while polling, routing, and receipt generation should be near-zero with a background tier.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must carry only the minimum decision context, never raw private-page contents unless required. Each interruption needs task/session binding, expiry, replay protection, and a clear spoken description of the consequence. No irreversible external submission should happen merely because the owner answered an unrelated pendant conversation; the browser and Mac must enforce the task identity and effect receipt.
missing: A first-class cross-surface task lease that binds pendant conversation, relay job, Mac job, browser session, and current step
A pendant-addressable decision inbox with interrupt/resume semantics and timeout behavior
Typed pause reasons and compact evidence payloads so the relay can ask one precise question rather than replaying full context
A verified effect receipt chain that distinguishes completed, awaiting-owner, expired, and abandoned states
Recovery when either the pendant link or browser extension disappears, without duplicating an already-applied step

proposals.user_asks: If something I asked you to do is blocked because a device or permission is unavailable, keep it safely parked, tell me what is missing, and resume it automatically when that device becomes usable—without repeating completed steps.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action can fail after a long wait (browser extension offline, Mac permissions absent) and the owner must remember and retry. This makes the hive dependable: judgement's intent survives disconnects, the always-awake relay watches readiness, the pendant explains the block, and the appropriate Mac/browser hand executes exactly the remaining steps with a final receipt.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed action envelope with idempotency key, preconditions, expiry, and safe-to-resume policy
relay stores the envelope and subscribes to Mac/browser heartbeat/readiness changes
faculty-perception reports fresh Accessibility/Screen Recording/browser-online facts and distinguishes unavailable from failed
home-macbook-bridge executes resumable Mac steps; browser-extension executes browser steps when polling resumes
pendant presents a short blocked/resumed/completed status and accepts cancel or expiry commands
dashboard shows the exact unmet precondition, next retry time, completed step receipts, and remaining steps
proposals.model_tier: Use the planner/judgement tier once to compile and risk-classify the envelope; use deterministic relay/job code for readiness, retries, leases, and idempotency; use a cheap text model only to summarize failures. Reserve realtime for the pendant's live explanation or cancellation.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate (<1 s) acknowledgement that the job is parked and why; readiness changes detected within one heartbeat (5–15 s); resumed execution starts within 2 s of a valid lease. No polling loop should hold a request open for 45 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per parked/resumed job depending on whether a model is needed for re-planning; most retries and receipts are code-only. Realtime cost occurs only if the owner asks follow-up questions.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only the typed plan, preconditions, and redacted receipts—not page contents or secrets. Never auto-resume an irreversible or externally visible step; resume only idempotent/reversible steps, and invalidate the envelope on expiry, changed tab/session, changed target, or permission scope. Require explicit owner cancellation and show a before/after receipt for any write.
missing: A durable resumable job state machine with per-step checkpoints, leases, retry/backoff, expiry, and idempotency across relay and Mac agent
A readiness-event contract carrying source, timestamp, freshness, and reason (not ready because Accessibility, Screen Recording, or browser bridge is offline)
Non-blocking browser progress events/resumable polling instead of the current single 45-second wait
A typed action-envelope schema shared by faculty-judgement, faculty-action, relay, Mac bridge, and browser bridge
Pendant/dashboard status and cancel controls for parked jobs

proposals.user_asks: Undo the whole thing I just asked you to do, across every device—not merely the last Mac step—and show me what will be restored before you do it.
proposals.why_useful: Today a compound request can touch a private browser session, Mac files/apps, and generated relay artifacts, but undo is surface-local and may leave a half-completed workflow behind. A cross-device compensation plan would let the owner recover from an unwanted result without manually reconstructing every change.
surfaces: faculty-judgement classifies the completed workflow into reversible effects and selects a compensation strategy
faculty-action gathers the signed receipts and before/after evidence from Mac, browser, relay, and pendant-produced artifacts
relay holds the durable cross-surface effect ledger and coordinates an ordered compensation transaction with leases and expiry
home-macbook-bridge performs supported inverse operations on files, reminders, app state, and typed Mac actions
browser-extension restores saved field values or removes drafts only when the original page/session fingerprint still matches
pendant summarizes the proposed restoration and lets the owner approve, cancel, or narrow it
dashboard presents a dependency graph of effects, uncertain steps, and the final restoration receipt
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic compensation planning from typed receipts wherever possible; use the planner tier only to explain ambiguous effects or propose a human-reviewed alternative. Realtime is used only for the owner's spoken approval and status, not for ledger or rollback logic.
proposals.latency_budget: Build the compensation preview in under 3 seconds for a normal job; execute independent inverse steps in parallel and report each result within 10 seconds. Never hold a single synchronous request open while waiting for a device.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually $0.001–$0.02 per undo preview/execution, dominated by an occasional planner call for ambiguous inverse actions; storage and coordination are inexpensive.
proposals.security_concerns: Never infer an inverse for an irreversible external action (sent email, submitted form, deletion without recovery). Require an explicit confirmation for any compensating write, bind restoration to the original device/session and target fingerprint, redact private page contents from receipts, and mark uncertain effects instead of pretending they were restored.
missing: A cross-surface effect ledger with signed before/after receipts and dependency links
A compensation-plan API distinct from the existing single-job or last-action undo endpoints
Stable inverse-operation metadata for each Mac, browser, relay, and artifact action
Target/session fingerprint checks and an uncertainty state for effects that cannot safely be reversed
A pendant approval and dashboard preview surface for whole-workflow restoration

proposals.user_asks: “Make this happen everywhere it needs to, and tell me only when you can prove it worked.” For example: update a private web record, mirror the result into a Mac file or reminder, and leave me a receipt I can trust even if the browser or Mac briefly disconnects.
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can choose a multi-step plan, but action cannot establish end-to-end success: a browser submission may succeed while the Mac mirror fails, or a disconnected surface may make an action look lost. This gives the owner one durable, evidence-backed completion state instead of optimistic acknowledgements or repeated manual checking.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed plan with step dependencies, allowed side effects, and a postcondition for each step
relay durable job runner owns retries, idempotency keys, deadlines, and a durable action ledger
browser extension performs authenticated private-page steps and returns URL/tab, extracted confirmation text, and before/after evidence
Mac agent performs local file/reminder/app updates and returns artifact hashes or API-level confirmation
faculty-perception independently re-reads each changed surface to verify the declared postconditions; it marks unknown rather than success when UI reachability is false
pendant displays a short success/partial/blocked status and lets the owner request retry or inspect the spoken receipt
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for decomposition, retries, and evidence comparison; reserve realtime only for the owner's live request and concise status. Deterministic idempotency/postcondition checks should not consume model tokens.
proposals.latency_budget: A reversible two-surface job should acknowledge in under 1 second, finish in 5–30 seconds when both surfaces are online, and remain durable for hours when offline. Speak only the final verified/partial result; never claim success from dispatch alone.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.02 per completed job depending on whether semantic extraction or conflict resolution needs a model; most steps are relay/database, browser bridge, and Mac-agent calls. Audio/status is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and local artifacts stay on their respective surfaces except for the minimum evidence projection (field names, hashes, and short confirmation snippets). Irreversible steps require the existing approval policy and a fresh consent lease; retries must be idempotent and never blindly resubmit. The receipt should expose exactly what changed, where, when, and what remains unverified.
missing: A durable cross-surface action ledger with step state, idempotency key, dependency, deadline, and evidence references
A typed postcondition verifier that can ask browser and Mac surfaces to re-read state after mutation
A relay durable runner (the existing browser router/receipt work is not enough)
A pendant status/receipt protocol and local indication for verified, partial, blocked, and retry states
A cross-surface consent lease enforced at execution time for irreversible steps
Fresh Accessibility/Screen Recording and browser-extension reachability before any GUI action can be considered executable

proposals.user_asks: “Coordinate this change across my private browser account and my Mac, but if one side fails, leave the other side in a safe, recoverable state and tell me exactly what I need to approve next.” For example, update a logged-in order or appointment, then update my local calendar/reminder only after the private site confirms the change.
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot safely perform coupled changes today: a browser mutation and a local Mac mutation are separate jobs, so a disconnect can leave contradictory state or cause a retry to duplicate the private action. This is a distinct transactional guarantee, not merely a receipt after independent actions.
surfaces: faculty-judgement declares a two-phase plan with a reversible preparation phase, a commit point, and compensation action
relay coordinates the transaction and persists a transaction record, fencing token, timeout, and commit decision
browser extension prepares and verifies the authenticated-site mutation without committing irreversible effects until the coordinator authorizes it
Mac agent prepares a local reminder/calendar/file change in a staging location and returns a deterministic artifact identifier
relay commits in a fixed order, then asks faculty-perception to verify both resulting states; if the second side fails, it invokes the declared compensation or leaves a clearly marked pending state
pendant announces the commit decision and exposes a single retry/abort control, never silently repeating a committed private mutation
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic orchestration and local adapters for transaction mechanics; use a cheap background model only to translate unstructured site confirmations into typed facts. Realtime is needed only to explain a pause or request approval during the owner's conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation should complete in under 10 seconds when surfaces are reachable; commit and verification typically under 10 additional seconds. If a surface disappears, freeze safely within the configured timeout and retain the transaction for later resume rather than guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.03 per transaction, dominated by occasional semantic confirmation extraction; storage and coordination are inexpensive. Compensation and verification add network calls but no continuous model usage.
proposals.security_concerns: Private account data stays in the browser adapter; the relay receives only typed facts and transaction identifiers. A fresh consent lease is required at commit for irreversible actions. Fencing tokens prevent stale retries, and compensation must be explicitly declared and bounded—never invent a reverse action.
missing: A transaction coordinator with prepare/commit/abort semantics across browser and Mac adapters
Staging APIs for local Mac changes and a browser-side prepare mode
Fencing tokens and durable commit decisions that survive relay or bridge restarts
Typed compensation definitions and a safe pending-state UI
Cross-surface approval enforcement at the commit boundary
Post-commit verification from an independent perception pass

proposals.user_asks: “Ask me on the pendant before you send, delete, buy, or submit—and only do it after I physically confirm.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can approve an irreversible action without returning to the Mac, while a spoken yes alone cannot be accidentally replayed or confused with dictation. The action remains bound to the exact preview they saw/heard.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a typed transaction preview and risk classification
relay stores a one-time confirmation nonce and sends a short spoken summary to the pendant
pendant displays the risk via its single LED pattern and waits for a deliberate second-button press
relay forwards the signed confirmation to mac-planner
browser-extension or mac-vision executes only if the preview hash, tab/session, lease, and nonce still match
faculty-action returns a before/after receipt to the pendant and Mac workbench
proposals.model_tier: Use the normal planner/judgement tier to draft and classify; use realtime only for the short spoken preview and confirmation exchange. No model call is needed to validate the nonce or execute the already-approved typed plan.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview within 2 seconds; confirmation acknowledgement under 300 ms; execution feedback as soon as the Mac/browser receipt arrives.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per confirmation, dominated by realtime audio turns; nonce validation and dispatch are local/relay metadata only.
proposals.security_concerns: Never accept a spoken confirmation for high-risk actions, never reveal secrets in the LED or spoken summary, expire the nonce after 60 seconds or any plan edit, and require re-preview after tab navigation or field changes. A lost link must leave the action unexecuted, not retry blindly.
missing: Pendant firmware button gesture and LED confirmation state machine
Relay endpoint for nonce issuance, expiry, and signed confirmation
Mac/browser executor gate that verifies preview hash and lease immediately before side effects
Receipt UI that makes the exact pending transaction audible and reviewable

proposals.user_asks: “If I long-press the pendant, stop anything you’re about to do everywhere.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a single physical emergency brake for queued Mac, browser, and relay work—even when the screen is locked, the browser is unavailable, or speech recognition is wrong. It prevents a stale plan from executing after circumstances change.
surfaces: Pendant firmware detects a held-button emergency gesture and gives an unmistakable LED/haptic warning
Relay immediately marks the paired owner's action leases revoked and broadcasts cancellation to the Mac bridge
mac-planner cancels cancellable jobs and prevents new side effects until the lease epoch changes
browser-extension drops pending commands and returns cancellation receipts for each tab/session
faculty-action reports what was stopped and identifies any step that had already become irreversible
proposals.model_tier: No model is needed for detection, revocation, or cancellation. Use the cheaper planner tier only to summarize the resulting receipts; realtime may speak the short emergency acknowledgement.
proposals.latency_budget: Local gesture acknowledgement under 150 ms; relay lease revocation under 500 ms; all reachable surfaces blocked within 1 second.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; a small authenticated control message and receipt per active job. Hardware cost is covered by the haptic/button production change.
proposals.security_concerns: Require a distinctive hold duration and local debounce to avoid accidental cancellation, but do not require network or speech. Authenticate the device control channel, persist a monotonic lease epoch to defeat replay, and fail closed when the relay cannot be reached. The owner must be told explicitly if an irreversible step already completed.
missing: Pendant offline emergency-stop firmware state
Relay-wide action-lease epoch and cancellation broadcast
Mac and browser executors that honor revocation between every side effect
A concise cross-surface cancellation receipt

proposals.user_asks: “If something you need to do is blocked, tell me exactly what is unreachable, keep the approved work safe, and resume it automatically once I fix the Mac or browser.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can claim success while Accessibility events do nothing and browser commands queue behind an offline extension. The owner needs one trustworthy explanation on the pendant, not a misleading receipt or a lost task. This is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant delivers the blocker and receives a local confirmation, the Mac diagnoses/repairs its reachability, the browser bridge reattaches queued tabs, and the relay holds the resumable job.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to explain the immediate blocker and ask a short local confirmation; use a cheap background worker for queue reconciliation, permission/extension health polling, and replay eligibility.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate blocker speech under 2 seconds; health polling every 10–30 seconds while a job is held; automatic resume within 5 seconds of a verified reachability transition.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per blocked job: polling and state transitions are local/relay work; realtime cost is only one short spoken explanation. No vision/model call unless the owner explicitly authorizes GUI repair.
proposals.security_concerns: Never infer reachability from a successful API receipt. Require fresh inputReachability and browser-heartbeat evidence, bind the held job to its original tab/session and idempotency key, and require explicit approval before changing permissions, enabling an extension, or replaying an irreversible step. Do not upload screenshots or private page content for diagnosis.
missing: A typed reachability contract emitted by Mac with freshness, binary identity, and proof that synthesized input reached the target
A durable blocked-job state machine spanning relay, Mac jobs, and browser commands (hold, repair-needed, revalidate, resume, expire)
A browser heartbeat/command acknowledgement that drains or safely invalidates the existing three pending commands
A pendant-facing short status/confirmation protocol for blocker, repair instructions, and resume/abort
An OS-permission repair path or owner-guided deep link; the agent must remain fail-closed when Accessibility/Screen Recording are absent

proposals.user_asks: “If I long-press the pendant, immediately freeze every pending action everywhere, even if the Mac or browser is unreachable, then tell me what was stopped and let me release only the safe ones.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has no guaranteed physical override when a queued Mac/browser action is stale, duplicated, or has lost reachability. A pendant-local kill switch gives them control at the one place they always have, while the relay, Mac agent, and browser reconcile the stop when links return. It is not merely an undo receipt: it prevents actions that have not started and marks in-flight work for cancellation across all surfaces.
proposals.model_tier: No model for the stop path: pendant firmware and relay use a signed emergency-stop event. Use a cheap background model only to summarize the resulting action inventory; realtime is optional for the spoken acknowledgment.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant LED/haptic acknowledgment locally under 100 ms; relay freeze under 1 second when connected; offline stop is durable on the pendant and applied before any queued replay after reconnection.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model/API cost for stop and reconciliation; small relay storage for a monotonic stop epoch and per-job cancellation markers.
proposals.security_concerns: Long-press must be physically deliberate, authenticated to the owner’s paired relay, monotonic, and resistant to replay. It must not claim to reverse an already completed external side effect. On reconnect, every worker checks the stop epoch before starting a step; release requires a fresh deliberate owner confirmation, with irreversible actions never silently resumed.
missing: A pendant-firmware emergency-stop event and durable monotonic stop epoch that survives dropped LTE
Relay-wide cancellation fence checked by Mac jobs, browser commands, and scheduled workers
Mac/browser adapters that distinguish queued, started, and completed work and acknowledge the fence
A dashboard/pendant inventory of frozen jobs with selective release and explicit expiry

proposals.user_asks: When I approve a multi-step task that spans my Mac and logged-in websites, carry it out as one staged transaction: prepare everything, show me the exact combined effects, commit each step in dependency order, and if a later step fails, automatically undo every earlier reversible step and tell me precisely what could not be rolled back.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action can succeed on one surface and fail on another, leaving half-finished bookings, messages, files, or settings for the owner to repair manually. This gives them one understandable approval and a reliable all-or-nothing attempt across the devices that actually hold the needed access.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for dependency analysis, field normalization, and compensation planning; use realtime only to speak the combined preview, request approval, and report the final receipt. Deterministic executors and browser/Mac harnesses perform the actual steps.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation may take 5–20 seconds depending on authenticated pages. After approval, commit each step with visible progress; target under 2 seconds between steps and fail closed on stale state, expired sessions, or missing proof.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.08 per task depending on page count and whether vision is needed; dominant costs are authenticated page reads/screenshots and any vision/computer-use turns, not the small orchestration model.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must carry opaque job IDs and approval tokens, not page secrets. A single-use approval token must bind to the complete plan fingerprint, ordered steps, recipients, amounts, and target accounts. Never compensate an irreversible external action by inventing a second external action; mark it unrecoverable and stop. Require explicit confirmation for financial, legal, deletion, or message-send effects.
missing: A cross-surface two-phase job coordinator with durable prepare/commit/abort states and dependency edges
A shared typed effect ledger so Mac and browser steps expose compatible before/after state and compensation handlers
Browser executor support for transactional checkpoints, idempotency, and compensation receipts
A relay-delivered pendant approval UI that speaks a compact combined diff and binds approval to the plan fingerprint
A recovery worker that resumes or aborts disconnected jobs without replaying committed step IDs
An owner-facing dashboard showing the aggregate transaction, partial failures, and per-step undoability

proposals.user_asks: “If I walk away or one of my devices disconnects, keep my task safe, then resume exactly where it stopped when the right hand comes back—without repeating anything—and tell me what still needs my attention.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a multi-step request can be left half-done when the Mac loses reachability or the browser bridge disappears, and a retry can duplicate an external action. The owner should be able to leave a task in progress, regain it later, and see a trustworthy distinction between committed, unverified, and not-yet-executed steps. This is more than background execution: it preserves semantic transaction state across different hands and reconciles uncertain outcomes before continuing.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a versioned semantic task graph and classifies each step as pure, reversible, or externally committing
faculty-action executes the graph and writes an append-only checkpoint after every step, including idempotency key, pre-state fingerprint, post-state evidence, and uncertainty status
Mac planner/terminal performs local files, apps, and scripts; mac-vision is used only when accessibility and screen proof are available
browser extension performs authenticated tab actions with tab/session affinity and DOM evidence; it can report an external commit that happened before disconnect
relay remains awake, stores encrypted task checkpoints and retry leases, and sends compact state changes to the pendant
pendant shows resumable-task state locally, vibrates/LED-signals blocked or reconciled states, and offers a physical resume/cancel action when connectivity returns
unified presents one owner-facing timeline that reconciles duplicate reports from Mac, browser, and relay
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic state-machine logic for checkpointing, deduplication, lease expiry, and reconciliation; use a background model for semantic step interpretation and recovery suggestions. Reserve realtime only for the owner's live spoken status request or urgent interruption.
proposals.latency_budget: Healthy local continuation should add under 300 ms per checkpoint. Reconnect reconciliation may take 1–5 seconds for local work and longer for authenticated browser work; the owner should immediately receive a concise 'paused / committed-but-unverified / resumed' status rather than wait for a full explanation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per step: mostly local/relay storage and deterministic checks. A background model call is needed only when an interrupted step's evidence is ambiguous, roughly one short call per ambiguous interruption; realtime cost is limited to live conversation. Dominant cost is encrypted checkpoint retention and browser/Mac evidence capture, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Checkpoints must never store passwords, cookies, raw page contents, or arbitrary command output by default—store hashes, redacted snippets, and local references. Resume leases must be single-use, scoped to the exact task version and step, and expire. External commits require reconciliation before retry; if outcome cannot be proven, stop and ask the owner rather than duplicate. A physical pendant cancel must override queued continuation.
missing: A durable cross-surface task-graph and checkpoint protocol, distinct from per-surface job receipts
A reconciliation adapter for each committing action type (browser submit, email send, file move, calendar mutation)
Relay storage and event APIs for encrypted checkpoints, leases, and reconnect notifications
Pendant firmware/UI support for resumable task state and physical cancel/resume
A local evidence redaction and hashing layer on Mac and browser
A policy and test suite for uncertain external outcomes and exactly-once versus at-least-once actions

proposals.user_asks: “Carry this out across my devices, and keep me informed of each handoff; if one device is unavailable, pause safely and tell me exactly what remains.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a multi-surface plan, but action is fragmented: a Mac job, browser command, relay job, and pendant receipt can each look successful independently. This gives the owner one execution transaction with dependency-aware handoffs, explicit queued/running/blocked/verified states, and a truthful final receipt even after a dropped link or partial completion.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a signed dependency graph and irreversible-step checkpoints
faculty-action leases each step to mac-planner/mac-vision, browser-extension, or relay; records idempotency key and precondition snapshot
mac-planner/mac-terminal execute typed Mac work and return structured evidence; browser-extension executes private-tab work and returns tab/url/locator evidence

relay stays awake, persists the transaction and pushes concise progress to the pendant; pendant shows the current step, blocked reason, and requires local confirmation for physical/irreversible transitions
unified reconciles late receipts and presents one completion/partial/failure summary with undo or resume options
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic state-machine and receipt verification for routing, leases, retries, and reconciliation; gpt-4.1-mini background for summarizing progress; reserve gpt-5.6-luna planner for ambiguous recovery only, and realtime solely for the live spoken update.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge and display the lease within 300 ms; each handoff update within 1 s of receipt. Recovery/reconciliation may run in the background after the owner leaves.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for deterministic D1/state-machine work; roughly one background summarization call per completed transaction, with planner escalation only on ambiguity. Dominant cost is evidence/context summarization, not each action step.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser content and Mac evidence remain on their local surfaces unless the owner-approved transaction explicitly permits relay summarization. Never replay an irreversible step without an idempotency key and fresh precondition proof. Pause on permission loss, stale UI, timezone conflict, or receipt trust unknown; pendant confirmation is required before sending, purchasing, deleting, or physical actions.
missing: A durable cross-surface transaction schema with dependency graph, leases, idempotency keys, precondition snapshots, and typed receipt states
A relay push channel and pendant progress UI for transaction updates and blocked reasons
A common evidence envelope (surface, timestamp, source locator, before/after hash, trust) accepted by Mac, browser, and relay
Resume/rollback policy and deterministic reconciliation for late or duplicate receipts
Accessibility and Screen Recording grants plus a live browser bridge for GUI/private-tab execution

proposals.user_asks: “Make this change everywhere it needs to change, show me the conflicts and side effects first, then commit the whole change—or leave everything exactly as it was.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently make a coordinated change across Calendar, reminders, private web accounts, and local files without manually tracking partial updates. This provides a true cross-system change set: discover dependencies, simulate consequences, obtain one understandable approval, and either commit all safe steps or recover every already-applied reversible step.
surfaces: faculty-perception builds a dependency map from the owner's calendar, reminders, open authenticated tabs, and relevant Mac documents
faculty-judgement turns the requested change into a versioned change set, identifies conflicts, distinguishes reversible from irreversible effects, and presents a compact pendant approval summary
faculty-action asks browser-extension and Mac agents to stage changes in isolated drafts or temporary records, validates post-stage state, then commits in dependency order
relay persists the change-set, approval token, and compensating actions so the owner can leave during staging and resume later
pendant presents the conflict list and final diff audibly/through LEDs/buttons; one confirmation is bound to the exact change-set hash
unified reports committed, partially committed with compensations, or safely abandoned—never a vague success
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic diffing, dependency ordering, approval binding, and compensation rules first; gpt-4.1-mini for extracting and summarizing conflicts; gpt-5.6-luna only for ambiguous cross-application dependency reasoning; realtime only for the owner's live explanation.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial dependency scan within 5 seconds for local data and already-open tabs; staged diff within 30 seconds. Commit can continue in the background, with a pendant update at every system boundary.
proposals.cost_estimate: One background extraction/summarization call per change set and planner escalation only when dependency semantics are unclear. Storage and API costs are modest; the dominant cost is authenticated-page and document inspection.
proposals.security_concerns: Private account data must stay on the Mac/browser surfaces unless explicitly included in the change set. Approval tokens expire, are one-time, and bind to a plan hash plus precondition versions. No irreversible external send, purchase, deletion, or cancellation is included in an atomic commit unless separately confirmed. If any precondition changes after staging, commit pauses rather than overwriting.
missing: A versioned cross-application change-set and compensating-action model, distinct from ordinary job receipts
Staging adapters for Calendar, Reminders, local documents, and authenticated browser forms
Conflict and side-effect extraction with before/after diffs understandable through the pendant
A commit coordinator that validates all preconditions immediately before each step and safely compensates reversible prior steps
A confirmation token bound cryptographically to the exact staged diff and its precondition snapshot

proposals.user_asks: “Do this, even if I walk away—finish it only while my approval is still valid, and tell me exactly what happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an approved action can sit behind an offline browser bridge or an unready Mac and later fail ambiguously (or be retried without a fresh decision). This gives every action a short-lived, scope-limited lease: the pendant records the owner's approval, the relay durably queues and expires it, the Mac/browser executes only after a live preflight, and the pendant receives a completion/failure receipt. It is useful precisely because no one node can both capture physical approval, survive disconnection, reach private browser sessions, and perform the Mac action.
proposals.model_tier: deterministic for lease validation, preflight, queueing, expiry, and receipts; background model only to summarize a completed receipt; realtime only to phrase the spoken acknowledgement
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 300 ms; preflight/dispatch under 2 s when Mac and browser are online; completion notification when the action finishes. No model call on the critical path.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for normal actions; roughly 1 background summarization call only when a multi-step receipt needs prose (about 1–3k tokens). Storage is a small D1/job record plus a compact pendant receipt.
proposals.security_concerns: Lease must bind to exact action hash, target account/tab/session, allowed effects, expiry, and one-use nonce; relay stores no page secrets beyond existing job references. Never auto-renew. Destructive effects still require a second confirmation at commit. If the Mac loses readiness, browser goes offline, or proof is stale, expire and report—do not retry blindly. Dashboard must show pending leases and allow revocation.
missing: A lease API shared by relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge (issue, claim, renew-for-progress only within original expiry, revoke, expire)
Mac/browser preflight that returns structured readiness and blocks dispatch when Accessibility, Screen Recording, or browser polling is unavailable
Pendant firmware event/LED/audio UX for approve, executing, succeeded, failed, and expired states (offline queue for the approval)
Receipt correlation from relay job ID through Mac/browser action receipts back to the pendant and dashboard
Explicit owner policy schema distinguishing reversible actions from commit points

proposals.user_asks: “Handle this end to end, and if you get stuck, ask me one simple question on the pendant instead of making me start over.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a long Mac/browser task either fails when it reaches an ambiguity or requires the owner to remain at the computer. This capability turns uncertainty into a resumable, physical conversation: the Mac or authenticated browser pauses at a typed checkpoint, the always-awake relay sends a concise choice or missing-value prompt to the pendant, the owner answers with a button/voice response from anywhere, and execution resumes from the exact checkpoint. It is not merely an approval prompt—the system can ask for a correction, choose among alternatives, or defer, while preserving the task's evidence and progress.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic checkpoint protocol and response routing; background model to compress the question and choices; realtime only if the owner answers by voice and clarification is needed
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant prompt delivery within 2 seconds when connected; a response is acknowledged immediately and resumes the worker within 3 seconds. Paused tasks persist for days without consuming model calls.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small background summarization call per ambiguity, roughly 500–1,500 tokens; no model cost while paused. D1 checkpoint and response records are tiny.
proposals.security_concerns: Each prompt must show the requesting task, target account/site, and consequence in plain language. Responses bind to a nonce and checkpoint hash, expire after a configurable period, and cannot authorize a new action outside the presented choices. Sensitive values should be entered only through a secure pendant path and never spoken back. Dashboard must expose the full pause/resume audit trail.
missing: A durable checkpoint protocol in the Mac job runner and browser bridge with serializable state, evidence capsule, and resumability contract
Relay push/poll delivery for pending questions plus nonce-bound responses from the pendant
A compact pendant interaction vocabulary for choice, correction, defer, and cancel, including offline response spooling
Planner support for declaring safe checkpoints and formulating bounded questions instead of failing on ambiguity
Dashboard UI for paused tasks, unanswered questions, expiry, and manual recovery

proposals.user_asks: If my Mac goes to sleep or I leave it, keep carrying out the approved task on whatever connected surface can safely finish it, then tell me exactly where it stopped or completed.
proposals.why_useful: Today an approved task is stranded when the Mac or private browser disappears, and retrying risks doing part of it twice. This would make the hive behave like one dependable agent: the relay preserves the intent and evidence, the Mac resumes local work when available, and the browser or pendant provides continuity and control without losing the owner’s place.
surfaces: pendant: announces that work was paused, offers cancel/revoke by button, and speaks the final outcome
relay-realtime: stores the signed intent, checkpoint, expiry, and idempotency key while the owner and Mac are absent
mac-planner: decomposes the task into checkpointed, resumable steps and reports durable state
mac-vision: resumes GUI steps only from a verified visual/state checkpoint, never from a guessed screen
browser-extension: reattaches to the same authenticated tab/session when available and returns provenance for each step
unified: reconciles receipts from all surfaces into one completion or partial-completion answer
faculty-perception: verifies the current target state before resuming a step
faculty-judgement: decides whether migration is safe and which step classes may resume automatically
faculty-action: executes only the currently leased step and records an idempotent receipt
proposals.model_tier: Use background model for checkpoint summarization and migration planning; use realtime only for the owner’s live spoken interaction and urgent pause/cancel. Use deterministic state checks for idempotency and completion proofs.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgement under 2 seconds; pause is recorded locally/relay-side within 5 seconds. Resume begins on the next valid heartbeat, typically under 15 seconds, with no model call for deterministic steps.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: mostly D1/checkpoint writes, heartbeats, and deterministic verification. One background-model call per migration or ambiguous checkpoint; realtime tokens only when the owner is actively speaking.
proposals.security_concerns: Never migrate secrets or authenticated browser work to an untrusted/public surface. Bind leases to device identity, session/tab identity, action hash, and expiry; require fresh owner confirmation for sending, deleting, purchasing, or any irreversible step after interruption. Encrypt checkpoint payloads, redact page contents from receipts, and expose revoke-all from the pendant.
missing: A shared checkpoint schema that records preconditions, postconditions, provenance, and idempotency keys across Mac, relay, and browser
A lease/revocation protocol that can survive Mac sleep and prevent duplicate execution
A heartbeat-triggered resume coordinator with explicit safe-to-migrate action classes
State verification hooks in mac-vision and browser bridge before replaying a step
Pendant firmware support for paused-task status and a local cancel/revoke gesture
Owner-side Accessibility, Screen Recording, and Browser Bridge activation so the execution surfaces can actually participate

proposals.user_asks: “Do this even if my Mac is asleep: when it wakes, carry out the reversible part, prove it actually happened, and tell me if anything was skipped.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can queue speech/alerts and can run Mac/browser actions, but a decision made on the pendant does not have a single durable handoff that survives link loss, Mac sleep, or a stale browser session and then verifies the real-world result. This gives the owner trustworthy deferred action rather than a false ‘done’ receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to acknowledge capture and later announce completion; use a cheap background planner for decomposition/retries. Mac planner executes typed reversible actions, browser extension handles authenticated tabs, and mac-vision is fallback only when typed/browser controls cannot reach the target.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 300 ms locally; execution begins within 30 s of Mac/bridge reconnect; verification within 10 s per step. Expire leases after 24 h or at the user-specified deadline, never retry irreversible steps.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per deferred job depending on planner retries; most cost is background model calls and optional vision screenshots, not realtime. Storage is small JSON receipts plus hashes.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only a redacted action plan, target fingerprints, deadline, and proof metadata; never persist page secrets or raw screenshots by default. Require explicit confirmation for send/delete/purchase. Bind jobs to the paired pendant and Mac, use idempotency keys, and show a visible pending/expired state so a stale command cannot execute silently.
missing: A durable cross-surface action envelope with lease, deadline, idempotency key, and dependency graph
A reconnect worker that drains pendant-held intents to relay then Mac/browser in order
Typed proof-of-effect adapters (file hash, reminder ID, app state, browser DOM/value) plus a safe ‘could not verify’ result
A single owner-facing queue showing pending, running, verified, skipped, expired, and undoable jobs
Pendant firmware support to store a compact offline action envelope and LED/button acknowledgement

proposals.user_asks: “Continue this on my Mac exactly where I left off on the pendant, with the same tabs, evidence, decisions, and one approval still waiting for me.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has separate conversations and action surfaces: a spoken task can produce a reply or job, but there is no owner-facing continuity when they move from wearing the pendant to sitting at the Mac. This capability makes the AI feel like one agent rather than repeated starts, while preserving the exact boundary between decided, executed, and awaiting approval.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only for the pendant handoff cue and short spoken status. A cheaper background model compiles the task capsule and reconciles state; mac-planner executes typed work, browser-extension reattaches private tabs, and mac-vision inspects only when structured state is unavailable.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant can mark a handoff in under 1 second. On Mac unlock/open, restore the capsule in under 5 seconds, then reconcile live state in under 15 seconds. Never block the owner from viewing the capsule while reconciliation runs.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.04 per handoff, dominated by one compact reconciliation call; no realtime generation beyond the brief cue. Store hashes and structured facts rather than transcripts or screenshots.
proposals.security_concerns: Bind capsules to the paired owner/device, encrypt them in transit and at rest, redact secrets, and preserve confirmation gates. Do not reopen a private tab or repeat a side effect solely because it appears in the capsule; compare idempotency keys and current state first. Expire capsules and let the owner revoke them from either surface.
missing: A versioned task-capsule schema containing goal, completed steps, evidence references, unresolved questions, approvals, idempotency keys, and next-safe action
Relay synchronization with conflict resolution when pendant and Mac both receive updates while briefly disconnected
Browser tab/session restoration linked to capsule evidence without storing page secrets
A Mac dashboard/notification that opens the capsule and clearly separates verified facts from stale or pending state
Cross-device resume tests covering sleep, duplicate delivery, changed tabs, and revoked approval

proposals.user_asks: “Do that in the browser, but only if you can prove the right tab is open and the result really happened; otherwise tell me exactly what blocked it.”
proposals.why_useful: This closes the dangerous gap between the mind deciding and a hand acting. The pendant supplies a spoken, time-limited approval; relay binds it to one plan; Mac/browser attest the target surface is actually reachable before any write; faculty-perception verifies the postcondition independently. Today perception reports uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false and browser offline, so the system must refuse rather than claim success. The owner gets honest completion or a useful blocker, not a plausible-looking receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture the owner's short approval and announce outcome; use the cheaper background model for plan compilation and post-action evidence reconciliation. Deterministic harness code should perform leases, preflight checks, and postcondition checks.
proposals.latency_budget: 1–2 seconds for preflight and approval acknowledgement; up to 10 seconds for browser/Mac execution; announce immediately on refusal or verified completion. Never wait indefinitely for an offline bridge.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost: one short realtime turn plus background reconciliation (typically <$0.02 excluding any model-specific computer-use call). Most work is deterministic status checks and DOM/accessibility evidence.
proposals.security_concerns: Approval is scoped to an action-plan hash, target tab/session, and 60-second lease, never a blanket permission. Before write, require fresh attestations: bridge online, Accessibility/Screen Recording enabled for GUI actions, browser tab identity/url match, and expected DOM/app state. After write, require independent evidence (DOM mutation, app state, or read-back); if absent, report unknown and do not retry automatically. Keep credentials and page contents on the Mac/browser; retain only hashes, timestamps, selectors, and redacted receipts. Irreversible sends/submissions still require a second explicit spoken confirmation.
missing: A signed preflight-attestation endpoint shared by Mac, browser bridge, and relay, with nonce/action-plan hash and short expiry
A common action lease and approval record propagated from pendant to the executing surface
Postcondition-verifier adapters for browser DOM, accessibility UI, and typed Mac actions
A truthful refusal/result protocol and dashboard view for blocked, succeeded, and unknown outcomes
Permission/entitlement health polling and browser-online readiness surfaced before planning

proposals.user_asks: “If the price drops below $X (or this appointment opens), reserve it for me, but only while the details still match what I approved.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can delegate a bounded real-world opportunity instead of repeatedly checking a site. The always-awake relay watches for the condition, the authenticated browser supplies private availability or pricing, the Mac can complete the reversible preparation, and the pendant provides the final confirmation or cancellation window. This is more useful than a reminder because it carries the owner's exact constraints forward and refuses to act when the offer, identity, or terms drift.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model or deterministic rules for polling, normalization, and constraint checks. Use realtime only when the pendant must ask a concise clarification or announce that the condition has been met. Use the expensive model only for ambiguous page changes or constraint interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Condition checks can run on a schedule with no conversational latency. Once matched, notify the pendant within 30 seconds, reserve a 2–5 minute execution lease, and finish or clearly expire within 15 seconds after approval.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low ongoing cost for deterministic polling and hashes; occasional background extraction costs cents per check depending on page complexity. Realtime cost occurs only for an owner clarification or confirmation, not every poll.
proposals.security_concerns: The owner must approve a structured capsule containing maximum price, dates, quantity, merchant/site, cancellation rules, payment/account scope, and expiry. Never infer missing limits. Keep private page contents on the Mac/browser; relay stores encrypted constraints and redacted evidence. Before commitment, re-read price, terms, recipient/account, and availability; require explicit pendant confirmation for purchases, submissions, or anything irreversible. If the browser disappears, terms change, or evidence is stale, do nothing and explain why.
missing: A durable conditional-intent capsule schema with versioned constraints and owner-visible expiry
A scheduler that wakes the relay and performs authenticated browser observations without keeping a model session alive
A change detector that distinguishes a qualifying condition from cosmetic page updates and records cited evidence
A reservation/checkout staging interface that stops at the exact irreversible boundary
A pendant notification and confirmation protocol that works when the owner is not currently speaking
A policy engine for payment, cancellation, quantity, and maximum-loss limits
Test fixtures for price drops, appointment openings, changed terms, expired sessions, duplicate matches, and race conditions

proposals.user_asks: If an action is blocked because my Mac or browser is unavailable, keep it safe, tell me exactly what I need to fix, and resume automatically when the required connection or permission returns.
proposals.why_useful: Today a request can fail after a long timeout or appear successful despite doing nothing. The owner should not have to remember which extension or macOS permission to repair, nor repeat the original intent.
proposals.model_tier: Background/state-machine orchestration with a cheaper model for recovery instructions; realtime only for the short spoken alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate blocked status within 1 second; health-triggered retry within 5 seconds of Accessibility/bridge recovery; no repeated action without idempotency and fresh preflight.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: mostly local health polling and durable state; occasional small-model recovery message, under $0.01 per blocked job excluding voice.
proposals.security_concerns: Store the intent and minimum parameters encrypted; never replay irreversible actions automatically. Require renewed approval if an approval window expired or page/account state changed; surface exact target and expiry on pendant/dashboard.
missing: Fail-closed reachability and postcondition adapter
Durable blocked-action state with idempotency keys and expiry
Mac permission/bridge health transition events
A pendant/relay notification path that can distinguish blocked, resumed, and expired

proposals.user_asks: When I ask you to create something—like a reminder, note, or draft—from my pendant, make sure it appears exactly once even if the pendant, relay, and Mac all retry or reconnect in a different order.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable can hear an instruction while offline, the relay can queue it, and the Mac can independently retry it after reconnecting. Today those paths can create duplicates or leave the owner unsure whether to try again. Exactly-once intent handling would make everyday capture dependable.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic idempotency ledger and reconciliation first; use a cheap background model only to normalize equivalent natural-language intents. Realtime is not needed except to acknowledge capture.
proposals.latency_budget: A local spoken acknowledgement immediately; durable deduplication and Mac reconciliation within 5 seconds of connectivity. Never block capture on a cloud round trip.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: a small durable intent record and hash per capture; occasional background normalization under $0.01. No extra realtime inference required.
proposals.security_concerns: Bind each intent to the paired owner/device and retain only the minimum content until execution. Do not deduplicate across different destinations without showing the owner the target; drafts and reminders may execute automatically, while sends/deletes/purchases still require confirmation.
missing: A shared intent-id and semantic-fingerprint ledger spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
Adapters that accept idempotency keys for Reminders, Notes, drafts, and shell actions
A reconciliation view that distinguishes applied-once, conflicting, and expired intents
A conflict policy for two captures that sound similar but are not the same request

proposals.user_asks: “Is my pendant audio healthy?”
proposals.why_useful: Instead of vague failures, the owner gets a one-sentence answer plus a receipt showing whether the fault is microphone capture, relay transport, Opus decode, resampling, or Bluetooth output, and a suggested recovery step.
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model summarizes deterministic measurements; realtime is used only if the owner asks this while wearing the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: 10–20 seconds for a live 10-second diagnostic; under 2 seconds for cached last-known health. The test fixture and DSP run locally; only metrics cross nodes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost for local signal checks; <$0.01 for optional natural-language summary. Dominant cost is a short diagnostic capture and Bluetooth playback.
proposals.security_concerns: Use synthetic tones or a locally stored consented fixture, never owner speech. Require explicit confirmation before emitting audible tones; redact UART and transcript data. Dashboard access must be paired/authenticated.
missing: The 24 kHz conformance harness and sample-counter telemetry proposed above
A user-facing health endpoint that correlates pendant, relay, and ESP32/BT receipts
A quiet diagnostic mode (headphone loopback or owner-confirmed audible test)

proposals.user_asks: “Prepare this action on my Mac, and let me approve it from the pendant when you’re ready.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can start a complicated task from a spoken request, walk away from the Mac, and approve the exact final action from the device they are wearing. The Mac/browser can gather context and fill reversible fields, while the pendant provides a clear, local final commit instead of requiring the owner to return to the screen.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background/model routing handles preparation and evidence extraction; realtime is used only for the initial spoken request or clarification. The final approval is a deterministic protocol, not an LLM decision.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation may take tens of seconds in the background; approval acknowledgement should reach the pendant within 1 second when connected. An approval remains valid for only a short, explicit lease window.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per preparation, dominated by browser/Mac work; negligible cost for the approval handshake and receipt.
proposals.security_concerns: The approval payload must be cryptographically bound to the exact target, account, fields, and irreversible effects, with a digest and human-readable summary spoken/displayed before commit. Expire approvals on content, tab, or account changes; require a second confirmation for sending mail, deletion, purchases, or other destructive actions. Do not expose secrets on the pendant; store only a short-lived nonce and receipt.
missing: A relay-mediated two-phase commit protocol binding Mac/browser evidence to a pendant approval nonce
A compact pendant confirmation UX using the single button and LED, including cancellation and timeout semantics
A durable, tamper-evident before/after receipt that the Mac and relay can reconcile after reconnect
Mac/browser adapters that can pause exactly before submission and resume only with the matching approval

proposals.user_asks: “Once you’ve decided to do it, carry the action through whichever device has the right reach, and don’t just tell me it ran—prove that the intended change actually happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide an outcome, but execution is fragmented: the relay may lose a job, the Mac may be offline, Safari may require its private session, and a browser click can report success without the server state changing. This gives the mind one action contract: a durable intent ID and exact payload travel from relay to Mac/browser, retries are idempotent, the pendant can report progress while the owner walks away, and a postcondition read provides evidence (or an honest unresolved state) rather than a false success. It complements existing draft/preview capabilities and respects the no-approval-gates policy: judgement authorizes; action executes and verifies.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed intent with target, allowed effects, idempotency key, and postcondition
relay persists the intent, leases it to the currently reachable Mac/browser, resumes after disconnect, and sends compact progress/failure events to the pendant
mac-planner routes each step to mac_run_actions or browser_run_actions; browser-extension binds the exact tab/session and returns typed before/after evidence
faculty-perception performs the postcondition read from the appropriate surface and reconciles it with the intended effect
pendant speaks only state transitions (accepted, working, blocked, verified/uncertain) and offers retry/cancel for reversible work; the relay stores the receipt and evidence manifest
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the live spoken status and immediate clarification. Use a cheaper background model for intent normalization, retry planning, and evidence reconciliation; deterministic code should own idempotency, leases, schemas, and postcondition checks.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 300 ms; first execution attempt within 2 s when Mac/browser are online. Long work is asynchronous and survives disconnects. Verification should follow each mutation within 5 s, with exponential retry and a clear uncertain result after the deadline.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per ordinary action depending on whether a background model is needed; deterministic routing and browser/Mac calls dominate latency, while any long-form reasoning should be background-tier. Spoken progress is a few short realtime turns, not a full context resend.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must not invent authority: it executes only a signed/typed intent from judgement, scoped to named surfaces and effects. Store payload hashes and redacted evidence, never raw secrets or page text by default. Private reads stay in Safari; public work may use the relay. A mismatch between postcondition and intent must be reported as uncertain, never auto-corrected. Cancellation must stop before the next irreversible step, but must not claim rollback where none exists.
missing: A cross-surface ActionIntent/ActionReceipt schema with payload hash, scope, idempotency key, lease, retry policy, and explicit postcondition
Durable relay worker with lease renewal, resumable step polling, and delivery of compact pendant progress events
Typed browser and Mac executors that return before/after evidence and distinguish accepted, applied, and verified
A perception verifier that can query the authoritative result surface after mutation
Pendant/relay protocol for progress, cancellation, retry, and offline queued status

proposals.user_asks: “If I get interrupted, save exactly where I was across my open apps and logged-in tabs, then let me say ‘resume that’ later—on the pendant, another Mac, or the browser—and continue from the same point without making me reconstruct the task.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner loses work at the boundary between surfaces: spoken intent lives in the pendant, evidence and drafts live in Safari, and edits or files live on the Mac. Existing jobs can keep running, but they do not create a human-usable checkpoint of the unfinished task. This capability would preserve the task’s semantic state, not merely a process status, and resume only after rechecking what changed while it was paused.
surfaces: pendant captures an interruption command and identifies the active task without retaining raw audio
relay stores an encrypted, expiring task checkpoint containing intent, completed steps, open questions, artifact references, and the last known surface/session bindings
Mac-planner snapshots relevant app/document state and browser-extension snapshots named tabs, selected regions, and draft values without copying credentials
faculty-perception revalidates each referenced artifact and marks stale or missing state
faculty-judgement chooses whether to continue, revise, or abandon the checkpoint
mac-vision/browser-extension/mac-terminal restore the required view and execute only the next bounded step; pendant narrates what was restored and where continuation begins
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic checkpoint serialization and cheap background reconciliation by default. Use realtime only to identify the owner’s ‘resume that’ request and speak the concise restoration status; reserve expensive reasoning for genuinely ambiguous stale state.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture a checkpoint in under 2 seconds after interruption. Restore a concise status on the pendant within 1 second, then revalidate and reopen surfaces asynchronously, usually within 5–15 seconds. Never block the owner’s live conversation on full restoration.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.04 per checkpoint/resume, dominated by encrypted metadata storage and occasional background reconciliation; no screenshot or transcript needs to be sent to the realtime model unless explicitly needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Checkpoints must be encrypted, short-lived, revocable, and scoped to the owner and originating device. Never persist passwords, cookies, access tokens, or unrestricted page dumps. Browser references must reattach only to the same authenticated profile and show a stale-state warning if the account or page changed. Resumption must not silently send, purchase, delete, or submit; it may restore context and prepare the next reversible step, while irreversible continuation requires the existing policy path.
missing: A cross-surface TaskCheckpoint schema with semantic step graph, artifact references, staleness rules, and TTL
Mac/browser snapshot adapters that can restore app and tab context without exporting secrets
Encrypted relay checkpoint storage and a resume lookup bound to the owner’s identity
A revalidation service that compares checkpoint references with current documents/pages before continuation
Pendant protocol for naming, listing, expiring, and resuming checkpoints

proposals.user_asks: When I approve a Now Card, carry out its steps exactly once—even if the pendant loses LTE, the Mac wakes later, or the browser reconnects—and tell me which steps completed, which are waiting, and what I can safely retry.
proposals.why_useful: Judgement can select a multi-surface plan, but today action execution can duplicate work or lose place across pendant/relay/Mac/browser handoffs. A durable execution lease and step ledger would let the owner trust that 'approve' means one action per intended resource, with honest recovery after disconnection.
proposals.model_tier: Background planner creates a deterministic step graph; realtime only speaks the approval/result summary. Relay persists the graph and leases; Mac/browser perform typed steps; pendant shows compact state; dashboard exposes receipts and retry controls.
proposals.latency_budget: Approval acknowledgement under 500 ms from relay; each step may complete asynchronously. Reconnect reconciliation within 5 seconds. No low-latency model call is needed for retries or reconciliation.
proposals.cost_estimate: ~$0.001–$0.01 per approved card, dominated by planner tokens; lease renewals, receipts, and retries are storage/edge operations.
proposals.security_concerns: Only explicitly approved graphs may mutate. Each step carries an idempotency key, target surface, precondition hash, expiry, and reversible/irreversible classification. Browser credentials never leave the browser. Require a fresh pendant confirmation for irreversible or changed-precondition steps; redact receipt payloads and expire evidence.
missing: A shared durable step-ledger/lease API across relay, Mac bridge, and browser extension (claim, heartbeat, complete, fail, reconcile, expire).
Executor adapters that honor idempotency keys and return typed receipts with before/after evidence; browser currently needs command deduplication and session reattachment.
