Pendant/dashboard rendering for per-step states and a compact retry/continue interaction.
A policy evaluator that blocks stale plans and routes changed or irreversible steps back to judgement for confirmation.

proposals.user_asks: Let me give you a goal once, then leave it running safely: coordinate the whole task across my logged-in browser and Mac, ask me only when a real decision is needed, and let one press of the pendant stop every pending action immediately.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can plan and execute isolated actions, but it cannot safely supervise a long-lived, multi-surface objective with a physical emergency stop and decision checkpoints. This would let the owner delegate chores such as arranging travel, resolving an account issue, or preparing a purchase without leaving an unbounded agent acting in the background.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background model maintains the task graph and detects decision points; realtime is used only for spoken checkpoint questions and immediate stop acknowledgement. The relay coordinates state, Mac and browser perform scoped steps, and the dashboard shows the active delegation.
proposals.latency_budget: Stop signal should be accepted by the relay in under 300 ms and prevent any not-yet-started step. In-flight cancellation acknowledgement within 2 seconds; ordinary planning and browser work may be asynchronous.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.05 per delegated objective, dominated by planner and checkpoint summaries; stop, lease, and event traffic is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Delegation must have an explicit scope, expiry, allowed domains/apps, maximum spend or message count, and a deny-list for irreversible operations. The pendant button is a local stop signal that works even if speech or the Mac is unavailable. Browser secrets remain in-browser. Pauses at changed facts, external communication, purchases, authentication, and any action outside the approved scope; require fresh confirmation. Encrypt and TTL task context and receipts.
missing: A relay-resident objective supervisor with scope, expiry, checkpoint, and cancellation state—not merely a one-shot job runner.
A priority stop channel from pendant to relay, plus cancellation propagation and acknowledgement in Mac and browser executors.
A policy/checkpoint protocol that turns planner uncertainty or changed page state into a compact spoken question and resumes only after the answer.
Executor sandboxing by app/domain and resource budget, with watchdogs for hung Mac/browser work.
Pendant and dashboard UI for active delegation, current step, pause reason, expiry, and emergency stop confirmation.

proposals.user_asks: “Use the best voice quality available.” The system should negotiate a true 24 kHz superwideband path end to end, fall back safely when LTE or a peer cannot sustain it, and tell me which mode is actually active.
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has a 15,625 Hz microphone feeding a nominal 16 kHz Opus uplink; a model may decide that high-quality speech is desirable but cannot make every hand in the chain agree. This capability makes the decision executable: the pendant, bridge, relay, and Mac playback each advertise measured capabilities, the relay selects a mode, and the pendant gets a short spoken/LED indication of the real mode rather than a promise. It also produces a per-turn quality receipt so regressions are diagnosable.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the live codec/transport negotiation and one-sentence user feedback; no LLM is needed in the audio loop. A cheaper background worker can aggregate quality receipts and detect regressions.
proposals.latency_budget: Negotiation <=150 ms before capture, no added steady-state conversational latency beyond one Opus frame; fallback within 2 seconds of sustained loss/jitter. Dashboard receipt can lag by minutes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost in the hot path; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per session for relay compute/storage depending on retention and telemetry volume. The dominant cost is LTE airtime and storing dual-mode test recordings, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Raw audio remains sensitive: do not upload diagnostic PCM by default. Send compact telemetry (mode, packet loss, jitter, sample counts, codec settings), encrypt receipts, and retain audio only under the existing policy. Changing mode is non-destructive and needs no confirmation; exporting recordings or sharing receipts requires confirmation.
missing: A firmware capture/codec implementation that genuinely produces 24 kHz samples (the current hardware contract reports 15,625 Hz capture), with resampler quality and CPU/RAM measurements
A versioned audio-capability handshake shared by pendant, ESP32 bridge, relay, and Mac playback, including an explicit reason-coded fallback
A relay jitter buffer and sequence/timestamp validation that can distinguish 24 kHz content from mislabeled 16 kHz frames
A Mac-side loopback/measurement harness and golden fixtures (sweep, speech, packet-loss simulation) to verify sample rate, intelligibility, and latency before claiming success
A compact pendant status indication and durable quality receipt linked to the conversation/job id

proposals.user_asks: “Do it, and prove it worked.” For any reversible cross-device action, verify the resulting state on the surface that owns it, and tell me if execution succeeded, is merely queued, or could not be verified.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action agent can queue a Mac or browser command and produce a receipt, but a queued receipt is not proof that the world changed. This closes the gap between judgement and action: after creating a reminder, the Mac reads it back; after a browser form mutation, the browser re-reads the authoritative page; after a pendant setting change, the relay receives a device acknowledgement. The owner gets one concise result and no false claims of completion.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model for deterministic verification. faculty-judgement supplies the typed expected postcondition; action executes it; faculty-perception compares observed state. Realtime is used only to speak the result if the owner is present; background retries use a cheaper worker.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local verification within 1 second; browser/server confirmation within 5 seconds, with durable polling up to 2 minutes after disconnect. If the postcondition is not observable, report ‘unverified’ rather than retrying blindly.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost for typed predicates; roughly $0.001 per browser verification and minimal Mac/relay compute. Storage is a small before/after evidence record, not a copy of page contents or audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification reads private state and must inherit the action’s tab/session permissions. Redact secrets and page bodies from receipts, retain only field hashes plus minimal evidence, and never turn a failed verification into an automatic repeat for side-effectful operations. Destructive actions remain confirmation-gated.
missing: A shared typed postcondition schema (entity, owner surface, predicate, timeout, freshness) emitted by faculty-judgement
Per-surface verify adapters: Mac read-back, browser authoritative re-read, and pendant/relay device ACK with monotonic sequence numbers
A state-machine result distinct from success: queued, applied, verified, rejected, timed out, and unknown-after-disconnect
Evidence-safe receipt storage and dashboard rendering that shows expected versus observed without leaking private values
Idempotency/lease integration so reconnect verification cannot replay the original mutation

proposals.user_asks: “Use my saved information to complete this, but never show or send my private values through the AI.” The system should let the browser or Mac fill secrets locally, have the pendant show only a redacted summary, and require my physical approval immediately before submission.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can ask for a form or account task, but today the model either needs the values in its context or cannot reliably coordinate private autofill with a safe final approval. This would let the AI prepare a transaction without learning passwords, payment details, recovery codes, or other secrets. The browser session or Mac Keychain remains the only component that handles the plaintext; the pendant and relay carry field labels, redacted previews, and a signed approval instead.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper planning model to map requested fields to typed intents. No model should receive secret values. Realtime is used only to explain the redacted preview and collect the final physical approval.
proposals.latency_budget: Prepare the redacted transaction preview within 3 seconds; local secret filling under 1 second; approval must expire after 60 seconds and submission acknowledgement should arrive within 5 seconds. Never continue submission after a disconnect or stale preview.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost after the initial field-intent plan. Main engineering cost is browser/Mac integration and security review; operational cost is a few encrypted metadata bytes per transaction, with no secret storage.
proposals.security_concerns: Secrets must never enter prompts, relay logs, D1, R2, screenshots, or dashboard history. Use OS Keychain/browser autofill handles or opaque local references, scoped to origin and field name. Bind approval to origin, account, field names, redacted value fingerprints, and a short expiry; reject if any changes. Require confirmation for submission, purchases, messages, or other irreversible effects.
missing: A local secret-provider adapter for Safari/Chrome autofill and macOS Keychain that returns opaque handles rather than values
A redacted transaction manifest with origin binding, field metadata, value fingerprints, and an immutable preview hash
A pendant approval protocol that displays safe labels and commits only the exact previewed manifest
Browser and Mac submit gates that refuse altered DOM, navigation, origin, or stale approvals
End-to-end tests proving plaintext secrets never appear in model context, relay telemetry, screenshots, or receipts

proposals.user_asks: Do this, and don't tell me it's done until you can prove the result is actually true.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can dispatch Mac/browser actions and produce receipts, but a receipt only proves that a command was accepted. This gives the owner a trustworthy closed loop: the pendant can trigger it, the relay can keep retrying after disconnects, the Mac or authenticated browser can act, and faculty-perception can independently verify the resulting state before speaking success. If verification fails, the owner hears 'not confirmed' rather than a false completion.
surfaces: pendant button/voice trigger sends a signed intent and displays an in-progress LED state
relay persists the intent, deduplicates retries, leases it to the reachable Mac/browser surface, and records an idempotency key
mac-planner selects mac_run_actions or browser_run_actions; browser-extension supplies tab/session-local evidence when private state is involved

faculty-perception runs a typed postcondition probe after a settle window (UI state, DOM field, file/reminder existence, or pipeline/device ACK) and returns pass/fail/unknown with timestamped evidence
relay delivers a compact spoken completion/failure result back to the pendant and Mac journal; unified retains the evidence link
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for planning and postcondition interpretation; reserve realtime only for the owner's live utterance and the final short spoken result.
proposals.latency_budget: Reversible Mac actions: 2–5 seconds including verification. Browser actions: up to 15 seconds. If the target surface is offline, keep the job durable and report queued immediately; retry for a bounded TTL, then report unconfirmed. No destructive action is sent without the existing owner confirmation policy.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per completed job depending on browser screenshots/vision; most cost is the independent verification pass and any browser computer-use step, not relay persistence.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser evidence must stay on the Mac/bridge and be reduced to typed predicates or redacted snippets; never upload full DOM or screenshots by default. Bind proof to the same session/tab and idempotency key to prevent proving an unrelated state. Sending mail, deleting files, purchases, or other irreversible effects still require confirmation before dispatch; unknown proof must never be presented as success.
missing: A shared typed action contract with expected postcondition, settle timeout, and verification recipe
A verifier endpoint/worker that can call Mac accessibility/file probes and browser DOM probes independently of the executor
Receipts need before/after evidence references and a three-state outcome: confirmed, failed, unconfirmed
Pendant/relay protocol needs durable job and result correlation so disconnect/retry cannot create duplicate actions
Fault-injection tests for executor success + stale observation, duplicate dispatch, tab replacement, Mac sleep, and relay reconnect

proposals.user_asks: Use my private browser accounts and Mac files to answer this, but guarantee that raw private content never leaves my Mac.
proposals.why_useful: The owner could safely ask the hive to combine logged-in browser data, local files, and the pendant without turning the relay into a copy of their private life. Today authenticated browsing and relay orchestration exist as separate pieces, but there is no enforceable boundary that proves what data crossed it.
surfaces: pendant states the privacy mode in the spoken request and shows a distinct LED state
browser-extension reads the logged-in page locally and reduces it to an approved typed claim, aggregate, or redacted excerpt
mac-planner/mac-terminal combines those local claims with files on the Mac; a local policy engine classifies and blocks raw secrets, credentials, full page text, and screenshots
relay carries only the task, schema-constrained claims, hashes, and completion status; faculty-judgement answers from that projection
faculty-perception can inspect the local audit record and tell the owner exactly which sources contributed without exposing their contents
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model locally on the Mac for extraction and redaction; use realtime only if the owner is speaking live. The relay model should receive only the minimized projection.
proposals.latency_budget: Local extraction and policy checks in 1–5 seconds; complex multi-page work up to 20 seconds. If a source cannot be safely minimized, stop and report that it was withheld rather than silently sending it.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per request; the dominant cost is local or browser-side extraction, with relay inference reduced by smaller context.
proposals.security_concerns: This must be enforced by code, not a prompt: deny-by-default egress schema, secret/token detection, page-origin and file-path allowlists, cryptographic audit hashes, and a visible privacy-mode indicator. The owner must explicitly opt into any raw excerpt or screenshot leaving the Mac. Logs and cached claims need short retention and encryption.
missing: A local privacy firewall/policy engine intercepting every browser-to-relay and Mac-to-relay payload
Typed claim schemas and deterministic redaction/secret scanning for browser pages and local files
A relay endpoint that rejects unapproved fields rather than merely trusting clients
An owner-visible audit view showing sources, fields released, hashes, and retention expiry
Cross-surface tests proving credentials, cookies, screenshots, and raw DOM cannot escape under retries or failures

proposals.user_asks: “Stop everything you’re about to do, right now.”
proposals.why_useful: A physical, offline-capable emergency stop is the missing safety hand on a system that can act through the Mac and private browser. One long press on the pendant should revoke pending browser/Mac jobs, cancel relay retries, close any staged transaction leases, and return a spoken receipt. It works even when the owner cannot reach the laptop or voice path.
proposals.model_tier: No model for the stop path; pendant firmware emits a signed stop event, relay performs deterministic cancellation, Mac bridge and browser extension acknowledge. Use a cheap background model only to summarize what was halted afterward; never put an LLM in the stop decision.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant LED/haptic acknowledgment under 150 ms locally; relay fan-out and Mac/browser acknowledgments under 2 s. If a surface is offline, mark it unacknowledged and keep retrying cancellation, but never claim it stopped.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost; roughly <1 cent per invocation for storage/events, dominated by durable relay writes and retries.
proposals.security_concerns: The stop event must be authenticated to the paired pendant, replay-protected, and scoped to this owner's action namespace. It should cancel queued and leased work, revoke browser command tokens, and prevent new execution until explicitly re-armed. It cannot undo an already completed external side effect, so the receipt must distinguish cancelled, in-flight/unknown, and completed. Do not upload audio or screen data.
missing: Pendant firmware emergency-stop event and local LED/haptic acknowledgment
Relay fan-out endpoint with idempotent cancellation and action-lease revocation
Mac executor and browser bridge cancellation checkpoints between every step, with acknowledgments
A re-arm flow requiring an intentional pendant gesture plus spoken/visual status
Dashboard showing per-surface stop receipts and any actions that were already completed

proposals.user_asks: “Make sure this happens exactly once, even if I say it again or the connection drops.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the pendant, relay, Mac planner, and browser bridge can retry or independently interpret the same request, creating duplicate reminders, purchases, messages, or form submissions. The owner should be able to delegate an intent with exactly-once protection: repeated speech, reconnects, and agent handoffs converge on one transaction and one honest outcome.
proposals.model_tier: Use a deterministic intent normalizer and durable idempotency ledger on the relay; use a cheaper background model only to resolve genuinely ambiguous natural-language references. No realtime model is needed after the initial intent is formed.
proposals.latency_budget: A duplicate request should be recognized locally or by relay in under 300 ms; first execution may take normal task time. After a disconnect, resume from the durable transaction state rather than restarting.
proposals.cost_estimate: Well under 1 cent per request for relay/database reads and receipts; cost is dominated by any ordinary browser or Mac execution, not deduplication.
proposals.security_concerns: Idempotency keys must be scoped to the owner, intent, target account, and an explicit expiry so a future legitimate action is not suppressed. Store hashes and outcome metadata rather than sensitive page contents. Ambiguous target changes must create a new transaction and require review; never treat a failed/unknown external result as safe to repeat automatically.
missing: A relay-owned durable intent ledger with states planned, leased, committed, failed, and unknown
Canonical idempotency-key derivation shared by realtime voice, Mac planner, and browser bridge
Commit tokens exchanged only after a verified external postcondition, with a reconciliation path for unknown outcomes
Execution adapters that accept and persist the key across retries and agent handoffs
Dashboard and spoken receipts that identify the single transaction and explain whether a repeated request was coalesced

proposals.user_asks: “Approve that exact change, but don’t do it if the page or data changed since I saw the preview.”
proposals.why_useful: Prevents a dangerous class of browser/Mac actions: the owner approves one exact form, message, purchase, or setting, then a page refresh, account change, or reordered list causes the same approval to apply to different data. The pendant can present a short confirmation code; the Mac/browser re-checks the authenticated tab and refuses or re-previews when any bound field, URL, identity, or permission changed.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to collect the owner's approval and read back a compact code. Use a cheaper background model (or deterministic code) to normalize fields and compare hashes; no model should decide equality of critical values.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview in 1–2 s; approval acknowledgement under 300 ms when the Mac and browser are online; final revalidation 1–3 s. If the bridge is offline, keep the approval pending rather than executing later without a fresh revalidation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per invocation when deterministic hashing handles comparison; a small background-model call (if semantic normalization is needed) dominates. Realtime tokens are limited to the spoken summary/code and confirmation.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitive authenticated page data remains on the Mac/browser bridge unless the owner explicitly asks for a remote summary. Bind approval to session/tab ID, canonical URL, account identity, normalized field values, screenshot/source hashes, action type, and a short expiry/nonce. Never treat a matching natural-language description as approval. Require a new button/voice confirmation after any mismatch; log a receipt containing what was approved and what was actually committed.
missing: A first-class approval token containing expiry, nonce, tab/session identity, field-level hashes, and owner confirmation code
A deterministic pre-commit revalidation step shared by browser extension and Mac actions
A refusal/re-preview event delivered to the pendant, plus tests for tab navigation, login/account switch, stale DOM, and duplicate retries

proposals.user_asks: “Before I approve this, show me what it will cause everywhere else.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a preview usually shows only the immediate form or message. The owner should be able to ask about a consequential change—booking, cancellation, purchase, account setting, or schedule change—and receive a compact impact map: affected calendar events, overlapping commitments, dependent tasks, notifications, files, subscriptions, and likely follow-up work. It must remain read-only until separately approved.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic extraction and graph queries for dates, amounts, identities, and dependencies. Use a cheaper background model to explain the impact map and identify likely-but-uncertain consequences. Reserve realtime for the owner's spoken question and concise readback.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial impact map in 3–8 seconds for one authenticated workflow and local Mac context; up to 20 seconds for several tabs or large local project data. The pendant should stream “checking calendar/files/account effects” rather than wait silently.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per invocation, dominated by summarizing multiple extracted sources; exact field and calendar matching should be local and deterministic. No paid model is needed when there are no detected dependencies.
proposals.security_concerns: This may expose more private context than the immediate action. Keep raw authenticated pages and local files on their owning surfaces; send only redacted entities and derived impact facts to judgement/relay. Label each consequence as confirmed, inferred, or unknown, include source and timestamp, and never treat an inferred consequence as a commit permission. Require explicit approval for any follow-up action.
missing: A read-only counterfactual planner that accepts a proposed action without executing it
Adapters that map browser form semantics and Mac calendar/files/tasks into shared typed entities and dependency edges
A provenance-ranked impact report with uncertainty and suppression of unrelated private data
A pendant-friendly streamed progress/result format for multi-source analysis

proposals.user_asks: “If you get interrupted, pick up where you left off and finish this without doing anything twice.”
proposals.why_useful: Long actions spanning the pendant, always-awake relay, Mac, and private browser currently stop at a dropped link, sleeping Mac, or expired browser lease. This would persist a typed checkpoint after every verified step, resume when the responsible surface returns, skip already-committed idempotent steps, and give the owner a concise spoken completion receipt naming what ran, what was skipped, and what still needs them. It is especially valuable for private-page workflows that cannot be moved to the relay.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background/job model to maintain checkpoints, retry transient failures, and compose receipts; invoke realtime only for the owner's live request or a concise interruption notice. Use the Mac planner for step decomposition, browser extension for authenticated tabs, relay for durable wake/retry, and pendant for offline acknowledgment/receipt playback.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge interruption/resume state to the pendant within 1–2 seconds when online; resume on surface heartbeat within 10 seconds. Individual browser retry may take up to 60 seconds, but never block the voice turn. Receipt generation under 2 seconds after the final checkpoint.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per resumed workflow depending on planner retries and receipt length; durable orchestration and browser polling dominate, not model inference. No model call for simple checkpoint transitions.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only action type, idempotency key, target surface, evidence hash, and redacted result—not page secrets or raw private content. Private tabs stay on the Mac/browser bridge; relay stores encrypted metadata and short-lived leases. Never auto-resume an irreversible send, purchase, deletion, or submission: stop at that checkpoint and require the owner's existing confirmation policy. Expire leases and allow cancel/undo from the dashboard.
missing: Durable cross-surface job/checkpoint runner with restart-safe state and retry classification
Progress/event stream from browser bridge instead of the current single blocking 45-second wait
A relay-to-Mac heartbeat/wake handshake and a user-visible resume/cancel queue
Typed checkpoint schema shared by /execute, browser commands, and receipts

proposals.user_asks: “While you’re doing that, change the plan: use the other account, skip that part, and continue.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a long-running Mac/browser task is effectively committed to its initial plan: the owner must cancel it and start over, risking stale work, duplicate edits, or losing the authenticated page state. This capability lets the owner correct an in-flight job from the pendant. The relay pauses dispatch, judgement validates the requested delta against the current checkpoint, perception re-reads only the affected state in the private browser or Mac, and action resumes from the first uncommitted step with a spoken summary of what changed. It is a genuinely cross-node behavior: the pendant supplies low-friction intent, the always-awake relay arbitrates a live lease, the Mac/browser hold private state, and the action facet performs the bounded splice.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief spoken correction and immediate acknowledgment. A cheaper background model computes the plan delta and receipt; faculty-judgement authorizes the splice, faculty-perception verifies affected state, and faculty-action executes it. No expensive model call for a simple skip of an unstarted step.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the correction within 1 second and pause new dispatch within 2 seconds. Show the revised step list within 5 seconds; resume within 10 seconds after verification. Never wait synchronously in the voice turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.06 per correction, dominated by one planner/verification call and any browser snapshot; relay pause/resume traffic is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Corrections must be scoped to the named job and expire with its lease. Never silently broaden permissions or switch to an account without displaying the selected account and affected steps. Re-read private state before applying a delta; do not persist page contents or credentials. If a correction touches send, purchase, deletion, or submission, stop at the existing confirmation boundary rather than treating the correction as approval. Keep an immutable before/after plan diff and allow cancel/undo.
missing: A first-class pause-and-replan protocol carrying a jobId, current step, requested delta, and revision number
Atomic compare-and-swap of the job plan so a late worker cannot execute the superseded plan
Pendant-to-relay interrupt messages while a background job owns the action lease
A typed plan-diff and affected-state verification record exposed in the job receipt and dashboard

proposals.user_asks: “Cancel everything you’re doing right now.”
proposals.why_useful: When the owner notices an unwanted or unsafe action, one spoken phrase or a physical pendant cancel should halt queued and in-flight work across the relay, Mac, and private browser instead of requiring them to find the right window or job ID.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model required for cancellation: relay-side deterministic emergency stop, with faculty-judgement only summarizing what was successfully stopped afterward.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant-to-relay acknowledgement under 500 ms when connected; Mac/browser cancellation fan-out target under 2 s. If disconnected, pendant records a cancel tombstone and transmits it on reconnect before any queued work resumes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; mostly authenticated control messages and local state writes. Optional summary uses a small/cheap text model.
proposals.security_concerns: The command must be authenticated to the paired pendant/voice session and scoped to the owner's jobs, not arbitrary relay tenants. Cancellation should be fail-closed: uncertain in-flight side effects become needs-review, never reported as undone. Do not promise rollback for external actions already committed; show a receipt and available undo.
missing: A relay-wide revocation/tombstone primitive that every worker checks before dispatch and between steps
Mac endpoint to cancel a job set, not just one job ID; browser queue flush bound to session/owner
Pendant offline cancel persistence and local feedback
Dashboard view of stopped, committed, and uncertain actions

proposals.user_asks: “Handle this across my Mac and logged-in browser, keep going if a device disconnects, and tell me exactly what was done, what was skipped, and what I can undo.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a multi-step outcome but cannot safely carry it through a partial Mac/browser outage: it may leave queued browser commands stale, mistake an untrusted UI receipt for success, or lose its place after a disconnect. A durable saga makes partial completion explicit, resumes only from fresh witnesses, and gives the owner a truthful per-step receipt plus compensation where available.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed step graph and risk/approval policy
relay persists saga and step state, leases, idempotency keys, retry/compensation records, and wakes the job after disconnects
faculty-action executes Mac steps through mac_run_actions/mac_delegate and browser steps through browser_run_actions plus /browser/poll and /browser/result/:commandId
faculty-perception supplies fresh /observe inputReachability and browser heartbeat/session witnessIds before every UI step
pendant receives concise progress, blocked, completed, and undo status; owner can confirm irreversible steps or request rollback
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for planning/reconciliation and retry classification; reserve realtime only for the owner's live confirmation and urgent interruption. Deterministic route/step validation and idempotency should be code, not model calls.
proposals.latency_budget: First acknowledgment under 1 second; reversible steps normally under 10 seconds each. A disconnected bridge should become “paused/unknown” immediately, never “failed/succeeded”; resume on a fresh heartbeat, with a bounded retry window. Progress can arrive asynchronously while the owner leaves.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly 1–3 background model calls per saga (plan, reconcile, final summary), plus one realtime turn only if approval is needed; dominant cost is context for private page evidence and repeated receipts, so pass compact witness IDs/hashes rather than full transcripts.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page content and action payloads stay on the authenticated browser/Mac path; relay stores hashes, minimal metadata, and encrypted short-lived payloads. Never retry an irreversible step without a fresh proof and explicit approval. A stale browser session, changed URL/tab identity, missing Accessibility/Screen Recording, or inputReachability != ready must quarantine the step. Unknown outcomes require inspection or owner confirmation, not automatic replay. Every step exposes before/after evidence, idempotency key, and compensation availability.
missing: Durable saga/step state machine and lease/heartbeat protocol spanning relay, Mac, and browser
A shared witness schema: observe inputReachability, browser extension heartbeat/session epoch, tab identity, and action receipt provenance
Quarantine/resume semantics for pending browser commands and unknown outcomes
Typed compensation registry and owner-facing partial-completion/undo view
A route/tool to inspect or approve one blocked saga step without replaying earlier steps

proposals.user_asks: “Take the document or secret I’m looking at in my logged-in browser and put it into the right Mac app or folder, without showing its contents to the AI; show me the destination and a fingerprint on the pendant, then let me approve the transfer.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently ask agents to read a private page or type data into a Mac app, but cannot safely move sensitive material between those trust domains without exposing it to model context, logs, clipboard history, or a broad browser command. This creates a sealed, owner-approved handoff: the browser produces an encrypted one-time payload, the Mac receives it directly, and the pendant verifies destination plus content fingerprint without displaying the secret.
surfaces: browser-extension extracts the selected download/document/field value and encrypts it locally under a one-time transfer key; it binds the payload to tabId, URL origin, and a short expiry
relay stores only ciphertext and transfer metadata, brokers the one-time rendezvous, and records delivery/expiry receipts without plaintext
faculty-judgement selects the destination app/path and sensitivity policy; faculty-action validates the destination and requests delivery
mac-planner/mac-terminal receives the ciphertext through a local authenticated handoff, decrypts only inside the target app or protected file write, and returns a hash/receipt
pendant displays destination, origin, byte count, and truncated fingerprint; a physical button confirmation authorizes release and a long press cancels/zeroizes the transfer
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background model for destination classification and metadata-only reconciliation; no model should receive the payload. Realtime is used only for the owner's live confirmation, if they ask conversationally.
proposals.latency_budget: Prepare metadata in under 2 seconds; after button approval, local delivery in under 5 seconds for ordinary documents. Expire an unapproved transfer after 60 seconds and make cancellation immediate.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap metadata classification call or none when destination is explicit; relay storage and bandwidth dominate, with no token cost for document contents. A small encrypted payload incurs ordinary relay egress/storage cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Plaintext must never transit model prompts, action logs, clipboard, or durable relay storage. Use authenticated encryption, one-time keys held only by browser and Mac, origin/tab binding, destination allowlists, expiry, replay protection, and zeroization on cancel/failure. Require physical pendant approval for secrets and external destinations; show a warning for uploads or sharing. Recovery must leave the source untouched and report whether delivery is unconfirmed, delivered, or verified by destination hash.
missing: A browser-to-Mac encrypted transfer protocol with one-time key exchange and origin/tab binding
A local Mac receiver that writes/imports directly without clipboard or model exposure, plus destination verification
Relay ciphertext rendezvous with short TTL, replay protection, and no-plaintext receipts
Pendant firmware/UI for fingerprint display, physical approve/cancel, and offline-safe zeroization signal
Typed transfer receipts and an owner-facing audit view distinguishing prepared, approved, delivered, and verified

proposals.user_asks: “Queue this for when my Mac and browser are back, and ask me on the pendant right before anything irreversible happens.”
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide an action, but execution fails or becomes unsafe when the browser bridge is offline, the Mac sleeps, or the page changes. This creates a durable cross-surface escrow: relay preserves the approved plan, Mac/browser revalidate it when reachable, and the pendant presents a short nonce-bound summary for physical approval immediately before send/delete/purchase. The owner can leave a task unattended without losing it or accidentally authorizing stale work.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a typed action plan with expiry, required evidence, and irreversible boundary
relay stores the encrypted pending action and wakes/retries it when the Mac bridge reconnects
mac-planner/mac-terminal performs read-only preflight and computes a before/after diff
browser-extension executes only reversible preparation, then reports current tab/session provenance
pendant displays/announces destination, exact effect, and expiry; one deliberate button gesture authorizes the nonce
faculty-action commits the final step and returns a signed receipt/undo handle to the pendant and Mac dashboard
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the short pendant approval conversation; use a cheaper background model for retry scheduling, preflight diff normalization, and receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate queue acknowledgement under 1 s; reconnect polling within 10 s; preflight under 30 s; physical approval prompt under 2 s after preflight. Expire/replan if evidence or page provenance changes.
proposals.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per queued task, dominated by one background reasoning pass and optional realtime approval turn; retries and relay storage are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Never persist raw secrets or form contents beyond encrypted, short-lived capsules. Bind approval to plan hash, destination, tab/session, evidence hash, and expiry; fail closed on any mismatch, duplicate delivery, or browser reconnect after stale commands. Require explicit confirmation for send/delete/buy, while reminders/notes remain policy-allowed. Show exactly what leaves the device before approval.
missing: Durable relay-side action escrow schema and wake/retry worker
typed preflight/revalidation endpoint with plan-hash and evidence binding
pendant-local physical approval UX and nonce display
signed cross-surface receipts and cancellation/expiry propagation
browser reconnect handshake that quarantines stale queued commands

proposals.user_asks: “Make sure I actually get this done before the deadline—only interrupt me when it matters, and keep trying until it’s finished or I explicitly release it.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can create a reminder today, but a reminder is not an outcome: it cannot tell whether the work was completed, whether the relevant browser/Mac state changed, or whether a missed alert should be escalated. This would create a closed-loop commitment that observes permitted completion evidence across the Mac and logged-in browser, adapts interruption timing to the owner's meeting/quiet state, and keeps a concise spoken status on the pendant until the owner acknowledges completion or cancels it.
surfaces: faculty-judgement defines the commitment, acceptable completion evidence, deadline, quiet hours, escalation ceiling, and cancellation policy
relay persists the commitment and runs the low-cost schedule/evidence checks while the Mac sleeps
mac-planner/mac-terminal checks local artifacts, calendar state, and application evidence without sending or deleting anything
browser-extension checks only the named authenticated page/session and returns provenance-bound evidence
pendant gives a brief vibration/audio prompt, accepts completion/defer/cancel, and escalates only according to the stored policy
faculty-action updates reminders or drafts reversible follow-up work and emits a final evidence-backed completion receipt
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for schedule decisions, evidence comparison, and concise status generation; reserve realtime only for the owner's live response on the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Status checks every 5–15 minutes near the deadline, with exponential backoff otherwise; prompt acknowledgement in under 2 seconds; completion receipt within 10 seconds of observed evidence.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.08 per commitment per day, dominated by background evidence normalization; most polling and scheduling can be deterministic.
proposals.security_concerns: The owner must choose the evidence sources and escalation audience. Never infer completion from sensitive content without an allowlisted selector or local artifact hash. Do not send messages or alter records automatically. Store hashes, timestamps, and provenance rather than page text; require confirmation for any follow-up external action. Provide a pendant emergency mute and immediate cancellation.
missing: Durable commitment state machine with deadline, quiet hours, escalation budget, and explicit terminal states
Evidence adapters that compare local files/calendar and authenticated browser regions without retaining secrets
Pendant acknowledgement/defer/mute events delivered to relay when the Mac is asleep
Cross-surface notification policy and deduplicated escalation delivery
A completion verifier that requires two independent signals or explicit owner acknowledgement for ambiguous tasks

proposals.user_asks: “Finish this across my Mac and my logged-in browser, and if anything fails, put everything reversible back and tell me exactly what changed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can delegate work, queue browser commands, and issue receipts/undo, but the implemented receipt layer explicitly has no precondition gates and cannot coordinate a partial multi-surface rollback. This gives the owner a trustworthy action transaction: the Mac can prepare a document, the browser can fill a private form, and a dropped pendant/link or failed later step cannot leave silent half-completion. The owner gets one concise spoken result plus a durable evidence bundle, rather than guessing which hand stopped where.
surfaces: pendant: capture the goal, speak progress/final receipt, and offer a physical cancel/confirm signal for the final irreversible step
relay-realtime: create a durable saga/job and resume status delivery when the live link returns
mac-planner/mac-vision/mac-terminal: perform typed Mac steps and verify postconditions
browser-extension: operate the owner-authenticated tab, capture before/after page evidence, and stop at irreversible checkpoints
relay: persist step state, idempotency keys, compensation records, and a compact proof bundle for later review
proposals.model_tier: Use the normal planner/judgement tier for decomposition and verification; reserve realtime only for the short spoken interaction. Run long retries, polling, and evidence summarization on a cheaper background model.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; begin reversible steps immediately. Each step may take seconds, but the owner should hear a progress event within 5 seconds and receive a final receipt when the Mac/browser finishes, even if they leave.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly one planner call plus inexpensive background verification/summarization per saga; dominant cost is browser/Mac screenshots and re-sent evidence context, so store hashes and short snippets rather than whole pages.
proposals.security_concerns: Private authenticated page data and local file metadata leave the browser/Mac only to the relay's job store; redact secrets from receipts. Never auto-compensate an irreversible send/purchase/delete: require the owner's explicit pendant or voice confirmation, show the exact final mutation, and lease the approval so an old confirmation cannot be replayed.
missing: A real saga coordinator spanning Mac jobs and browser command IDs, with durable dependencies and idempotent retries
Precondition/postcondition gates that can refuse to continue when the app, tab, URL, DOM/value, file hash, or account identity differs
Compensation hooks that restore earlier reversible Mac/browser mutations on later failure, plus a single cross-surface proof/undo receipt
A final-action approval lease and pendant-visible progress/cancel state

proposals.user_asks: “Do it, then check the real result and tell me whether it actually took effect.”
proposals.why_useful: Action receipts currently describe what the Mac or browser executor returned, not whether an external system accepted the change. A browser click can be acknowledged while a form validation error, stale tab, network retry, or calendar conflict leaves no change. This capability performs an independent post-action read through the other available hand (fresh page/API state or a local file/status query), compares it to the intended effect, and speaks a truthful verified/uncertain/failed result. It is especially valuable for the owner's failed Gmail/GitHub/Calendar requests and prevents reporting intent as completion.
surfaces: pendant: receive the short verified/uncertain/failed spoken receipt and optionally ask for retry
relay-realtime: correlate the mutation with a fresh verification job and retain evidence while the owner is away
mac-planner/mac-vision/mac-terminal: execute local mutations and independently re-read files, app state, or network responses
browser-extension: reattach to the same authenticated session, refresh or reopen the relevant page, and extract the resulting record rather than trusting the click result
faculty-perception: classify fresh evidence and detect stale/ambiguous state before faculty-judgement reports success
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background verifier with deterministic typed comparators for most checks; use the expensive realtime tier only to resolve genuinely ambiguous evidence or explain a concise exception.
proposals.latency_budget: Return an immediate 'working' acknowledgement, then verify within 5–15 seconds for local/browser changes; long-running external systems can remain queued and notify through the pendant when the read-back is available.
proposals.cost_estimate: One extra browser read or Mac status call per mutation, plus a small comparator; API cost is low and dominated by screenshots/page extraction only when structured evidence is unavailable.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification reads can expose private account data, so retain only the minimum matching field and a source URL/tab ID, redacting tokens and message bodies. Never treat cached DOM or an old receipt as proof; require a fresh timestamp and matching account/record identity. Do not send or retry an irreversible action automatically merely because verification is uncertain.
missing: A typed intent-to-observation contract (expected record, fields, and comparator) for each action type
Freshness/session/account checks and a verifier separate from the mutating executor
Cross-surface evidence storage linking mutation receipt to read-back citation
Spoken receipt states that distinguish attempted, verified, contradicted, and unable-to-verify

proposals.user_asks: “Send this private page to the person I’m with, but only let them see exactly this one thing for the next ten minutes.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can read authenticated pages in Safari, but cannot safely turn a selected fact into a controlled, recipient-bound handoff. Today they must expose the whole tab, copy sensitive text manually, or use an ordinary share link that may persist indefinitely. This would let the pendant identify the intended excerpt, the browser extract it from the logged-in page, the relay issue a one-time capability, and the nearby recipient prove possession before seeing it. It is a new action surface: sharing a narrowly scoped result, not merely reading or changing the owner’s account.
surfaces: pendant: capture the spoken scope and recipient cue, show a short code/QR via the LED or paired display, and require a deliberate button press before release
browser-extension: extract only the named fields from the authenticated tab, retain source URL/locator evidence, and never transmit session cookies or the whole page
Mac: render or print the one-time handoff code and show the exact excerpt and expiry for owner review
relay: mint a single-use, recipient-bound encrypted capability, enforce expiry/revocation and prevent replay, then deliver a compact spoken/audible completion receipt
faculty-perception/judgement: resolve which page and fields the owner meant, detect ambiguity, and refuse broad or secret-bearing scopes
proposals.model_tier: Use the ordinary judgement tier for scope resolution and a cheap deterministic service for token minting, field filtering, expiry, and audit. Realtime is needed only for the short spoken confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Show a preview in under 3 seconds and make the recipient handoff available within 5 seconds after confirmation. Revocation should take effect immediately; expired links must fail without model work.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per handoff: one short planning call plus relay storage and cryptographic token operations. Cost is dominated by authenticated-page extraction only when the requested field is not structurally identifiable.
proposals.security_concerns: Default-deny extraction and redact credentials, cookies, hidden DOM, and unrelated fields. Bind the capability to a one-time recipient challenge and exact content hash; require owner confirmation for every release, never allow forwarding or indexing, log access time/device, and support immediate revocation. The relay must store ciphertext or only a pointer to an encrypted payload with short retention.
missing: A field-scoped authenticated-page extraction contract with DOM provenance and secret redaction
One-time recipient challenge/QR or short-code exchange between pendant, Mac, and relay
Encrypted ephemeral payload storage with replay prevention, revocation, and access receipts
A pendant-visible confirmation/revocation interaction and a Mac preview surface
A policy engine that distinguishes harmless excerpts from secrets and blocks the latter by default

proposals.user_asks: “If that failed, show me why and give me a safe way to retry it—without making me explain everything again.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner’s history contains repeated opaque failures for Gmail, GitHub, Calendar, and browser access. Existing job receipts can say an action failed, but they do not produce a cross-surface diagnostic that distinguishes a dead bridge, stale tab, permission problem, changed DOM, rejected server request, or a genuinely unsafe request. This capability automatically preserves a redacted, replayable failure bundle and proposes the smallest safe recovery, so the owner gets a useful explanation and can retry from the exact checkpoint rather than starting over.
surfaces: pendant: speak one sentence naming the failure class and offer retry/cancel; provide a physical cancel path while a retry is pending
relay: correlate request, bridge heartbeat, Mac job, browser command, and pipeline events into one incident timeline; encrypt and expire the bundle
Mac: collect local executor diagnostics, app/frontmost state, exit codes, and pre/post observations without recording microphone input
browser-extension: capture tab/session identity, URL, command result, relevant DOM locator/error region, and bridge heartbeat while redacting page secrets
faculty-action: synthesize a recovery plan that is idempotent and reversible, then resume only from the first failed checkpoint
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic classifiers for transport/permission/stale-state failures and a cheaper background model for summarizing evidence. Invoke the realtime tier only for the short owner-facing explanation or an ambiguous recovery choice.
proposals.latency_budget: Failure diagnosis should be available within 2 seconds of the failed result; collecting a full redacted bundle may take up to 10 seconds. Never block the initial safe cancellation on model latency.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: mostly local structured logs and hashes; screenshots or DOM excerpts are collected only when needed. Background summarization costs more than classification but can run after the spoken response.
proposals.security_concerns: Diagnostics can contain authenticated URLs, file paths, clipboard contents, and page text. Apply field-level redaction before relay upload, retain bundles briefly, require owner confirmation before retrying any write/send, and exclude audio and raw keystrokes by default. A replay must use fresh credentials/session state, never stored cookies or captured secrets.
missing: A cross-surface incident schema with causal event ordering and stable request/step IDs
Redaction at capture time for browser DOM, clipboard, shell output, URLs, and local paths
Failure classifiers and typed recovery suggestions with confidence
A checkpoint-aware replay executor that can revalidate preconditions before retry
A pendant/Mac incident viewer with retry-from-checkpoint and delete-bundle controls

proposals.user_asks: When you’ve prepared something consequential on my Mac or in a logged-in website, ask me on the pendant for a one-button approval, carry it out only once, and tell me exactly what happened—even if I walk away during the process.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide and several hands can prepare work, but an approval can be lost between surfaces or an action can be left half-done. This gives the owner a dependable, reversible transaction boundary: private browser data stays in the browser, Mac work stays on the Mac, the relay survives disconnection, and the pendant is the physical final say.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a typed action plan and risk summary
relay-realtime sends a short approval prompt and receives the pendant's button event
relay durable job runner holds a lease and two-phase transaction record
browser-extension reads/fills the authenticated tab and returns before/after evidence
mac-planner/mac-terminal performs the Mac-side reversible step
faculty-action commits only after all preconditions and the pendant approval match, then reports a receipt back through relay and pendant
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for plan normalization, evidence comparison, and receipt summarization; reserve realtime only for the brief approval prompt and interruption handling.
proposals.latency_budget: Approval prompt under 1 second; after approval, visible commit within 5 seconds for a normal Mac/browser action. If either surface misses its lease heartbeat, abort before commit and tell the owner, rather than guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per transaction, dominated by evidence extraction and any browser/Mac model calls; approval and lease bookkeeping are negligible. No audio needs to be resent beyond the short prompt and result.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay stores only an opaque plan hash and expiry, not page contents or credentials. Browser and Mac return redacted evidence plus hashes. Require a fresh physical button press for irreversible actions, bind approval to plan hash, target tab/session, and expiry, make retries idempotent, and expose undo where the underlying operation supports it. Never auto-approve on timeout or reconnect.
missing: A durable two-phase transaction/lease protocol joining browser and Mac job records
A pendant approval event and explicit cancel/timeout event in the relay
Precondition and plan-hash verification at commit
A single cross-surface receipt that links browser and Mac evidence
Owner approval policy defining which risk classes require the physical button

proposals.user_asks: Give the hive permission to do exactly this one thing in my account, for the next ten minutes, and nothing else; show me what it was allowed to touch and revoke it when it’s done.
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets useful delegation without granting the Mac, browser, or relay a standing master key. This makes cross-device action safe enough for private accounts: one request can span the logged-in browser and Mac, but its authority is narrow, visible, expiring, and independently auditable.
surfaces: faculty-judgement turns the request into a typed scope (account, tab/app, allowed reads, exact mutations, expiry)
relay issues and tracks a single-use capability token and revocation state
browser-extension enforces the token on the authenticated tab and returns redacted evidence
mac-planner/mac-terminal enforces the same token for local actions
faculty-action assembles the signed receipt and the pendant speaks the scope, completion, or revocation result
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize the requested scope and summarize receipts; use realtime only if the owner asks follow-up questions while the temporary delegation is active.
proposals.latency_budget: Scope preview under 2 seconds; token issuance and revocation under 300 ms online. If the relay is unreachable or the scope is ambiguous, do not issue authority.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per delegation, dominated by scope explanation or evidence summarization; cryptographic checks and revocation are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Never expose credentials to the model or relay. Bind the token to the exact browser tab/app, operation names, data classes, plan hash, and expiry; require fresh pendant confirmation for any external send, purchase, deletion, or permission change; revoke on completion, timeout, disconnect, or owner cancellation; retain hashes and signed receipts rather than content.
missing: Cross-surface capability-token enforcement (not just approval)
Authenticated relay issuance/revocation and a durable revocation list
Browser and Mac middleware that rejects unscoped mutations
A scope-preview response and owner policy for high-impact operation classes
A signed, merged receipt proving what the temporary authority actually touched

proposals.user_asks: “When I approve a prepared change on the pendant, carry it out even if the connection briefly drops—but never twice—and tell me exactly what happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can prepare an action and the Mac/browser can execute one, but a real-world approval is split across unreliable links and there is no end-to-end guarantee that the approval, execution, and receipt refer to the same one-time change. This gives the owner a safe commit protocol: the pendant shows the final before/after summary, the owner's button press or spoken approval creates a short-lived one-time authorization, the relay holds it through a reconnect, the Mac/browser performs the idempotent step, and the pendant gets a concise success/failure/expired result. It is useful specifically because no single surface can both authenticate the human's physical approval, reach private browser state, survive disconnects, and report a durable receipt.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a normalized action plan and irreversible-step boundary
relay-realtime assigns a one-time nonce, expiry, and durable delivery state
pendant displays a compact diff and records a local approval event (or cancellation)
mac-planner dispatches the approved plan through mac_run_actions or the job queue
browser-extension executes authenticated tab steps and returns typed before/after evidence
relay records the receipt and pushes the outcome back to the pendant; faculty-action can report or undo
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background/deterministic executor for queue delivery, idempotency and receipt validation; use the realtime tier only for the short approval conversation and spoken result. No expensive model call is needed to replay or verify a known plan.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview should reach the pendant in under 1 s; approval acknowledgement under 300 ms when online. Reconnect delivery may take seconds. The authorization should expire after 60 s (configurable), and every retry must be safe because the same operation key is reused.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per invocation, dominated by the initial judgement/preview model call; retries, relay storage, Mac execution, and browser bridge traffic are negligible. A receipt/undo path avoids paying for a second model call in the common case.
proposals.security_concerns: Never send credentials or page contents to the pendant; show only a redacted diff and origin/tab identity. Bind the nonce to plan hash, account/session, exact irreversible step, device identity, and expiry; reject replay, altered plans, stale tabs, and duplicate operation keys. Require a fresh physical button hold for irreversible actions, with spoken approval as non-authorizing. Persist an audit receipt and provide undo where the operation supports it. Data leaves the Mac only as the minimum redacted preview and result.
missing: A durable one-time approval envelope shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser bridge
Offline pendant approval spool with replay protection and a visible pending/expired state
An executor-side idempotency/compare-before-commit check for browser and Mac actions
A unified receipt schema linking plan hash, approval nonce, tab/session, before/after evidence, and undo token
The owner must still grant Accessibility/Screen Recording if a step requires GUI-only control; AppleScript and existing browser routes remain usable without it

proposals.user_asks: “Carry this request through all the dependent systems: if the private site accepts the change, update my Mac calendar and remind me; if it fails, leave everything untouched and tell me exactly where it stopped.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently ask for a single dependable real-world outcome spanning a logged-in website and local Mac state. A browser action may succeed while the calendar step is skipped, or a retry may create duplicate reminders. This capability is a compensating transaction (a saga), not merely a queued click: it commits each step only after verifying the prior step, uses idempotency keys, and performs safe compensation for already-completed reversible steps. The pendant gives one concise outcome instead of forcing the owner to reconcile several surfaces.
surfaces: faculty-judgement turns the request into a dependency graph with commit points, allowed compensations, and a final success invariant
relay-realtime persists the graph and resumes it after disconnects or Mac sleep
browser-extension reads the authenticated page, performs the approved reversible/irreversible step, and returns authoritative evidence
mac-planner uses Calendar/reminder APIs or AppleScript to create the local follow-up only after the browser commit is verified
faculty-perception independently checks each resulting state and detects partial completion
pendant receives step-by-step progress and a final success, partial-success, or safely-rolled-back result
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for graph compilation and recovery classification; deterministic adapters perform known browser and Calendar operations. Reserve realtime for approval and concise progress, not orchestration.
proposals.latency_budget: Show the first plan on the pendant in under 2 seconds. Each dependent step may take seconds to minutes because sites can be eventually consistent; reconnect resumption must not restart a committed step. A stalled graph should become paused, not silently fail, after a bounded timeout.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.03 per request, mostly one planning/recovery call; deterministic execution and verification dominate latency rather than API cost. Compensation avoids costly duplicate actions and support effort.
proposals.security_concerns: Require approval for the exact graph and every irreversible node; bind all nodes to the original plan hash and operation id. Keep private page contents on the Mac/bridge; send only redacted values and evidence hashes to relay/pendant. Never compensate by sending a message or canceling a purchase automatically. If compensation is unsafe, stop in partial-success state and ask the owner.
missing: A durable dependency-graph job format with node state, commit markers, idempotency keys, and compensation policy
Adapters that can verify authenticated browser outcomes and local Calendar/reminder outcomes without GUI permissions
A recovery worker that resumes paused graphs after reconnect and never replays committed nodes
A partial-success UI and explicit owner choices for unsafe compensation
A shared redacted evidence/receipt format across browser and Mac

proposals.user_asks: Run a 24 kHz audio path check and tell me exactly where quality or timing breaks.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently decide to ship the audio path but cannot obtain one trustworthy, end-to-end proof across the worn pendant, relay, Mac, and Bluetooth bridge. A tagged test run would distinguish codec, transport, I2S, resampling, and A2DP failures instead of reporting that a command merely queued.
proposals.model_tier: background/scheduled work on a cheaper model; use realtime only to explain the short spoken result
proposals.latency_budget: Start within 2 seconds; a 10–20 second test is acceptable. Spoken result under 3 seconds after the run ends.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per run, dominated by a small diagnostic transcript; most work is local counters and timestamps.
proposals.security_concerns: Test audio should be generated locally and contain no microphone content. Do not upload owner speech. Bluetooth device names and packet diagnostics may leave the Mac only if explicitly enabled. Require confirmation before any firmware flash, pairing change, or sustained speaker output.
missing: A pendant-side diagnostic command that emits packet/frame timestamps and counters without flashing
A relay test-session mode that tags and correlates frames end to end
Mac/bridge capture of A2DP underruns and a deterministic return/telemetry channel
A signed, durable audio acceptance receipt with per-hop evidence
An owner-approved audio-path acceptance spec (the 24 kHz criteria request is still pending)

proposals.user_asks: From whatever private page I’m looking at, turn the relevant deadline or follow-up into a Mac reminder and tell me what you used.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can read a logged-in page and it can create a reminder, but it cannot safely join those two acts into one provenance-preserving handoff. The owner must manually copy the date, title, URL, and context, which is exactly where deadlines get lost. This would make the browser, Mac, relay, and pendant function as one hand rather than separate tools.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for extracting and normalizing the deadline; use realtime only for the short spoken confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Extract and prepare in under 5 seconds; create the reminder in under 2 seconds after preparation; one short spoken receipt immediately afterward.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.04 per invocation; model extraction dominates, while browser and reminder operations are local.
proposals.security_concerns: The source may contain private account data. Keep page text and URL on the Mac/relay job record with least-privilege retention, redact unrelated text, and include a source link and exact quoted evidence in the receipt. Creating reminders is allowed without confirmation under the owner’s policy; never send messages or submit forms as a side effect.
missing: A typed cross-surface handoff contract carrying source tab/session, quoted evidence, timezone, confidence, and reminder fields
A browser extraction action that returns a stable citation for the selected deadline rather than an unverified summary
A Mac reminder action that accepts the contract and returns the created reminder identifier
A compact pendant receipt that can read back title, due time, and source without replaying private page contents

proposals.user_asks: “Pause that and remind me where we left off when I’m ready.” Resume any in-progress request across the pendant, relay, Mac job, and private browser tabs without restarting or repeating completed actions.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can interrupt naturally while walking or in a meeting, then continue later with the exact pending decision, tab/session, and next safe action. Today each node can know status, but there is no single resumable handoff artifact.
proposals.model_tier: Background model compiles a compact checkpoint; realtime model only speaks the short pause/resume acknowledgment.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgment under 1 s; checkpoint durable within 3 s; resume brief under 5 s, excluding external page load.
proposals.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.01 per checkpoint/resume; dominated by one small background-model call, with ordinary relay/database costs.
proposals.security_concerns: Checkpoint may contain private page excerpts and action parameters. Encrypt at rest, TTL by default (24 h), bind browser references to session IDs, redact secrets, and require confirmation before any irreversible resumed action.
missing: A cross-surface checkpoint schema with completed/remaining steps and evidence references
Pendant reconnect event and a spoken pause/resume command route
Job runner support for idempotent continuation from a step boundary
Browser tab/session reattachment and stale-page detection
A dashboard view of resumable checkpoints

proposals.user_asks: “Let me know silently when the thing you’re doing is ready, needs my decision, or failed.” The pendant should give distinct tactile patterns for queued, waiting-for-approval, completed, failed, and stale/disconnected work, with the Mac/browser continuing to do the work and the relay delivering the state even when voice is unavailable.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can walk, attend a meeting, or keep the phone away without missing a decision or completion. Today status exists in jobs and receipts, but the wearable has no private, glance-free channel that distinguishes actionable states.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model for state transitions; deterministic event mapping. Use the realtime model only if the owner presses the button or asks for a spoken explanation.
proposals.latency_budget: Tactile state change within 500 ms of relay receipt; reconnect reconciliation within 3 s; no model latency for routine signals.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per event (metadata over the existing relay/job channel). Hardware prototype roughly $3–$8 for a low-power ERM/LRA haptic motor plus driver, with a few mA only during short pulses.
proposals.security_concerns: Patterns can reveal that private work exists to someone holding the pendant, so allow a neutral mode and user-configurable mapping. Never encode sensitive content in vibration. Approval-required states must remain approval-required; haptics only notify and cannot authorize.
missing: A pendant haptic actuator and driver (the current device exposes only one button and one LED)
Firmware notification-pattern task with reconnect-safe event sequence numbers and battery-aware duty limits
Relay-to-pendant job-event push and durable last-unacknowledged state
Mac/browser job events normalized to queued, blocked, done, failed, and stale
Dashboard controls for pattern preferences, quiet hours, and a test pulse

proposals.user_asks: “Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, and keep going if I walk away; tell me exactly what happened, and never repeat a step after a dropped connection.”
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can choose a multi-surface action, but execution cannot reliably carry a typed plan across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant interruption boundaries. This would turn a decision into a resumable real-world transaction: the pendant can announce staged/running/blocked/completed, the relay can keep the lease alive, the Mac or browser performs only the next verified step, and the owner gets a concise receipt rather than a vague success/failure.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model to compile a decision into a typed step graph and reconcile receipts; use realtime only for the owner's live request and a short status utterance. No model call is needed to replay an already verified step.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant in under 500 ms; begin the first reversible step within 2 s. Resume after reconnect within 10 s. Human approval remains required immediately before sending, deleting, purchasing, or other irreversible steps.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.003–$0.02 per ordinary multi-step job depending on graph compilation and receipt summarization; durable state and step hashes dominate engineering/storage cost, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only opaque job IDs, step hashes, target surface, and redacted evidence by default; never copy page secrets into relay logs. Bind each step to account/session/tab identity and an expiry lease. Require owner confirmation for irreversible effects, and expose undo where available. A stale lease or changed precondition must stop rather than guess.
missing: A durable cross-surface step runner with atomic checkpoint commit and idempotency keys (the current browser runner backlog is still open).
A typed action envelope shared by judgement and faculty-action: preconditions, effect class, proof required, lease expiry, retry policy, and owner-confirmation state.
Pendant/relay status events for staged, waiting-for-approval, resumed, blocked, and completed; current durable audio exists but action-state delivery is not established.
Semantic receipt verification that records before/after evidence and prevents replay after a disconnect.

proposals.user_asks: “Show me exactly what will change, and let me approve it from the pendant—even when I’m away from my Mac—but cancel that approval if anything on the page or target changes.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently prepare browser work and may approve reversible actions, but cannot safely carry approval from a cited preview to a later execution on another surface. This gives them a wearable-native, exact-intent consent token: the pendant speaks a compact before/after summary and receives one deliberate approval; faculty-action executes only if the same tab/session, target identity, evidence hash, and effect class still match. A changed price, recipient, amount, page, or account automatically invalidates the approval and asks again.
proposals.model_tier: Use a small background model to compress cited before/after evidence into a short spoken approval card; realtime is only for the live confirmation exchange. Verification and invalidation are deterministic hashes and policy checks, not model work.
proposals.latency_budget: Approval prompt under 1 s after preparation; execution starts within 2 s of a valid pendant approval. Any stale or changed target blocks immediately and reports the reason in one spoken sentence.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.005 per approval for evidence summarization; cryptographic binding, expiry records, and receipts dominate implementation rather than inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Never treat voice recognition alone as authorization. Require a physical pendant button press after the spoken challenge, bind the token to job ID, exact effect summary, target/session/tab, evidence hash, expiry, and owner policy. Do not store raw page data or audio in relay logs; keep only redacted hashes and a receipt. Sending mail, deleting, purchasing, or account/security changes always require this explicit approval and must offer a clear cancel path.
missing: A signed, single-use approval-token format shared by relay, judgement, action, and browser bridge.
A pendant status/confirmation event with replay protection and a way to display or speak the exact effect summary.
A deterministic pre-execution verifier that re-reads target identity and cited before/after values and invalidates tokens on any mismatch.
A receipt field that proves which approval token authorized which browser/Mac effect.

proposals.user_asks: If you’re interrupted halfway through something I asked you to do, tell me exactly what is finished and let me resume it from the pendant without repeating any completed step.
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac, browser bridge, or relay can leave the owner unsure whether an email, form, or file operation happened. This gives them a trustworthy recovery path: a spoken pendant status, an explicit next step, and continuation from the last verified checkpoint rather than accidental duplicate actions. It is genuinely cross-surface because the pendant is the interruption/status surface, the relay retains the job, the Mac/browser perform the work, and the action faculty turns receipts into the next executable step.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short pendant interruption/status exchange; use a cheaper background model to reconcile journal/receipts and derive the next safe step, escalating to realtime only when the owner asks to resume or a high-consequence ambiguity remains.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant should receive a compact interrupted/awaiting-verification status within 2 seconds when connected. Recovery reconciliation may take 5–20 seconds in the background; resuming an individual Mac/browser step should begin within 3 seconds after confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per interruption with a small background model; costs are dominated by rereading large browser evidence or screenshots, so persist compact step summaries and hashes rather than resending full context.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not claim completion from an intent or an attempted command. Store requested, attempted, witnessed, and confirmed states separately; require fresh owner confirmation before irreversible continuation; never replay a write whose receipt is ambiguous.
