Private URLs, page snippets, and local file paths remain on the authenticated Mac/bridge unless explicitly needed for the spoken summary.
missing: A durable, typed checkpoint record shared by Mac, browser bridge, relay, and faculty-action (step id, idempotency key, precondition, side-effect class, receipt, witness, expiry).
A resume endpoint that accepts a checkpoint id and executes only the next unverified step, with stale-session and changed-page guards.
Pendant-visible pending/interrupted/disputed events and a compact confirmation interaction.
Mac and browser readback adapters that can independently verify side effects after a crash or reconnect.

proposals.user_asks: When a website or Mac app changes while you’re carrying out my task, pause at the exact changed step, tell me what changed in plain language, and let me approve a corrected plan from the pendant instead of guessing or starting over.
proposals.why_useful: Real tasks fail at the moment a page adds a verification challenge, changes a price, moves a button, or an app opens a different dialog. The owner should get a small, actionable interruption—what was expected, what is now present, and what the proposed correction would do—while all already-completed safe work remains intact. This is different from a generic approval prompt: it is adaptive replanning at a verified divergence point.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to compare precondition snapshots and classify the divergence; use the realtime model only to explain the delta and collect a short owner decision. Use vision only when structured DOM/accessibility or AppleScript state is insufficient.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect and pause within 1–2 seconds of a changed precondition. A concise pendant explanation should take under 3 seconds; after approval, resume the corrected step within 5 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for structured state diffs; roughly <$0.02 for an interruption, with vision/screenshot analysis the dominant cost and used only as fallback.
proposals.security_concerns: Never transmit full private page contents when a field-level diff is enough. Treat changed prices, recipients, permissions, account destinations, and security challenges as high-consequence divergence requiring explicit confirmation. Do not attempt to solve CAPTCHAs or MFA silently; display that the owner must take over.
missing: A precondition snapshot and semantic-diff schema for browser DOM, app state, and filesystem targets.
A divergence classifier that distinguishes harmless layout drift from changed intent, destination, amount, or authorization.
A pause-and-replan protocol that preserves completed steps and invalidates stale action leases.
Pendant event and response support for a compact delta with approve, edit, cancel, and take-over choices.
A Mac/browser adapter that returns stable semantic state rather than screenshots alone.

proposals.user_asks: “From the pendant, gather the things I need to act on from Mail, Calendar, GitHub, and my currently open private browser tabs; turn each into a sourced action card, create any reversible reminders or drafts, and keep working if I walk away.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner repeatedly asks to read Gmail, GitHub, and Calendar, but those requests currently fail or require separate surface-specific commands. This is a genuinely cross-body workflow: the pendant captures a short command, relay persists it, the Mac uses granted native AppleScript where browser access is unavailable, the authenticated browser bridge supplies private web context, and the relay returns a concise spoken result plus durable local workbench. It executes reversible follow-up (reminders/drafts) without sending or deleting.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to interpret the short spoken command and speak the final 1–2 sentence digest; use a cheaper background model for extraction, deduplication, prioritization, and action-card drafting.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds, return an initial digest in 15–30 seconds, and continue asynchronously for slow browser sources. The owner can ask for status or completion receipt from the pendant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn plus 2–4 background extraction turns per invocation; dominant cost is re-sending multi-source context, so pass compact per-item snippets, timestamps, and hashes rather than full pages. Native Mail/Calendar extraction avoids public-web calls.
proposals.security_concerns: Private mail, calendar, GitHub, and logged-in tabs remain on the Mac/bridge; only minimized snippets and provenance leave for prioritization. Never send mail, submit forms, delete, or purchase. Creating reminders/notes is allowed by owner policy; drafts must be visibly marked unsent. Require explicit confirmation for any irreversible follow-up.
missing: A durable cross-source action-card schema and local workbench writer
Native Mail/Calendar/GitHub adapters using the already-granted AppleScript/macOS surface, with browser fallback
A resumable fan-out/fan-in job that persists source cursors and per-item provenance
A pendant-friendly completion/status packet and audio queue integration

proposals.user_asks: “Use my private apps and logged-in sites to complete this task, but don’t send the underlying private text to the cloud—just return the minimum facts and a preview of what would happen.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can reach separate private surfaces, but it cannot give the owner a trustworthy guarantee that cross-app work is performed with field-level minimization. This would let the owner delegate genuinely sensitive tasks—such as reconciling a calendar commitment with an account form—while keeping raw mail, page contents, and credentials on the Mac/browser. The owner receives only a redacted result and an exact, local before/after preview.
proposals.model_tier: Use a local/background model on the Mac for extraction, joining, and redaction; use realtime only for the short spoken request and final confirmation summary. The cloud model should receive typed facts or hashes, never raw source text.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 2 seconds; local extraction and preview within 10–20 seconds; long browser work continues asynchronously with a spoken completion receipt.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small realtime turn plus inexpensive local/background inference. Cloud token cost is substantially lower because only selected fields, confidence, and hashes cross the relay; local storage is a few kilobytes per task plus encrypted audit metadata.
proposals.security_concerns: The Mac privacy broker must enforce a deny-by-default source/field policy, redact secrets and unrelated text, keep raw artifacts local, and bind every outgoing fact to source, purpose, TTL, and hash. The owner must explicitly approve the minimized payload before any irreversible browser or messaging action; previews remain unsent.
missing: A Mac-local privacy broker that performs source joins and redaction before relay/model access
A typed field-level policy and secret detector covering Mail, Calendar, browser DOM, clipboard, and files
Cryptographic provenance/preview records that prove the proposed action used only approved fields
Relay and pendant protocols for showing the minimized payload summary and requesting confirmation

proposals.user_asks: “Prepare this across my logged-in browser and Mac, then ask me on the pendant to approve it. After I press once, do it only during a short lease, verify the result from the source, and tell me exactly what changed.”
proposals.why_useful: This is the missing safe handoff between judgement and action: browser-extension gathers private facts and stages a form, Mac performs local side effects, and the pendant provides an unmistakable physical approval that survives the owner leaving the screen. A durable relay lease prevents stale approval; postcondition reads catch silent failures (for example, a form that looked submitted but was rejected). The owner receives one sourced completion receipt or a clear failure/expiry, rather than trusting that an agent said it clicked.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed transaction plan and risk summary
browser-extension reads the authenticated tabs, stages reversible fields, and returns before-state evidence
mac-planner/mac-terminal performs the local reversible steps and records action receipts
relay holds the pending transaction, lease expiry, approval nonce, and completion event while the Mac/browser may reconnect
pendant displays approval-needed via its single LED, accepts one deliberate button press, and gives success/error indication
faculty-action dispatches only after the nonce is approved, then browser-extension or Mac rereads the authoritative source and publishes a receipt to relay-realtime
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the spoken explanation and approval prompt; use a cheaper background model for extracting fields, checking postconditions, and composing the completion receipt.
proposals.latency_budget: Stage in 5–15 seconds; approval prompt within 1 second of staging; after button press execute within 2 seconds; verify within 10 seconds. Expire the lease after 2 minutes or on any material plan/state change.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically 1 realtime turn plus 2–4 cheap extraction/verification calls; roughly $0.02–$0.10 excluding provider pricing, dominated by authenticated page extraction and any vision fallback.
proposals.security_concerns: Never transmit secrets or full page contents to the relay when hashes/snippets suffice. Bind approval to a plan hash, account/session, target, and before-state; reject replay, changed tabs, duplicate presses, and expired leases. Require a second explicit spoken confirmation for irreversible financial, legal, deletion, or message-send actions. Store only redacted receipts and allow owner deletion.
missing: Pendant firmware skill for a nonce-bound approval gesture and local LED states (one button/one LED)
A durable relay transaction/lease store and push channel
Executor-enforced preconditions and approval gates (currently receipts exist but observeBeforeAction verdicts are ignored)
Typed postcondition verifiers for browser and Mac actions
Owner-facing pending-approval and completion UI/audio queue

proposals.user_asks: “Cancel everything you’re waiting to do right now.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an owner can ask the system to act, but cannot reliably revoke all queued or in-flight authority from the thing they are wearing. A pendant emergency cancel would stop staged browser submissions, queued Mac jobs, and reconnecting workers without finding the laptop or opening a dashboard. It is a distinct safety primitive: cancellation is owner-controlled revocation, not approval, undo, or a report after the fact.
surfaces: pendant detects a deliberate long-press/chord and gives immediate local cancellation feedback
relay atomically records a per-owner revocation epoch and pushes it to connected Mac/browser workers
mac-planner/mac-terminal and browser-extension check the epoch before every side effect and acknowledge cancellation of queued work
faculty-action reports which jobs were cancelled, which were already irreversible, and which require manual follow-up
dashboard and relay-realtime expose the cancellation receipt without exposing page secrets
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for the stop path. Use firmware and relay logic first; use a cheap background model only to summarize any already-completed effects.
proposals.latency_budget: Local LED acknowledgement under 200 ms; relay broadcast under 1 second; workers must stop before their next side effect, with a 2-second escalation timeout for stale workers.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; small durable relay write and one broadcast per cancellation. Hardware uses existing button/LED and adds no meaningful power draw.
proposals.security_concerns: Require a deliberate gesture to prevent accidental cancellation, but never require speech or network availability. The revocation epoch must be monotonic, authenticated, persisted, and checked by every executor; cancellation cannot erase receipts or pretend already-completed irreversible effects did not happen.
missing: Pendant firmware emergency-revocation gesture and offline LED state
Relay-wide revocation epoch with worker acknowledgements
Pre-side-effect cancellation checks in Mac and browser executors
A typed cancellation receipt and stale-worker escalation path

proposals.user_asks: “Carry out this decision everywhere it applies, and tell me exactly what changed.” For example: update the calendar event, send the approved browser reply, and save the final document on my Mac as one coordinated operation.
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide a multi-surface outcome, but action tools are isolated 1–3-step calls. This gives the owner one dependable handoff: preflight all targets, execute only the approved changes, detect partial failure, and report a single truthful result instead of implying that a bundle succeeded when one surface did not.
proposals.model_tier: A cheap background execution planner compiles the already-decided intent into typed steps; relay-realtime is used only for a short spoken approval or exception prompt. No expensive reasoning call is needed per step.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight and first reversible steps within 2–5 seconds when Mac/browser are online; long work continues as a durable job. A partial-failure or approval exception should be spoken within 1 second of detection, with the job resumable later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly one cheap planner invocation plus existing Mac/browser/relay calls; about $0.01–$0.05 per bundle depending on browser extraction and retries. The dominant cost is context and screenshots, so send typed step inputs and compact receipts rather than full transcripts.
proposals.security_concerns: Never widen approval from one target to another. Bind an approval token to an intent hash, target account/session, exact fields, and expiry; re-check preconditions immediately before each irreversible step. Do not transmit private page contents to the relay unless required. Store redacted before/after evidence and provide undo only where a compensating action is safe. If a step is irreversible or a session changes, pause and ask again.
missing: A first-class bundle/transaction route with typed preconditions, idempotency keys, dependency ordering, and compensation metadata

Per-step verification and proof tools so success means observed postcondition, not merely queued executor work
A durable runner that can resume a bundle and distinguish skipped, applied, failed, and compensated steps

proposals.user_asks: “If the app or website changes while you’re doing it, recover and finish the approved task without making me start over.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an approved action can fail when a tab reloads, a form changes, a Mac app presents a different dialog, or a session expires; the owner must repeat the whole task or manually take over. The mind should preserve the approved goal, re-observe the changed world, and repair only the affected step—without silently broadening what it is allowed to do.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap local recovery model for classifying executor errors and proposing bounded repairs. Escalate to the expensive realtime model only when the repair changes the approved effect, encounters an unfamiliar security prompt, or needs a spoken decision.
proposals.latency_budget: Attempt recovery within 2–4 seconds after a recoverable mismatch; continue as a durable background job if the page/app is slow. Ask the owner promptly only for scope, identity, payment, or security changes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one small recovery inference and a fresh compact observation; roughly $0.005–$0.03 per recovery. Screenshots and repeated page context dominate cost, so retain structured locators and hashes rather than replaying full transcripts.
proposals.security_concerns: A changed interface must not become permission to do a different thing. Keep an immutable approved effect envelope (account, recipient, amount, destination, content hash, and allowed mutations); require renewed approval if any envelope field changes. Treat MFA, CAPTCHA, payment, deletion, and external-send prompts as hard stops. Redact observations before relay logging.
missing: An executor error taxonomy distinguishing stale locator, transient transport failure, session expiry, changed content, and scope change
A perception-to-action repair loop that can re-observe the affected app/tab and generate a bounded replacement step
An effect-envelope and approval-scope verifier shared by Mac and browser executors
Structured post-action verifiers that prove the intended state after repair, rather than trusting a click/type acknowledgement

proposals.user_asks: “Do this, but only if the right account, page, and conditions are still true; ask me on the pendant at the last safe moment, then prove it actually happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an action and individual surfaces can execute it, but there is no single durable handoff that binds the decision to the correct authenticated browser tab/Mac account, obtains owner-presence confirmation, expires safely, and verifies the resulting world state. This would prevent a stale tab, wrong account, navigation race, or dropped connection from turning an intended action into a silent mistake. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant establishes presence, relay holds the lease, Mac/browser performs the act, and perception proves the postcondition.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed intent, allowed scope, deadline, and machine-checkable postcondition
relay creates a durable action escrow/lease, binds browser session/tab or Mac target, and waits through reconnects
pendant presents a terse local summary and nonce; owner confirms with the physical button or spoken confirmation, with a short expiry
mac-planner/mac-terminal or browser-extension executes only the listed reversible/irreversible steps and emits before/after evidence
faculty-perception re-reads the target (page state, Calendar/Mail record, filesystem, or API result) and checks the postcondition independently
faculty-action closes the escrow with a signed receipt, or marks it expired/failed and tells the owner exactly which condition was not met
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to compile and validate intents and postconditions; reserve realtime only for the pendant's confirmation exchange. Use deterministic route/action validation and perception checks wherever possible, not an expensive model call.
proposals.latency_budget: Confirmation prompt should reach the pendant in under 1 second after the target is ready; execution generally under 10 seconds; postcondition verification may take up to 30 seconds and can continue as a durable job after disconnect. Never keep an approval lease alive indefinitely: default 2 minutes, configurable per action.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per invocation depending on whether semantic page comparison is needed; most cost is one planner/verification inference and browser/Mac round trips. Deterministic receipts and lease handling are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: The escrow must contain least-privilege target/account/session bindings, a nonce to prevent replay, an expiry, and an explicit irreversible-action class. Do not send credentials or page contents to the pendant; show only a redacted summary and destination. Require fresh confirmation for send/purchase/delete/permission changes, reject if account, URL origin, tab identity, or relevant fields drift, and retain evidence only for the owner's configured short retention. A failed verification must never be reported as success. Browser bridge and bearer-token scope remain trust boundaries.
missing: durable action-escrow/lease state with atomic claim and expiry
pendant local confirmation/nonce UI and offline-safe confirmation semantics
typed precondition and postcondition schemas plus deterministic drift checks
a faculty-perception verification call that can inspect the same bound target after execution
cross-surface signed evidence envelope and idempotency key

proposals.user_asks: “Don’t just do it—tell me when it is independently witnessed as done, and tell me immediately if the witnesses disagree.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently distinguish an executor's acknowledgement from a real-world completion. A browser can report a click while the server rejects it, a Mac can report a file write while sync fails, or a relay can lose the result. This gives the owner a trustworthy completion answer based on independent witnesses rather than another optimistic receipt. It is new beyond ordinary job status, receipts, or undo because completion requires correlated evidence from the action surface and a separate observer, with disagreement surfaced as uncertainty.
surfaces: faculty-judgement declares the expected outcome and which independent witnesses are required
relay correlates a single action id across the pendant, Mac, browser, and any public endpoint, and applies a quorum policy
Mac/browser executor emits signed before/after evidence tied to the target session and idempotency key
faculty-perception independently re-reads the resulting state or observes a separate confirmation channel, producing a freshness-bounded witness
pendant announces witnessed, disputed, or unknown in plain language and keeps a compact unresolved alert until the owner dismisses it
faculty-action reconciles witnesses, retries only when safe, and records the disagreement and final disposition
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic witness correlation and state comparison first; use a cheap background model only to normalize heterogeneous evidence. Realtime is needed only to announce a dispute or answer the owner immediately.
proposals.latency_budget: Normal completion in 2–10 seconds; a dispute should reach the pendant within 2 seconds. Witnesses may continue asynchronously for up to 60 seconds, after which the result is explicitly unknown rather than success.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.04 per action, dominated by one independent readback and occasional normalization; correlation, hashes, and timeouts are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Witnesses must be independent in both credentials and failure mode where possible; never count two reports derived from the same executor as separate proof. Bind evidence to origin/session/tab, nonce, timestamp, and action hash. Redact private page contents, retain only hashes/snippets for short configurable retention, and require owner confirmation before any retry that could duplicate an external side effect.
missing: witness-quorum protocol and typed evidence envelope
independent readback adapters for browser, Mac apps, and public APIs
dispute/unknown state in spoken and dashboard UX
idempotent safe-retry classification

proposals.user_asks: Finish this across my Mac and logged-in browser tabs—even if I leave: carry out the dependent steps, resume after a device or network drops, and tell me exactly which steps happened, which did not, and what was undone.
proposals.why_useful: Today a decision can be made but execution is fragmented: Mac actions, private Safari state, public web work, and relay persistence have separate lifecycles. A cross-surface saga lets one spoken goal actually complete, or recover cleanly, instead of silently stopping halfway or duplicating an action after a retry.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to parse/confirm the spoken goal and report concise progress; use a cheaper background planner to compile the dependency graph, and deterministic action adapters for Mac/browser/relay steps. Escalate only ambiguous failures to the planner, not every step to the expensive model.
proposals.latency_budget: Start acknowledgement under 2 seconds; first executable step under 5 seconds; background continuation may run for hours. Progress is event-driven, with a final spoken or queued result rather than polling every turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per ordinary multi-step job depending on planner retries; most cost is background model calls for recovery/ambiguity, while deterministic Mac/browser actions dominate wall-clock time. Storage/event overhead is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and action evidence remain on the Mac/browser bridge unless explicitly summarized to relay. Persist only redacted step receipts and hashes by default. Idempotency keys prevent duplicate sends or purchases. The owner policy currently has no approval gates, so this must not invent prompts; it should obey existing action policy and clearly mark irreversible steps and failures.
missing: A durable cross-surface saga/job schema with dependency edges, leases, idempotency keys, and resumable checkpoints
Adapters that expose Mac and authenticated-browser actions as typed steps under one job, plus relay/public-browser fan-out
Compensation/undo handlers and a final causal receipt linking each action to its evidence
A job event stream to the planner/pendant, and durable persistence across Mac agent and relay restarts

proposals.user_asks: Watch for the exact condition I described, and then carry out the whole prepared action automatically—for example, when the authenticated portal shows the approved invoice and the Mac is online, download it, file it, and tell me; do not act while any precondition is false.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can ask the system to do a one-shot action, but cannot leave behind a precise, durable conditional instruction that waits for facts across private browser state, Mac state, and relay availability. This turns an intention into an execution that happens at the right moment rather than failing early or requiring repeated voice commands.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model only to compile the owner's natural-language condition into typed predicates and resolve ambiguity at setup; use deterministic polling/event adapters for predicates and actions. Realtime is only for setup and final notification.
proposals.latency_budget: Register the watch in under 3 seconds. Evaluate event-driven predicates within 30 seconds where a source supports events, otherwise at a bounded cadence (for example 5–15 minutes); execute the action within one evaluation cycle and report immediately.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 to compile and recover an instruction; ongoing cost is mostly lightweight relay storage and source polling, with no realtime-model spend while waiting.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser content stays at the browser bridge; relay receives only predicate outcomes and redacted evidence. Conditions must be immutable and inspectable after registration, with expiry, owner-scoped credentials, replay protection, and a complete receipt. It must never broaden a predicate after a near-match or act on stale cached content; existing owner action policy governs whether a resulting action is allowed.
missing: A durable conditional-intent record containing typed predicates, freshness limits, expiry, and action graph
Cross-surface event adapters for authenticated browser changes, Mac reachability/files/apps, and relay wake/retry
A predicate evaluator that requires all preconditions from the same fresh observation window
A wakeable scheduler/event subscription layer and a cancellation/status interface exposed to the pendant
Evidence binding from the triggering observation to each executed action

proposals.user_asks: When I tell the pendant to do something on my Mac, give me a physical completion signal, speak the exact result, and let me press once to undo the last reversible action.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can issue an action without looking at a screen, know whether it actually completed, and recover immediately from a mistaken reversible action. This closes the gap between judgement deciding and the action being observable in the real world.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to parse the short command and speak the result; use the cheaper local planner/worker for execution, receipt reconciliation, and undo eligibility.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 300 ms; completion beacon within 2 s for short actions; long jobs announce queued/running/done without holding the voice session open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for short commands; approximately one planner/action call per request. Storage is a few hundred bytes per receipt and undo token.
proposals.security_concerns: Only reversible, explicitly classified actions may be one-press undo; never undo sends, purchases, deletes, or external side effects. The spoken result may reveal private data to nearby people, so support a terse mode and require confirmation for sensitive receipts.
missing: Pendant firmware event channel for queued/completed/error/undo states
A durable undo lease bound to the exact action receipt and expiry
Mac-side proof that the inverse operation actually ran
Relay route to push completion events to the pendant

proposals.user_asks: When I say “I’m leaving,” check the unfinished work across my Mac, browser, and relay, tell me what is still exposed or running, and—only for the safe items I approve—close or hand them off so I can walk away with a spoken all-clear.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner cannot get a trustworthy, cross-device departure state: the Mac may have unsaved work, authenticated tabs may remain exposed, and relay jobs may continue without a clear handoff. This gives them a single wearable-originated leave-state with evidence and bounded remediation, rather than making them inspect every surface.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only interprets the short departure command and speaks the result. A cheaper background planner performs inventory, evidence reconciliation, and safe handoff; the Mac/browser executors perform only explicitly approved reversible steps.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial spoken inventory in 3 seconds; deeper cross-surface scan may continue for up to 30 seconds and return a completion event to the pendant.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus one background planning pass per departure check; storage is a small signed state snapshot and action receipt. No continuous model polling when the owner is not asking.
proposals.security_concerns: The scan necessarily sees private tab titles, active applications, and job metadata; retain only redacted findings with short TTL. Never auto-close, log out, send, delete, or kill a job. Require explicit approval per category, and show exactly which tabs/jobs would be affected before execution.
missing: A cross-surface departure-state schema with freshness and evidence provenance
Mac APIs for unsaved-document and active-session inventory without relying on Accessibility
Browser session exposure/lock metadata and a safe handoff operation
Relay job lease/handoff semantics so queued work cannot be abandoned or duplicated
Pendant offline acknowledgement and a durable completion event when the Mac link drops

proposals.user_asks: “Do this across my Mac and browser, and keep going if one step fails—tell me exactly what completed, what did not, and safely undo whatever can be undone.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a multi-surface request can leave a half-finished real-world state: a calendar event created but an email draft not, or a browser form changed after the Mac step failed. This gives the owner one durable transaction with explicit checkpoints, idempotent retries, compensating actions, and a concise pendant-visible partial-failure report instead of guessing or silently repeating side effects.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap/background planner to compile a typed saga and classify retry/compensation; use realtime only to obtain an owner confirmation for an irreversible step or report a live failure. Deterministic executors and receipts do the actual work.
proposals.latency_budget: Queue immediately and acknowledge in under 1 second; reversible steps may run asynchronously. Retry transient failures with bounded backoff, and report each checkpoint within 5 seconds. Pause before any irreversible or ambiguous compensation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost: one planning call per transaction plus cheap status synthesis; most execution is deterministic Mac/browser work. Storage is small (step definitions, hashes, receipts, and compensation records), with configurable retention.
proposals.security_concerns: Never retry non-idempotent actions without an idempotency key and a fresh proof of current state. Require explicit pendant confirmation for sends, purchases, deletion, or compensation that could lose data. Store only redacted before/after evidence; authenticated page content stays on the Mac/relay boundary. A stale browser tab or changed DOM must fail closed, not click by coordinates.
missing: A durable saga/transaction coordinator spanning Mac and authenticated browser jobs
Per-step precondition checks, idempotency keys, retry policy, and declared compensating action
A common receipt schema linking browser command IDs and Mac action receipts
Pendant/dashboard rendering of running, paused, partially-complete, and safely-undoable states
A verified compensation endpoint and owner confirmation handshake

proposals.user_asks: “After you do it, verify that the real-world result actually happened—not just that the click or command succeeded—and tell me if it didn’t.”
proposals.why_useful: Current automation can report that an action was queued or a UI interaction completed, but the owner cannot reliably know whether the external system accepted it: a calendar invite may not be created, a support form may time out after submission, or a payment may remain pending. This capability closes the loop by checking an independent confirmation surface and escalating ambiguity instead of claiming success.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background verifier for deterministic polling, matching, and evidence comparison; reserve realtime for speaking an urgent ambiguity or asking whether to retry. Use the expensive model only when evidence conflicts or the verifier needs semantic interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Return immediate execution acknowledgement, then verify on a task-specific schedule (for example 10 seconds, 2 minutes, and 15 minutes). Speak only on confirmed success, confirmed failure, or a timeout requiring owner input.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually a few deterministic reads and one low-cost synthesis; cost is dominated by authenticated browser reads and any repeated verification window, not generation. Retain compact evidence hashes and redacted snippets rather than full pages.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must never mutate state or accidentally trigger duplicate submission. Bind it to the original account, tab/session, and expected result; treat a changed login or ambiguous matching record as unknown. Do not infer success from a toast alone. Require confirmation before any remedial retry, cancellation, or duplicate action.
missing: A first-class outcome-verification job linked to an originating action, with expected-result predicates and deadlines
Read-only authenticated browser and Mac probes that can inspect an independent confirmation surface after the originating tab closes
Deduplication and correlation rules for confirmation IDs (event IDs, appointment IDs, order numbers, or message IDs)
A receipt schema with execution evidence versus external-outcome evidence as separate states
Pendant/dashboard notifications for confirmed, pending, failed, and ambiguous outcomes

proposals.user_asks: Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, but only carry out steps that are still valid; stop at any irreversible step and show me exactly what would happen, then tell me what completed and what remains.
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can choose surfaces and the Mac can return receipts, but there is no shared execution contract that turns a multi-surface decision into a dependency-aware, stale-safe run. This would prevent a later step from acting on an earlier failed or changed state, and gives the owner one truthful completion report rather than scattered job/browser statuses.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed action contract
faculty-action validates preconditions, leases, dependencies, and idempotency before dispatch
browser-extension/browser_run_actions executes authenticated-tab steps with tab/session affinity
relay records progress and rehydrates the run after disconnect
pendant announces waiting-for-approval, completion, or blocked states
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap planner/router for contract validation and step compilation; reserve realtime only for the owner's live approval conversation. Use background execution for long-running jobs and a small deterministic reducer for receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: A contract should validate in under 300 ms; each surface dispatch remains bounded by its existing round-trip. Approval prompts should reach the pendant within 1 s, while disconnected work can continue asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost: deterministic validation/reduction dominates, with one cheap model call only when translating an ambiguous goal into steps. Browser/Mac execution and receipt storage dominate latency, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Never transmit page secrets into the contract or receipt; store references and redacted hashes. Bind each step to an app/path/tab/session and an expiry. Require explicit pendant approval for send/submit/delete/purchase/auth changes. If a precondition changes, fail closed rather than guessing. Keep an append-only receipt plus compensating undo where available.
missing: A typed action-contract schema and validator shared by judgement, action, Mac, browser, and relay
Precondition evaluation and dependency-aware scheduler that can skip stale steps
A durable run state machine with lease expiry, resumable checkpoints, and per-step idempotency keys
Pendant-visible approval/blocked events and a final cross-surface receipt reducer

proposals.user_asks: Hold this consequential task until I am physically present, then ask for one button press on the pendant and finish it across my logged-in browser and Mac; if the deadline passes or anything changes, stop and tell me exactly what remains.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently approve in conversation, but cannot create a durable, presence-bound handoff that survives a dropped link and guarantees the approval came from a deliberate physical interaction at execution time. This is useful for purchases, submissions, account changes, and other actions where a spoken 'yes' hours earlier should not be enough.
surfaces: judgement creates a sealed, deadline-bound commitment containing the intended outcome and a redacted preview
relay stores the commitment and wakes it when its deadline or prerequisite arrives
pendant displays a short hash/summary, indicates waiting state locally, and captures a deliberate button gesture with a nonce
faculty-action verifies the nonce and fresh owner presence, then dispatches dependent Mac and authenticated-browser steps
Mac and browser return before/after evidence and signed receipts; relay delivers a final spoken/status summary
proposals.model_tier: Use a deterministic state machine and cheap model for preview compression and result explanation; use realtime only when the owner is actively approving through the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Local button acknowledgement under 150 ms; approval-to-dispatch under 1 s when both bridges are online. Waiting and deadline handling are asynchronous.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: mostly durable state and cryptographic nonce checks; one small model call for the owner-facing preview/result. Browser and Mac round trips dominate latency.
proposals.security_concerns: Bind approval to a one-time nonce, commitment hash, device identity, expiry, and narrow action scope. Never put secrets or full page contents in the pendant display or relay events. Require a fresh observation after approval; invalidate on changed URL, recipient, amount, or account. Irreversible actions need this physical confirmation and cannot be approved by a stale voice transcript.
missing: A pendant-local one-shot approval primitive with nonce display, haptic/LED feedback, replay protection, and offline persistence
A relay commitment store with deadline wakeups and atomic consume semantics
Cross-surface proof format tying the physical approval to the exact browser/Mac action set
Owner-facing recovery flow for expired, changed, or partially completed commitments

proposals.user_asks: “Prepare this booking or purchase, show me the exact final change, and only carry it through once I approve—if the browser or Mac disconnects, recover safely and tell me whether it actually completed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can prepare browser/Mac actions and record receipts, but it cannot treat a consequential multi-surface action as one transaction. This capability prevents duplicate submissions and false success: it freezes the exact final delta, binds approval to that version, executes each step once, verifies the external service’s acknowledgment, and reconciles after a dropped link before offering retry. The pendant gets a concise pending/completed/needs-review state while the Mac/browser do the work.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to explain the proposed delta and capture the owner’s approval. Use a cheaper background model for plan validation, idempotency/reconciliation, receipt comparison, and post-disconnect polling; deterministic executors perform the actual clicks/API/AppleScript steps.
proposals.latency_budget: Show a frozen preview in under 2 seconds when tabs/Mac are reachable; execute in the background with progress updates within 1–3 seconds per step. On disconnect, stop issuing new writes immediately, poll/reconcile for up to 2 minutes, then surface a clear needs-review state rather than retrying blindly.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per transaction depending on reconciliation and page extraction; most cost is browser snapshots and background model checks, not realtime speech. Storage is small structured plans, approval nonce, hashes, and receipts.
proposals.security_concerns: Only authenticated tabs already open in the owner’s browser and explicitly authorized Mac actions are used. The approval must be bound to a hash of the exact before/after values, destination, amount, and expiry; any DOM/value drift invalidates it. Never send credentials or page contents beyond the existing browser bridge/relay. Require explicit approval for purchases, submissions, messages, cancellations, or anything irreversible; redact sensitive receipt fields in pendant speech.
missing: A durable two-phase transaction record spanning browser and Mac (prepare/freeze/approve/execute/reconcile), with idempotency keys and an approval-expiry nonce.
A verifier that distinguishes external acknowledgment from local click success and can poll/reconcile after link loss.
A single owner-facing pendant state machine for prepared, approved, executing, acknowledged, uncertain, reconciled, and failed.
Browser bridge availability/heartbeat and durable runner completion when the current browser device is offline.

proposals.user_asks: “When I’m physically with my Mac, let me authorize a sensitive action by pressing the pendant, and make the browser or Mac accept it only while that short-lived presence proof is valid.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a practical, phishing-resistant way to authorize sensitive local actions without speaking secrets aloud or leaving a standing approval behind. The pendant supplies an independent physical presence signal; the Mac and browser verify that signal before acting, and the relay records the authorization for later audit. This is not merely a confirmation prompt: it binds authorization to the owner’s nearby wearable, the specific action digest, the intended computer/session, and a short expiry.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic cryptographic verification and local state for the authorization path. Use the realtime model only to explain the action digest and ask for a press; use a cheaper background model for audit summarization and anomaly review.
proposals.latency_budget: The pendant press should unlock a prepared action in under 500 ms locally, with Mac/browser verification under 2 seconds. Presence proofs expire within 30–60 seconds and are single-use.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost for each authorization; approximately $0.001 or less in relay/storage overhead. Main engineering cost is secure key provisioning, replay protection, and adapters in the Mac and browser executors.
proposals.security_concerns: Private keys must remain on the pendant or a secure element; relay stores only signed action digests and timestamps. Bind each proof to a nonce, exact action hash, target device/session, and expiry. Reject replay, altered payloads, stale proofs, and unexpected target changes. Provide a lost-pendant revocation path and never treat Bluetooth proximity alone as authorization.
missing: A pendant-resident signing/proof primitive with protected key storage and a physical-button trigger.
Mac and browser executor middleware that verifies target-bound, single-use proofs before side effects.
Relay endpoints and durable audit records for nonce issuance, proof consumption, revocation, and recovery.
A clear owner flow for revoking a lost pendant and falling back to an explicitly slower alternate approval method.

proposals.user_asks: “Carry this out across my Mac and logged-in browser, but if anything changes underneath you, pause safely, keep my place, and tell me exactly what completed and what remains.”
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface can queue work and produce receipts, but a multi-surface task can lose its place between the Mac job queue and browser command lease. This gives the owner one resumable operation: the relay coordinates typed checkpoints across pendant, Mac, and browser, automatically stops on stale preconditions or lost leases, and reports a concise spoken state rather than claiming completion or replaying an action.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the owner's short command and announce state changes; use a cheaper background model for planning/reconciliation and deterministic executors for Mac/browser steps.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; individual steps may run asynchronously. On disconnect, checkpoint within 5 seconds and resume only after lease/state reconciliation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per multi-step operation for background planning/reconciliation; dominant cost is model calls for ambiguous recovery, not deterministic Mac/browser execution.
proposals.security_concerns: Action packets must contain only task-scoped private data, with browser session IDs never exposed to the pendant. Never replay a step whose idempotency key has an unknown outcome. Any send/delete/purchase remains stopped for the existing owner confirmation policy. Log before/after evidence and redact secrets from receipts.
missing: A cross-surface saga coordinator with durable action packets, step dependencies, checkpoint state, and compensating/reconciliation rules
A resumable browser result protocol replacing the current single blocking browser wait with progress events and polling
Mac executor precondition evaluation and lease renewal (the implemented receipts/undo layer currently records outcomes but does not gate stale state)
A pendant-visible compact state/lease indicator and a dashboard timeline joining Mac and browser receipts

proposals.user_asks: “Stop whatever you’re doing everywhere.” (or double-press the pendant button)
proposals.why_useful: A long-running Mac/browser action can outlive the spoken conversation. The owner needs a physical, low-latency stop that cancels queued work across surfaces, prevents a leased browser command from being replayed, and reports which steps could not be stopped. This is an emergency interrupt, not an approval gate: it should work even when the relay is reconnecting and should never silently undo irreversible effects.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model on the stop path. The pendant emits a signed stop event; relay, Mac, and browser executors apply deterministic cancellation. Realtime only speaks the resulting receipt if a link is available.
proposals.latency_budget: Local LED/button acknowledgement under 100 ms; relay fan-out under 1 second; each executor marks cancellation or unknown outcome within 5 seconds. If disconnected, persist the stop intent and apply it when the link returns before accepting new work.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model/API cost; implementation and durable event storage dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Only a physically authenticated pendant and the active owner session may issue the global stop. Stop events need monotonic sequence numbers and replay protection. Cancel does not delete data or claim rollback; every already-started irreversible step is explicitly reported. Store no page contents in the stop record.
missing: A firmware-local stop-event spool and button gesture handler that survives a dropped relay link
A relay fan-out endpoint that atomically marks an operation cancelled before dispatching cancellation to Mac and browser
Executor cancellation tokens and a terminal unknown-outcome state for in-flight commands
A compact pendant LED/audio acknowledgement and dashboard view of stopped, completed, and unknown steps

proposals.user_asks: “Handle this form using my logged-in information, but keep sensitive fields on my devices—do not send passwords, payment numbers, or identity numbers to the model or relay.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot safely delegate many everyday tasks today because the browser may contain secrets that must not enter model context or relay logs. This would let the mind coordinate a private browser-to-Mac action while proving that sensitive values stayed local, rather than forcing the owner to type every protected field themselves.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background planner for field classification and deterministic local executors for filling protected fields. The realtime tier should receive only a short status and never the values. A stronger model is needed only for ambiguous field semantics, with a hard deny-by-default policy for protected data.
proposals.latency_budget: Classify the page and produce a redacted plan within 2 seconds; local protected-field filling should feel interactive, under 1 second per field. If classification is uncertain, pause rather than transmit.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost because sensitive values never become prompt tokens; the dominant cost is one planning/classification call for an unfamiliar form and local browser execution.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitive values must be represented by device-local opaque handles, never copied into relay requests, model prompts, screenshots, receipts, or spoken output. The browser extension needs a strict field policy, DOM-origin binding, clipboard prevention, and audit hashes rather than plaintext. Require explicit confirmation for any protected value that would leave the local device; default is refusal. Recovery must clear temporary values and invalidate handles after completion.
missing: A browser-local sensitive-field broker that detects password, payment, identity, and private-contact fields and fills them without exposing values
A redacted action-plan schema carrying field labels, origin, constraints, and opaque local handles rather than field contents
End-to-end secret-flow enforcement across relay, Mac logs, browser results, screenshots, receipts, and dashboard
A user-visible privacy receipt proving which fields stayed local and which (if any) crossed a boundary

proposals.user_asks: “Hand this off to Alex.” From the pendant, create a safe, time-limited handoff packet containing the exact goal, relevant files or links from my Mac and logged-in browser, current status, and the one decision Alex needs to make; show me the packet before sharing, then let me revoke it or see whether Alex accepted it.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can act on the owner's Mac, browser, or pendant, but it cannot turn an interrupted personal task into a controlled delegation to another person. This would preserve context across a handoff without exposing the owner's whole account or making the owner reconstruct the work manually.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to resolve the spoken target and summarize the handoff aloud. Use a cheaper background model to assemble and redact the packet, classify files/links, and generate the concise decision request. Deterministic code should enforce scope, expiry, and revocation.
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken preview in 2–4 seconds; packet assembly may take 10–30 seconds while the Mac and browser are queried. Sharing must wait for explicit owner confirmation; acceptance/revocation status should update asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per handoff depending on document summarization; storage and notification traffic dominate for large attachments. Avoid sending raw account pages to the model when structured extraction is sufficient.
proposals.security_concerns: The packet must use scoped, expiring links or copied redacted artifacts—not live browser cookies or unrestricted account URLs. Show every included file, recipient, and permission before share; require confirmation for external sharing. Encrypt at rest, log access and acceptance, support immediate revocation, and never infer the recipient from an ambiguous name. Data leaves the Mac only for the explicitly selected packet and its audit metadata.
missing: A first-class handoff object and recipient/permission model in the relay
Mac-side artifact collector that can package selected files and browser evidence without exporting session credentials
A secure external delivery/notification channel and acceptance page
Dashboard and pendant preview/revoke/status UI
Redaction and secret-scanning policy for files and extracted browser content
built_from: GET /machine-context and GET /context-graph for task and identity context

proposals.user_asks: “Finish the prepared action.” The system should show me the exact pending changes in a short spoken summary, let me approve from the pendant, carry out the browser and Mac steps in order, survive a dropped voice connection, and later tell me exactly which side effects happened (or safely reconcile and stop).
proposals.why_useful: Today planning, browser dispatch, Mac execution, voice, and receipts are separate. This gives the owner one reliable hands-free commit path for multi-surface work: approval is unambiguous, execution resumes after disconnection, and the final answer distinguishes dispatched, verified, and not-done effects instead of claiming success from an HTTP response.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to summarize the pending commit and speak the result; use the cheaper background/relay worker for checkpoint execution, retries, and reconciliation; use local Mac/browser agents for their respective steps.
proposals.latency_budget: Approval summary under 2 seconds; pendant acknowledgement under 300 ms; each checkpoint may take seconds. After disconnect, reconciliation can run in the background and report on reconnect or the next briefing.
proposals.cost_estimate: About one realtime turn for the spoken preview and one for the final receipt; background orchestration is low-cost. Dominant cost is browser/Mac model calls for ambiguous steps, not the durable checkpoint store.
proposals.security_concerns: Never infer approval from speech being heard or a stale plan: bind approval to a plan hash, expiry, owner session, and a deliberate pendant button gesture. Destructive browser/Mac steps remain individually gated. Persist only redacted before/after hashes and provenance; private page content stays on the Mac/browser bridge. If proof is missing, stop and say unknown rather than retrying a possibly non-idempotent action.

A common side-effect proof schema from browser and Mac (before/after evidence, not just dispatch receipt)
A pendant approval/acknowledgement transport and local pending-state indicator
Reconnect-time delivery of the final spoken receipt and a dashboard timeline

proposals.user_asks: “Keep this situation under control until it is resolved.” The system should monitor the outcome of a decision across my logged-in browser and Mac, detect an exception, choose the next permitted reversible step, and escalate to my pendant only when judgment is needed—for example, track a support case or delivery, prepare the next response when the status changes, and stop before any irreversible action.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can perform a task or watch a page, but it cannot maintain a bounded course of action whose next step depends on verified real-world changes. The owner gets continuity rather than repeated re-explanations, while irreversible decisions remain theirs.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for polling, state comparison, and selecting among pre-approved reversible branches. Invoke the realtime model only for a genuinely novel exception or a short pendant escalation. Keep browser/Mac execution local to their surfaces.
proposals.latency_budget: Routine checks can run on a minutes-to-hours cadence. An exception should reach the pendant within one polling interval; spoken escalation under 2 seconds once connected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low background inference and storage per monitored case; cost is dominated by authenticated page reads and occasional local-agent calls. Realtime usage occurs only for unresolved exceptions.
proposals.security_concerns: The owner must define scope, expiry, allowed surfaces, and permitted reversible actions. Never send, purchase, delete, or submit without fresh confirmation. Store state fingerprints and provenance rather than private page bodies where possible. If authentication expires or evidence conflicts, pause and notify rather than improvising.
missing: A bounded case/contingency object containing goal, expiry, allowed actions, escalation policy, and stop conditions
State-transition evaluation that compares verified browser/Mac observations against the case and selects a pre-approved branch
A durable exception queue that can wake the relay and deliver a pendant notification
Per-branch authorization and proof that an action changed the intended state, not merely that it was dispatched

proposals.user_asks: “Before my next call, verify that my pendant audio is healthy; if it is not, fix what you can and tell me exactly what failed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide that audio quality matters but cannot establish which hand is broken. This gives the owner a one-sentence preflight result and an automatic, reversible recovery path instead of discovering a bad mic, relay profile, or bridge playback after the call starts.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to interpret the spoken request and announce the result; use a cheap background/local worker for metric comparison, packet accounting, and receipt generation.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive preflight under 10 seconds; fallback/reconnect may continue in background with a completion receipt.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per preflight, dominated by one short audio/test exchange and storage of metrics; no expensive model call is needed after intent parsing.

The relay receives only counters and timestamps; any Mac repair action must be limited to reversible audio-route/profile changes and produce an undoable receipt. Require confirmation before changing unrelated system audio or starting a microphone.
missing: pendant-local calibration chirp/capture test and counters
relay-side 24 kHz profile validation and safe fallback

proposals.user_asks: “After you do it, prove that it actually happened—check the resulting app, page, or device state, and tell me if the proof is missing or contradicts the plan.”
proposals.why_useful: Execution receipts currently report what the harness attempted, not whether the outside world accepted it. A mail send can be rejected, a browser click can hit the wrong tab, a reminder can fail silently, and a dropped pendant link can hide the result. This capability closes the action loop with independent postcondition evidence and an honest UNKNOWN state instead of claiming success.

proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic checks and a small background model for semantic matching of evidence to postconditions; use realtime only to explain the verified result during live conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Add 1–3 seconds for local Mac checks and up to 10 seconds for a browser re-read. If a surface is offline, report PENDING/UNKNOWN and verify automatically on reconnect.

For irreversible effects, require positive evidence or explicitly tell the owner that confirmation is unavailable; do not automatically retry non-idempotent actions.

reconciliation route that stores before/after evidence and contradiction reasons

proposals.user_asks: “If this becomes urgent, keep trying every way to reach me until I acknowledge it—and show me when and where I acknowledged it.”

This is an escalation contract, not a one-shot notification: it continues across relay, pendant, and Mac fallback until there is a real acknowledgment, then records a trustworthy delivery and acknowledgment history.

relay remains the durable coordinator and schedules retries while the Mac is asleep or disconnected

mac-planner uses granted AppleScript/notifications as a fallback when the pendant is unavailable
relay reconciles duplicate deliveries, stops all escalation on one valid acknowledgment, and exposes a concise receipt to unified and relay-realtime
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic scheduling, delivery, deduplication, and acknowledgment validation; use the background tier only to summarize the receipt or classify an ambiguous spoken acknowledgment. Realtime is reserved for the live alert conversation.

pendant firmware alert/retry/acknowledgment state that survives a dropped link
common delivery-attempt and acknowledgment proof schema across pendant and Mac
deduplication and cancellation when multiple channels reconnect

proposals.user_asks: Make this change across my Mac and logged-in sites, and keep working until you can prove the final state is correct; if one step fails, tell me exactly what remains and safely repair only the reversible parts.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can execute actions and produce receipts, but a receipt is not proof that an external service accepted the change. This gives the owner a single outcome across browser, Mac, relay, and pendant: an explicit target invariant, independent postcondition checks, partial-failure accounting, and a repair/resume path rather than false success.

proposals.user_asks: If this exact situation occurs, carry out the approved action automatically—but only while the facts I approved are still true, and tell me if the situation changed instead of using stale permission.
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot safely delegate conditional real-world actions today. Existing routines, watches, plans, and approvals are separate: an approval can outlive the page state it was based on, or a delayed Mac/browser job can act after circumstances change. This would let the owner delegate time-sensitive work without granting a broad standing permission or forcing them to stay present.
proposals.model_tier: Use the background tier for polling and deterministic condition evaluation; use gpt-5.6-luna only to interpret an ambiguous condition or construct the proposed action; use gpt-realtime-2.1 only for a just-in-time pendant confirmation or exception.
proposals.latency_budget: Condition checks should be seconds to minutes depending on the trigger, with no model call for unchanged structured facts. Once triggered, start within 2 seconds; refuse execution if the approval lease or state hash is stale.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for structured triggers: approximately $0.001–$0.02 per evaluation cycle when deterministic, with occasional $0.02–$0.10 planner calls for ambiguous page changes. Storage is a small signed condition/approval record.
proposals.security_concerns: A permission must be narrowly bound to operation type, account/site, maximum amount or scope, expiry, and a hash of the facts shown to the owner. Private browser data stays behind the authenticated bridge/relay; secrets never enter the model. Any irreversible action requires an explicit policy choice and a single-use approval token; if facts drift, pause and notify rather than guessing.
missing: A durable conditional-operation primitive with trigger, predicate, action, expiry, and failure policy.
Signed state snapshots and approval leases bound to the exact precondition hash, with revocation and audit history.
A deterministic event source joining browser changes, Mac state, and relay schedules without repeatedly sending full context to a model.
A safe executor that re-checks predicates immediately before each side effect and reports stale/changed conditions to the pendant.

proposals.user_asks: “Carry this through everywhere: update the source on my Mac, reflect it in the logged-in site, and tell me only when all sides agree it is done.”
proposals.why_useful: Today actions are handed to one surface and receipts describe individual attempts; a Mac change, private-browser mutation, and pendant notification can diverge. A cross-surface transaction gives the owner one coherent outcome: staged reversible work, explicit commit at the irreversible boundary, authoritative checks on each surface, compensation for completed reversible steps, and a concise spoken explanation of any partial failure.
surfaces: faculty-judgement creates a typed plan with dependencies, risk class, preconditions, and irreversible boundary

dashboard exposes the transaction graph, evidence, compensation attempts, and a one-tap retry/undo for still-reversible steps
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the live confirmation and short status utterances. Use a cheaper background model for plan decomposition, retry/compensation selection, evidence normalization, and final briefing.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; staged local actions within 5 seconds when surfaces are online; authenticated browser waits may take up to 60 seconds per step. Never hide a pending state behind a success phrase.

Dominant costs are screenshots/page extraction and repeatedly re-sending large evidence; use hashes, snippets, and typed deltas instead.

Require explicit recipient/account identity and owner confirmation for irreversible sends/deletes/purchases; redact secrets from evidence; bind each step to a session, tab, machine, and short-lived lease; never treat a receipt as proof. Data leaving the Mac is limited to requested fields, hashes, and redacted evidence unless the owner opts in.

Evidence envelopes linking receipts to source, pre/post snapshots, and transaction/step IDs
Pendant-visible transaction state and exactly-once irreversible confirmation

proposals.user_asks: “Stop everything right now.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently revoke an in-flight action everywhere with one unmistakable command. A browser command may be queued while a Mac job is running and the relay may still be speaking progress. A pendant-triggered global stop would immediately halt queued and dispatchable work, prevent new mutations, and return a bounded inventory of what completed, what was cancelled, and what needs inspection.
surfaces: pendant detects the dedicated stop gesture or spoken stop phrase locally and emits a high-priority signed stop signal

dashboard shows a red global-stop state, cancellation acknowledgements, and any mutation that could not be interrupted
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model is needed to stop or revoke work: use signed protocol messages and deterministic cancellation. Use a cheaper background model only to summarize the resulting partial-state inventory; use realtime solely if the owner is actively asking what stopped.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant-to-relay revocation under 500 ms when connected; relay-to-Mac/browser acknowledgement within 2 seconds. If the pendant link is down, the local stop indicator must still suppress queued local actions and retry revocation when connectivity returns.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for the stop path; small durable relay writes and cancellation requests. Optional post-stop summarization is one cheap background call, dominated by evidence collection rather than inference.
proposals.security_concerns: The stop signal must be authenticated, replay-protected, and scoped to this owner and device pair. It must fail closed for new mutations but never pretend an already-completed irreversible action was undone. Preserve tamper-evident cancellation and completion records while applying existing retention/deletion policy.

A high-priority cancellation channel that outranks normal queued work
Pendant-local stop gesture/state that works during a dropped network link
A deterministic post-stop reconciliation report

proposals.user_asks: “Do it, and don’t tell me it’s done until you’ve verified the result.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can queue Mac/browser actions and issue receipts, but a receipt only proves an attempt—not that the world changed. This cross-surface capability would execute the judged plan, then have perception independently inspect the relevant Mac window, browser tab, or device state and report success, partial completion, or an actionable failure. It is especially valuable for reminders, edits, browser forms, and multi-step work where silent no-ops are costly.

proposals.security_concerns: Private page text, screenshots, and local state remain on the Mac/relay according to existing retention policy; evidence must be redacted before persistence and expire quickly. Never verify by performing a second destructive action. Sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting still requires the owner's confirmation before execution; verification may run automatically afterward.

proposals.user_asks: “Do this for me, but only if the world still matches what we agreed; tell me exactly what changed, and stop safely if anything is different.”
proposals.why_useful: Turns the mind’s decision into a safe, auditable real-world action across the pendant, relay, Mac, and private browser. The owner gets a single spoken result—completed with evidence, paused for approval, or safely stopped—rather than trusting that a queued command probably ran.

proposals.user_asks: “When I walk away from my Mac, put my private work into a safe state; when I come back, restore exactly what I was doing.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets automatic, presence-bound privacy and continuity: sensitive browser sessions can be locked or obscured when the pendant leaves, while non-sensitive work remains recoverable. Returning to the desk restores the prior workspace without requiring them to remember a security ritual.

proposals.user_asks: “Handle this end to end, and keep me in control.” The system should carry out a reversible multi-step task across my logged-in browser and Mac, pause only at irreversible steps, and let me approve, cancel, or resume it from the pendant.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a goal but execution is fragmented: browser commands can time out, Mac jobs can continue without the pendant knowing whether they are safe to resume, and a spoken approval is not a durable transaction boundary. This gives the owner one honest action state: what was planned, what precondition was checked, what changed, what is waiting for approval, and how to undo it. It is genuinely cross-node: the relay persists the job, the browser supplies private web state, the Mac performs local actions, and the pendant provides a physical cancel/approve affordance.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to interpret the owner's short command and announce state; use a cheaper background model for plan decomposition, precondition/proof reconciliation, and retries. A physical pendant cancel must revoke the lease immediately; stale approvals and duplicate retries must be rejected.

A single executor that can route each step to browser or Mac, verify typed results, and reconcile receipts before advancing

proposals.security_concerns: Never silently substitute a different account, recipient, or destructive operation. A cross-surface receipt that links compensating actions and never claims completion for unexecuted steps

proposals.user_asks: “If this cannot be done now, keep it alive until the deadline, retry only when the missing device or account becomes available, and tell me before the deadline if it still cannot be finished.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an unavailable browser or disconnected pendant turns a potentially time-sensitive request into a terminal 45-second failure. The owner should be able to delegate work with a deadline and receive either a verified completion or an early, actionable warning—without repeatedly re-running side effects or burning expensive planner turns.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic scheduler and health/event matching for retries; background model for concise status summaries; planner only when a failed precondition requires a new plan.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge and persist the request in under 2 seconds. Retry on reachability/precondition events rather than polling; warn at configurable checkpoints (for example 24 hours and 1 hour before deadline).
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for typed retry rules and health events; background summaries generally under 2k input tokens. Storage and event delivery dominate, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only the minimum task data, encrypted and with an explicit expiry. Never retry sends, purchases, deletions, or submissions without a fresh confirmation lease. Bind retries to the original account/tab/app and invalidate them if identity, page state, or authorization changes. Show every attempt and its reason.
missing: A deadline/quiet-hours/expiry contract for delegated actions
Event-driven reachability and precondition notifications from Mac, browser, relay, and pendant
Retry classes separating safe reads, idempotent writes, and confirmation-bound irreversible actions
A scheduler that can wake durable jobs without repeatedly invoking the planner
Owner-facing deadline warnings and a final failure receipt with the exact unblock action

proposals.user_asks: If the pendant's reply was clipped, garbled, or interrupted, say “repeat that” or press the button once and have the system resend only the missing part, then report whether recovery succeeded.
proposals.why_useful: A dropped LTE packet or speaker underrun should not make the owner repeat an entire request. The pendant can detect its own playback gap, the relay knows the exact PCM receipt, and the Mac can regenerate only when the original is unavailable.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the owner's short recovery command; no LLM for packet repair. Use the cheaper background tier to reconcile telemetry and regenerate speech only when needed.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect locally within 150 ms; resume cached audio immediately; relay resend target under 1 s; fallback regeneration under 4 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost because the original PCM is reused; fallback TTS is one small speech generation, dominated by audio transfer and retention.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio receipts and telemetry must be authenticated and short-lived; never expose prior private speech to another device. Require confirmation only if recovery would replay a sensitive response after a long delay.
missing: Pendant playback sequence numbers, underrun/CRC telemetry, and a local replay buffer
Relay endpoint to fetch/resume an audio segment by pipelineId and sample range with idempotency
Mac-side audio repair/regeneration worker and a user-visible recovery receipt
Dashboard timeline showing which samples were replayed and whether fallback TTS occurred

proposals.user_asks: When I tell the pendant “finish this when I’m at my Mac,” have it preserve the exact spoken intent, wait until my Mac and browser session are both present, complete the reversible parts, and leave me a proof-backed review packet instead of making me repeat myself.
proposals.why_useful: Today a request made while walking cannot reliably become a finished computer task later. This would turn the pendant into a durable handoff point: the wearable captures intent, the always-on relay preserves it, the Mac acts only when reachable, and the browser supplies authenticated context.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture and acknowledge the short handoff. Use a cheaper background model to normalize the intent, select the Mac/browser execution plan, and summarize the completed packet.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgement; handoff persistence under 1 second; execution starts within 10 seconds of both presence signals; review packet ready within the task's normal duration.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus low-cost background planning; browser and Mac work dominate latency, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Encrypt the intent and bind it to the owner's device identity; do not execute while only the pendant is present. Browser mutations remain reversible or stop at a review gate, and the packet must include before/after evidence and timestamps. Expire stale handoffs rather than acting on ambiguous old speech.
missing: A durable handoff object carrying raw transcript/audio reference, normalized goal, expiry, sensitivity, and required surfaces
Presence attestation from both the Mac bridge and the authenticated browser session, not merely an online heartbeat
A scheduler that wakes the handoff when those surfaces co-occur and leases it to one executor
A review-packet schema linking browser evidence, Mac receipts, and the original pendant capture
Pendant UI for listing, cancelling, or deferring pending handoffs without network access

proposals.user_asks: If the browser bridge is unavailable, check my currently open logged-in Safari tabs anyway, gather the requested facts, and tell me clearly whether anything could not be verified; never submit or change anything through the fallback.
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser task simply fails when the extension is offline (currently offline with 9 pending commands), even though Safari automation is granted on the Mac. This gives the owner a useful read-only answer instead of a misleading timeout, while keeping all writes blocked until the bridge is healthy and separately approved.
