proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to clarify the owner's request and give the short spoken result; use a cheaper background model on the Mac to extract and normalize page facts. faculty-perception supplies current tab/page evidence, and faculty-action executes only read-only Safari automation.
proposals.latency_budget: 3–8 seconds for currently open tabs; if Safari or AppleScript does not answer within 10 seconds, return a partial result with an explicit unverified status rather than retrying indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn plus a low-cost extraction call; negligible Mac execution cost. Avoids paying for repeated 45-second browser waits.
proposals.security_concerns: Logged-in page contents leave the Mac only as the minimum extracted fields needed for the answer. No passwords, cookies, or raw page dumps are sent. The fallback is read-only by construction; any form fill, send, purchase, or navigation beyond the requested open tabs requires the authenticated browser bridge and an explicit later decision. Every fact carries app/tab URL/time and a verification state.
missing: A read-only Safari AppleScript extraction adapter with bounded timeouts and typed evidence capsules
A router rule that selects Safari fallback only for read-only requests when browser status is offline
A shared result schema distinguishing verified, stale, partial, and unavailable facts
Owner must re-enable the Browser Bridge for any browser write or private-tab operation that Safari automation cannot expose

proposals.user_asks: Let me approve one real-world outcome once, then have the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser carry it through as one coordinated transaction: each surface reports its precondition and postcondition, the next step cannot run until the previous one is evidenced, and if I walk away or a device drops, it resumes safely without repeating completed side effects.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide a multi-surface outcome but cannot reliably carry it across a dropped link or partial failure. The owner gets either brittle one-shot automation or repeated manual supervision. A coordinated transaction would make a request such as preparing a document on the Mac, attaching it in a logged-in browser, and leaving a spoken confirmation on the pendant behave as one auditable action rather than disconnected attempts.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the owner's initial clarification/approval and concise status. Use a cheaper background planner to compile the dependency graph and recovery plan; use deterministic local executors and faculty-perception for evidence, not an LLM, at each step.
proposals.latency_budget: Approval and preflight under 2 seconds; each local step should report within 5 seconds. On interruption, persist immediately and resume within 30 seconds after a surface reconnects, without replaying any step lacking an idempotent proof.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus low-cost background planning per transaction; local state and evidence dominate storage, not API spend. Recovery should avoid re-paying for already completed model work.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay stores only opaque transaction IDs and minimal step metadata; page contents and files remain on their owning device unless explicitly needed. A write step requires fresh preconditions, an owner approval scope, and postcondition evidence. Expired approvals, changed destinations, authentication changes, or missing evidence force a halt rather than a guess. The pendant gets a plain-language final receipt and can cancel the lease.
missing: A cross-surface transaction protocol with durable dependency/commit state, idempotency keys, leases, and recovery states distinct from ordinary jobs
A typed evidence contract for preconditions and postconditions that faculty-perception can sign for Mac files, browser fields, and pendant playback
A relay coordinator that can resume a transaction after Mac/browser reconnect without replaying committed effects
A single approval object carrying scope, destination, expiration, and allowed side-effect class across all surfaces

proposals.user_asks: “If I tell you to do something while I’m away, queue it safely, carry it out when the right device comes back, and tell me whether the intended result actually happened—not merely whether a command ran.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an intent can be handed to a Mac job, but online/offline transitions, browser failure, and semantic success are separate. This would let the worn voice surface, always-awake relay, Mac/browser hands, and perception/judgement form one reliable action loop: accept a bounded intent, execute only while its lease is valid, verify the postcondition, retry only safe steps, and return a human-readable outcome.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture/acknowledge the owner's short intent; use a cheaper background model for intent normalization, retry classification, and postcondition summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; execution may wait for device return. Verification within 10 seconds after each step, with a hard expiry supplied by the intent.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per deferred intent, dominated by background verification/retry reasoning; routine Mac actions and receipts are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only the normalized goal, allowed surfaces, expiry, and redacted evidence pointers. Never replay an expired lease or escalate an irreversible browser/Mac step without explicit approval. Private page content remains on the Mac/browser; relay stores hashes and status. Pendant should announce failure without reading sensitive evidence aloud unless requested.
missing: A first-class intent/lease record shared by relay and Mac jobs, including expiry, allowed actions, and a semantic postcondition
A verifier callback that can ask faculty-perception to inspect the resulting Mac/browser state and classify success, failure, or unknown
Bounded retry and cancellation semantics across reconnects, with an idempotency key spanning relay, /execute, and browser commands
Pendant delivery of final receipt/status when the device is paired again

proposals.user_asks: “Pause that job here and let me resume it from the exact next step on whichever device is available, with a compact explanation of what already happened and what will happen next.”
proposals.why_useful: Today long-running work is tied to the device and execution job that started it. A sleep, reconnect, or handoff can force the owner to repeat context or guess whether a step already happened. A portable checkpoint would make the hive act like one continuous worker: the Mac can stop after a verified boundary, the relay can preserve the checkpoint, the browser can reattach its session, and the pendant can resume or cancel without replaying completed side effects.
proposals.model_tier: Use a small background model to summarize checkpoints and select the next eligible step; use realtime only for the owner’s resume/pause voice interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 1 second. Resume briefing under 3 seconds, then execution proceeds asynchronously. Checkpoint writes must be atomic before any next side effect.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically under $0.02 per handoff; cost is dominated by one short checkpoint summarization, not the ordinary action calls.
proposals.security_concerns: Checkpoints must contain opaque references and redacted state, not copied private page contents or credentials. Bind each checkpoint to the owner/session and an expiry. Never resume an irreversible step merely because a checkpoint exists; require the same approval class and fresh confirmation when needed.
missing: A portable, append-only checkpoint schema with completed-step receipts, verified state, next-step preconditions, and browser session affinity
Atomic pause barriers in Mac and browser runners so no step is half-committed when a handoff is made
A resume planner that rejects stale checkpoints and reconciles them against fresh perception before continuing
Pendant-visible checkpoint summaries and explicit resume/cancel controls

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving now—carry out the prepared departure packet, but stop and tell me if anything no longer matches.”
proposals.why_useful: Judgement can prepare a departure packet, but today there is no single action-side operation that binds the approved intent to the right private browser tab and Mac app, checks freshness immediately before each mutation, executes only safe steps, and returns evidence. This turns a spoken 'go' into dependable real-world completion without silently sending stale or wrong things.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to resolve the spoken packet reference and report interruptions; use a cheaper background planner to compile and validate the packet, then deterministic executors for each typed step.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 1 second; validate and begin the first step within 3 seconds; speak per-step completion or pause on stale state. Long-running steps continue as durable jobs and are reported later.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per packet for background compilation/validation, usually dominated by private-page extraction; realtime cost is limited to brief acknowledgement and exception speech. Mac/browser execution itself adds no model cost when typed.
proposals.security_concerns: Private tab contents and local files remain on their owning surfaces except for minimum fields needed for validation. Never auto-send, purchase, delete, or publish unless the packet marks that exact irreversible step and the owner gives a fresh confirmation. Bind every step to session/tab identity, expiry, before-state hash, and idempotency key; if any check fails, pause rather than improvise.
missing: A shared DeparturePacket/ActionStep schema between faculty-judgement and faculty-action
A precondition/postcondition checker that can read current browser and Mac state immediately before mutation
Per-step proof records and compensation/undo linkage, not merely a final job status
A durable coordinator that can resume after relay or Mac sleep without repeating completed steps

proposals.user_asks: “If this changes while I’m away, carry out the fallback I approved—within these limits—and tell me exactly what you did.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can inspect pages and run a task, but it cannot safely connect a future observation to a bounded action policy. This would let the owner delegate time-sensitive contingencies—such as responding to a cancellation, moving a meeting, or completing a prepared fallback—without granting open-ended autonomy. Perception detects the triggering fact, judgement evaluates whether the policy still applies, and action executes only the pre-authorized bounded branch.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to normalize trigger evidence and compile policy branches. Use deterministic predicates and typed executors for enforcement. Reserve realtime only for the owner’s setup, interruption, or exception report.
proposals.latency_budget: Register a policy in under 5 seconds. On a qualifying event, evaluate in under 10 seconds and begin a reversible branch promptly; pause for a fresh spoken confirmation when a branch is irreversible, ambiguous, or outside its limits.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per triggered policy, dominated by private-page/calendar reads; idle monitoring should use event pushes or low-cost polling rather than realtime inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Policies must be capability-scoped, time-bounded, destination-scoped, and budget-limited—not general permission to act. Store only the minimum trigger and action fields, redact private evidence in relay logs, and require confirmation for sending, purchasing, deleting, publishing, or contacting a new recipient. Every execution needs a receipt tied to the triggering evidence and policy version; revoke immediately when the owner says stop.
missing: A conditional-policy schema with explicit predicates, branches, limits, expiry, and revocation
Event correlation across authenticated browser sessions, Mac Calendar/Mail/files, and relay events
A policy evaluator that distinguishes a genuine state transition from page noise and prevents repeated firing
A secure policy registry and per-branch approval/receipt audit trail

proposals.user_asks: Start this job now, but make it safe if I disconnect: pause before any irreversible step, tell me exactly what completed, and resume only after reconciling the Mac/browser state when I return.
proposals.why_useful: Today a multi-surface task can be queued or acted on, but a dropped pendant link can leave uncertain partial work. This gives the owner one reliable contract for unattended execution: bounded progress, an explicit pause point, and no duplicate actions after reconnection.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture the request and speak status; use a cheaper background planner/worker for the job, with the local Mac planner for execution and relay for durable orchestration.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge and issue a signed fence within 1 second; status updates within 5 seconds of each step; reconnect reconciliation can take 10–30 seconds before resuming.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per job when the background tier handles planning; dominant costs are browser/Mac execution and any screenshots or page extraction, not the fence metadata.
proposals.security_concerns: Departure packets may contain private URLs, account context, and action parameters, so encrypt at rest and minimize projections. Never transmit credentials. Require explicit owner confirmation for irreversible actions; a pendant pause or expired lease must stop workers before that boundary.
missing: A durable execution-fence/lease service shared by relay, Mac worker, browser bridge, and pendant
Signed pause/resume control and an offline-visible pendant fence indicator
A typed reconciliation endpoint that compares preconditions/state hashes with receipts before replay
Dashboard rendering for packet timeline, checkpoint, pending approval, and undo handles

proposals.user_asks: Prepare the real-world change on my Mac or in my logged-in browser, then send me a compact exact summary on the pendant so I can approve that specific change from wherever I am; apply it only if the approved summary still matches, otherwise stop.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently approve work through a dashboard or a live conversation, but cannot safely approve a prepared browser/Mac transaction while away from the computer. This gives them a portable, human-readable commitment check: approve the exact recipient, amount, text, or file change—not a vague job—and prevents stale approvals from being applied.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to explain the pending change and capture a short confirmation; use a cheaper background planner and local Mac/browser workers to prepare and validate the transaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation may take seconds to minutes; pendant approval delivery should be under 2 seconds when connected. Applying an approved transaction should begin within 5 seconds, after a fresh state check.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low metadata and speech cost per approval. The dominant cost is preparing private-page evidence or screenshots, which should happen once and be cached by transaction digest.
proposals.security_concerns: The approval must be cryptographically bound to a normalized action digest, target account/session, expiry, and precondition snapshot. Do not read secrets aloud; redact sensitive fields while preserving enough detail to identify the change. Reject replay, changed amounts/recipients, expired approvals, and approvals from an unpaired pendant. Irreversible actions still require explicit confirmation.
missing: A transaction-preparation record that freezes the exact normalized mutation and evidence capsule
A relay-signed approval token bound to that digest, owner identity, expiry, and target session
Pendant rendering/input for a short redacted summary plus approve/reject buttons, including disconnected retry semantics
Worker-side compare-and-swap validation immediately before the external mutation

proposals.user_asks: When I say 'check Gmail, GitHub, or my calendar' from the pendant, capture it even if my Mac or browser is offline, then resume automatically when they reconnect and give me a sourced spoken result; never send, edit, or delete anything without my confirmation.
proposals.why_useful: The owner's recent attempts to read these accounts failed outright. This turns a transient disconnected bridge into a trustworthy asynchronous handoff: the pendant can accept the request now, the relay preserves it, and the authenticated browser on the Mac completes it later without moving credentials to the relay.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to acknowledge and clarify the short spoken request; use a cheaper background model for queued account reads, evidence reconciliation, and concise briefing generation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second offline; resume within 30 seconds of Mac/browser heartbeat; deliver a 1–3 sentence spoken result within 2 minutes of reconnection, with explicit queued/running/completed status.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per queued check depending on page count and extraction; dominant costs are authenticated page extraction and speech synthesis, not the short acknowledgement.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep cookies and page contents on the browser/Mac; relay stores only an encrypted intent, bounded account targets, and status. Redact secrets from receipts and logs. Reads are allowed by owner policy, but any send/edit/delete/purchase must become a separate confirmation checkpoint on the pendant and Mac. Expire unstarted intents and provide cancellation.
missing: A durable offline intent spool with idempotency keys, TTL, and reconnect replay
A device-visible queued/running/completed/failure state and cancellation action
A resumable authenticated-read workflow that can reattach to the intended browser session and return citations
A compact spoken-result/audio delivery path from completed background jobs to the pendant

proposals.user_asks: When I say “get this ready for me,” let the pendant capture the request, have the Mac and my open browser determine the relevant document, messages, calendar constraints, and files, then assemble a private ready-to-review packet on the Mac and announce exactly what is missing—without sending, submitting, or changing anything.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can inspect or act on individual surfaces, but it cannot turn an underspecified real-world request into one coherent, evidence-linked preparation packet spanning the owner's open browser, Mac files, and calendar. This would make the system useful at the moment of intent rather than requiring the owner to name every app and step.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to capture the short request and ask one clarification if genuinely necessary. Use a cheaper background model to gather, normalize, and assemble the packet; reserve the expensive tier for resolving conflicts or ambiguity.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; produce an initial packet in 1–3 minutes and continue gathering for up to 10 minutes, with a spoken progress update if the owner leaves the conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.15 per preparation, dominated by multi-page authenticated extraction, local file inspection, and optional audio rendering; most orchestration should use the background tier.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep private page contents and files on the Mac where possible. Every packet item needs source, timestamp, and access scope. Do not cross account boundaries or infer recipients. The output is draft-only: sending, submitting, deleting, purchasing, or editing requires a separate explicit approval. Expire packets and provide deletion.
missing: A cross-surface preparation workspace that can merge browser evidence, local files, and calendar facts into one provenance-linked packet
A goal-to-artifact contract distinguishing gather, draft, and mutate operations
Conflict and ambiguity reporting that stops at missing information instead of guessing
A Mac-side review surface with per-item source links, freshness, and a clear final approval boundary

proposals.user_asks: Make sure that happened, and tell me if it didn't.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action receipt reports what the executor attempted, not independent proof that the external state changed. This gives the owner a trustworthy spoken result: the Mac performs the reversible action, perception re-reads the target, and the relay keeps retrying or reports the exact failure instead of claiming success. It is specifically useful when the owner is away from the screen and wearing the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the pendant's short confirmation; use the cheaper local planner/vision and deterministic observation routes for execution and verification, with relay background retries.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial action acknowledgment under 1 second; verification within 3 seconds for app/file/browser state, with background retry up to 2 minutes for delayed effects.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one local Mac action plus one local observation, near-zero external API cost; model cost only when semantic GUI interpretation is needed. Background retries should use the cheaper tier.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may read private app/browser state and must remain bearer-authenticated. Never infer success from HTTP 200 alone. For send/delete/purchase actions, verification is evidence only and the existing confirmation gate remains mandatory. Surface before/after fields and a confidence level in the receipt.
missing: A verify_operation_step tool or equivalent authenticated observation endpoint that accepts the action's expected postcondition and returns observed evidence
A durable job state for pending verification/retry and an explicit distinction between attempted, verified, contradicted, and unknown
Pendant-safe spoken/error signaling when verification fails offline

proposals.user_asks: When I tell you to do something later, do it when I am actually at the right place and device—not merely at a clock time—and tell me if the opportunity passed.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can make decisions while wearing the pendant away from the Mac, but today the system cannot safely defer an action until the physical and digital context makes it appropriate. This would turn an intent into a context-sensitive handoff: the relay holds it, the pendant supplies presence/button confirmation, and the Mac/browser executes only when the owner is at the intended workstation or site.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to capture and clarify the intent. Use deterministic relay rules and a cheaper background model to evaluate context and select the execution surface; use the local Mac planner only at execution time.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture immediately; evaluate context on device events or a low-frequency heartbeat; execute within 5 seconds after the required context appears. Expire or ask again at the owner's stated deadline.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: mostly event matching and local observations; occasional cheap model call to resolve ambiguous context. No continuous realtime inference is needed.
proposals.security_concerns: A deferred intent may contain private account or location context. Encrypt it at rest, retain only until completion/expiry, and expose a visible pending-intent list. Require explicit confirmation for sends, purchases, deletion, or physical-risk actions even when context matches. Never use inferred location as sole authorization.
missing: A pendant-to-relay presence/context event stream (BLE proximity, button event, and connection state with timestamps)
A durable conditional-intent state machine with predicates, expiry, cancellation, and exactly-once handoff
Mac and browser observations normalized into context facts such as active user session, focused workspace, network, and authenticated tab
A cross-surface pending-intent UI and pendant indication that an intent is waiting or has expired

proposals.user_asks: “Start this on my Mac, and if it needs my approval while I’m away, ask me on the pendant; when I confirm, continue and tell me exactly what happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a job can be planned, blocked on the Mac dashboard, or leave receipts, but the owner cannot safely bridge a mid-job approval from the wearable. This gives one cross-surface transaction: the pendant starts it, the Mac/browser performs it, the relay holds durable state, and a spoken/button confirmation resumes only the exact pending step. The owner can walk away without losing the job or approving a different action than the one previewed.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only for the short spoken approval prompt and response; use the cheaper background/local planner for decomposition, evidence comparison, and final receipt narration.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under 1 s; approval prompt as soon as a gate is reached (target under 2 s); resume within 3 s of confirmation; background work may run for minutes while the owner is away.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn for the approval exchange plus local/background planner calls; <$0.03 typical excluding any browser/model work. Dominant cost is repeated evidence/context if the job is re-planned rather than resumed.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must send only a redacted preview and action hash, never page secrets. Confirmation is single-use, expires (for example 10 minutes), is bound to jobId/actionId/target tab and precondition hash, and cannot authorize a changed action. Require explicit spoken yes or pendant button gesture for irreversible writes/sends; record the confirmation and before/after evidence in the receipt. If the bridge disconnects, hold rather than execute.
missing: Durable cross-surface approval envelopes with action-hash binding and expiry
A relay-to-pendant notification/confirmation transport and a resume endpoint on the Mac executor
A true precondition gate (the current receipt/undo implementation observes pre-state but explicitly does not refuse or pause)
A unified job state machine that survives Mac/browser/relay disconnects and correlates the final receipt to the spoken prompt

proposals.user_asks: “If this task gets stuck while I’m away, follow my fallback rules: save a draft, notify me, or cancel—whichever I specified—and never leave a half-finished change.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently express what should happen when a Mac or browser action loses its tab, hits a dialog, times out, or waits for approval. Jobs simply fail or remain pending. A bounded contingency policy would let work continue safely without pretending that a timeout is success: preserve a draft or checkpoint, notify through the relay/pendant, and choose an explicitly authorized safe exit when the owner is unreachable.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background/local model to classify the failure against the owner’s predeclared policy and prepare the checkpoint; use realtime only to announce an urgent exception or request an override.
proposals.latency_budget: Classify and checkpoint within 2 seconds of a failure; notify the pendant promptly; policy execution within 5 seconds. No model call is needed for deterministic timeout, cancel, or save-draft branches.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per incident; most branches are deterministic. Cost is dominated by optional summarization of the saved checkpoint, not policy evaluation.
proposals.security_concerns: Policies must be explicit, scoped by app/site/action type, and deny-by-default. Never auto-send, purchase, delete, or publish. Store only a redacted checkpoint and action metadata in the relay; keep private page contents on the Mac/browser. Every fallback must produce a receipt and be reversible where possible.
missing: A declarative contingency-policy format with allowed fallback effects and expiry
Failure classification that distinguishes timeout, changed precondition, lost browser tab, permission block, and partial completion
Atomic checkpoint/fallback primitives spanning Mac files, browser drafts, relay notifications, and receipts
A policy simulator/preview so the owner can test what would happen before enabling it

proposals.user_asks: Prepare this on my Mac and logged-in browser, then ask me on the pendant to confirm; only after I press the button should you commit it, and tell me exactly what happened.
proposals.why_useful: This is the missing handoff between preparation and real-world commitment: the Mac/browser can gather and stage a transaction, while the worn pendant is the one surface that can ask the owner at the moment of action. It prevents accidental sends or purchases and still works when the owner is away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the brief spoken confirmation and disambiguation; use the cheaper background planner for gathering data, preparing fields, and validating the final diff.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation may take seconds to minutes; spoken confirmation should arrive within 1 second of the final diff becoming stable. The commit must expire if not confirmed within 2 minutes or if the browser/Mac state changes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.03 per transaction excluding model/provider fees; most cost is background browser extraction and Mac planning, not the short realtime confirmation.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not send mail, buy, delete, or submit without the physical confirmation token. Bind the token to a hashed final diff, target tab/session, owner identity, and short expiry; invalidate on any precondition change. Never transmit page secrets to the pendant or relay beyond a concise summary.
missing: A pendant-side confirmation primitive with local button event and visible/aural lease state
A verify_operation_step/verify_action_proof preflight API that can bind confirmation to the exact planned step
Browser bridge recovery and tab/session affinity while the transaction is staged
A durable staged-transaction record with expiry and cancellation

proposals.user_asks: After you do something for me, verify that the intended real-world result actually happened—not merely that the command returned success—and tell me if the outcome is confirmed, disproved, or still unknown.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action can produce a successful-looking receipt while Accessibility is ineffective, a browser bridge is offline, or a site has rejected the change. The owner needs truth about the result, not just whether an agent attempted a command. Verification could independently check that a sent message appears in Sent, a calendar event exists with the expected fields, a file has the expected hash, or a browser transaction shows its confirmation state.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to derive and run deterministic postconditions; use the realtime model only to explain an ambiguous outcome briefly to the owner.
proposals.latency_budget: Add up to 2–10 seconds for deterministic verification, with longer workflows allowed to remain pending. Never claim success until the postcondition passes or explicitly mark the outcome unknown.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: usually one or two lightweight reads per action; model cost is dominated by ambiguous reconciliation, which should be rare.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must be scoped to the target resource and avoid exposing private contents. For irreversible actions, require a predeclared postcondition and retain before/after evidence. If verification cannot safely inspect the target, report unknown rather than retrying.
missing: A typed postcondition language for Mac, browser, filesystem, and service outcomes
Independent read-back adapters that do not reuse the mutating command's success flag
Receipt fields for expected outcome, verification evidence, confidence, and unknown state
A retry policy that distinguishes failed execution from successful-but-unverified execution

proposals.user_asks: When you do something for me, don't just say it was sent—keep working until the result is independently verified, tell me what actually changed on my pendant, and recover or ask me if it did not complete.
proposals.why_useful: Today a queued Mac job, a browser command, and a real-world outcome are easy to confuse. This gives the owner a closed loop: judgement's intended outcome is handed to action, perception checks the postcondition using the appropriate surface, the relay keeps the job alive if the voice session ends, and the pendant reports success, failure, or a precise request for help. It is specifically useful for cross-surface tasks such as changing a logged-in webpage and then confirming the account state, or creating a Mac reminder and confirming it exists.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed intent with an expected postcondition and sensitivity/approval requirement
faculty-action selects Mac AppleScript, Mac job execution, or authenticated browser bridge based on reachability and records stable action IDs
faculty-perception independently re-reads the target (browser DOM/account page, Calendar/Reminders/Mail state, or a relay receipt) and compares it with the expected postcondition
relay persists the job and retry/timeout state after the live voice turn ends, then publishes a concise signed result event
pendant receives success/failure/pending status over the relay and uses spoken audio plus LED patterns; if unavailable, the Mac dashboard shows the same evidence and next step
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only for the owner's immediate acknowledgement and final short explanation; use a cheaper background planner/verifier for retries, polling, evidence comparison, and receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; reversible Mac actions usually complete within 10 seconds; allow up to 2 minutes for browser propagation and verification, with durable background continuation rather than blocking the conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 for a normal background plan/verification cycle, dominated by browser/page extraction and retries; realtime cost is limited to two short utterances. Storage is small typed receipts plus bounded evidence snippets.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not send page contents or credentials to the relay/model beyond the minimum redacted evidence. Never claim completion from an HTTP 200 or dispatch acknowledgement. Require explicit confirmation before irreversible external effects; redact secrets from receipts; expire evidence and provide cancellation. If verification disagrees, report 'unverified' rather than retrying a potentially duplicated action.
missing: A typed postcondition schema shared by judgement, action, and perception
A durable state machine distinguishing planned, dispatched, observed, verified, failed, and unverified
A verifier route/worker that can poll the same tab/session and attach source/timestamp evidence
Relay push to the pendant for job state changes and a retry budget with idempotency enforcement

proposals.user_asks: If I (or another device) change something while you are working on it, notice the conflict, show me both versions, and continue from the one I choose—never overwrite my newer change.
proposals.why_useful: The system currently treats an action as one agent's linear job. In real life the owner may edit the same calendar event, browser form, file, or message from an iPhone or another tab while the Mac is offline or retrying. Conflict-aware reconciliation prevents stale automation from erasing the owner's newer work and makes multi-device continuity trustworthy.
surfaces: faculty-action attaches a target version/fingerprint and pauses before any stale write
faculty-perception rereads the target across Mac APIs or authenticated browser tabs and identifies which fields changed, by whom if available, and when
faculty-judgement computes a field-level three-way diff against the original observation and asks the owner only about conflicting fields
relay keeps the suspended intent and conflict evidence durably after the voice session ends
Mac/browser perform only the selected non-conflicting merge; pendant speaks a compact conflict summary and accepts the owner's choice, while dashboard shows the full diff
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for field normalization and three-way diff; use realtime only to explain the conflict and capture the owner's selection.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect conflicts before the first write when possible; otherwise within one readback cycle (seconds). Suspend indefinitely without expiring into a silent overwrite.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per conflict for normalization; storage is a small original/current/proposed field diff. Realtime cost is limited to the short spoken choice.
proposals.security_concerns: Private field values must stay on the Mac/browser where possible; relay stores redacted diffs and hashes with short retention. Never infer ownership from timestamps alone. Require explicit choice for conflicting sensitive or irreversible fields; maintain an audit trail of the selected version.
missing: A versioned target-observation contract with field-level fingerprints and provenance
Three-way merge/conflict representation shared by Mac, browser, and relay
A durable suspended-job state and owner-choice endpoint that cannot be mistaken for cancellation
Per-field merge adapters for Calendar/Reminders/files and authenticated browser forms

proposals.user_asks: When I ask “did that happen?”, give me a proof-backed answer across my Mac, browser, relay, and pendant—what was only queued, what executed, what was delivered, and what cannot be verified—then offer the safest next step.
proposals.why_useful: Current receipts can say a Mac action succeeded even when browser is offline, Mac input is unavailable, or pendant playback was never acknowledged. The owner needs an honest answer about real-world effect, not an optimistic job result. This is uniquely cross-device: the Mac knows execution, the browser knows tab/session delivery, the relay knows accepted audio, and the pendant must provide physical delivery/playback evidence.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the owner's immediate spoken question; use a cheaper background verifier to join receipts and telemetry, and never infer delivery from missing evidence.
proposals.latency_budget: Spoken answer within 2 seconds from cached evidence; refresh Mac/browser/relay evidence asynchronously when stale and follow up when it changes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per query (mostly local D1/JSON joins); occasional background refresh dominates, not model tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private URLs, page text, file paths, and message metadata; retain hashes and minimal snippets, redact secrets, bind every fact to job/action/device identity, and require confirmation before any retry or compensating action.
missing: A shared execution-state schema with queued/accepted/executing/executed/delivered/played/failed/unknown states
Authoritative pendant delivery and playback acknowledgements with device clock/source timestamps
A cross-surface evidence joiner that distinguishes live evidence from historical records and expires stale claims
A retry/repair planner that treats unknown as unknown rather than success

proposals.user_asks: Before you carry out a consequential request, show me the likely cross-device state change; afterward, show me the actual state delta attributable to this action, including unexpected side effects, without relying on the app's claim that it succeeded.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can report that an action returned successfully, but it cannot establish what changed because of the action across files, browser sessions, messages, calendars, relay jobs, and pendant output. A causal before/after view would let the owner catch wrong-recipient, wrong-account, duplicate, and partial-completion failures even when ordinary receipts look green.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background/read-only observer for snapshots and diffing; reserve the realtime model for explaining the resulting delta to the owner.
proposals.latency_budget: Read-only preflight under 3 seconds for common actions; post-action delta within 5 seconds, with slower reconciliation for external services.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate storage and API cost for compact typed snapshots; model cost is limited to unusual diffs and owner-facing explanations.
proposals.security_concerns: Snapshots may contain private page text, files, recipients, and account state. Store minimized typed fields and hashes rather than raw content, encrypt retained deltas, enforce job ownership, and require confirmation whenever the predicted delta includes an irreversible or external side effect.
missing: A cross-surface causal snapshot format with field-level hashes and provenance
Read-only observers for external account state and pendant output state
Correlation IDs propagated from intent through every action and resulting event
A delta classifier that separates expected, incidental, and unexplained changes

proposals.user_asks: “Do this for me, and keep going until you can prove whether it actually happened.” The pendant should capture my intent, the judgement agent should turn it into a bounded action bundle, the Mac or private browser should execute it, and perception should independently verify the resulting state before telling me it is done.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action can be reported as successful even when the UI did nothing, or a browser command can sit pending while the owner assumes it ran. This gives the owner one honest answer: completed with evidence, safely queued with an expiry, or failed with the exact handoff that broke. It works across the pendant, always-on relay, Mac automation, and authenticated browser rather than being another Mac-only feature.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture/confirm the short owner utterance; use a cheaper background model for plan normalization, retries, and evidence reconciliation. No expensive model is needed for routine status polling.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge intent on the pendant in under 2 seconds; execute when a surface is available; verify within 10 seconds for Mac actions and up to 60 seconds for browser actions. If unavailable, persist a queued state rather than spinning or claiming completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly one short realtime turn plus 1–3 background calls per action; dominant cost is evidence reconciliation and any vision fallback, which should run only when typed/API verification fails.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay stores only a signed action bundle, expiry, sensitivity class, and receipts—not page contents by default. Irreversible effects require an explicit owner confirmation bound to the exact final parameters; stale approvals, changed targets, and browser-session changes invalidate the bundle. Never treat a relay_result or UI success alone as proof.
missing: A durable two-phase action-bundle state machine (prepared/approved/dispatched/verified/failed/expired) shared by relay and Mac
Typed precondition and postcondition probes for common Mac and browser actions
Independent verification route that can refuse the word done when no authoritative state change is observed
Pendant delivery acknowledgements once a real pendant is connected
Browser extension availability and owner-granted Accessibility/Screen Recording for vision-only actions

proposals.user_asks: “Before you send or change anything irreversible, make sure the final target still matches what I originally meant—even if the task crossed apps or took an hour.” The system should detect semantic drift in recipient, amount, account, attachment, destination, or scope across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, and interrupt only when the final operation differs materially from the owner’s captured intent.
proposals.why_useful: Today an approval can become stale or detached from the exact operation after a long workflow, a page refresh, a changed tab, or a handoff between agents. This protects the owner from sending to the wrong person, paying the wrong amount, modifying the wrong account, or approving a broader action than they requested without forcing confirmation for every harmless step.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize and compare structured intent fields. Use realtime only to ask the owner a short clarification when a material mismatch is detected; deterministic hashes and policy rules should handle ordinary matches.
proposals.latency_budget: No noticeable delay for reversible steps. For an irreversible step, compare the final parameter capsule in under 500 ms; if ambiguous, pause and ask one concise question rather than executing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually a small structured comparison with negligible model cost; one realtime turn only for genuine mismatches. The dominant cost is extracting final fields from an unstructured page when typed browser evidence is unavailable.
proposals.security_concerns: Store a minimized intent capsule rather than raw speech or page contents, with sensitivity labels and expiry. Bind confirmation to the exact normalized parameters, session/tab identity, and destination. A changed recipient, amount, or scope invalidates approval. Never silently broaden an action because an agent inferred more context.
missing: A canonical intent capsule schema shared by judgement, action, Mac, and browser
Field-level semantic diffing with materiality policies by action type
A mandatory pre-commit hook that can pause every executor, including AppleScript and browser commands
Final-state extraction for recipients, amounts, attachments, and scopes from each supported app
A concise pendant/dashboard clarification and resume protocol

proposals.user_asks: If something I asked you to do partly fails, recover it safely: show me what actually changed, undo the reversible parts when possible, and continue only after asking about the one blocked step.
proposals.why_useful: Today a Mac/browser workflow can leave the owner unsure whether it stopped before or after a mutation. This gives the action layer a bounded recovery behavior: inspect receipts and live state, compensate reversible changes, preserve irreversible changes, and present a precise continuation request. It requires the action node, browser private-session node, Mac bridge, and always-awake relay together.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for receipt classification, state diffing, and compensation planning; reserve realtime for the owner's short approval/continuation exchange.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial recovery report in 5–15 seconds after failure; compensation can run asynchronously with relay_job_status updates.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per recovery, dominated by model calls over receipts and state diffs; most steps are deterministic.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and local action receipts remain on the authenticated Mac/relay path. Never compensate sends, purchases, deletions, or other irreversible actions automatically; require explicit approval and retain before/after evidence.
missing: A transaction/compensation record that links each step to its precondition, observed before-state, after-state, reversibility class, and proof.
A deterministic state-diff and compensation executor for Mac and browser steps, with an explicit irreversible-step boundary.
A failure-injection test suite covering bridge loss, stale tabs, duplicate requests, and a mutation that succeeds but returns an error.

proposals.user_asks: Give me an emergency stop for anything you are doing on my Mac or in my browser: when I press and hold the pendant button, stop new actions immediately, cancel queued work, and tell me whether anything was already changed.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently start work through the voice surface but cannot physically interrupt it when their attention is elsewhere or a workflow behaves unexpectedly. A local, tactile stop path is useful precisely when speech, the browser, or the Mac is busy or unresponsive. This is a cross-surface capability: the pendant detects the hold offline, the relay distributes a signed revocation, the Mac and browser executors enforce it between steps, and the relay reports the last proven state.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for the stop itself. Use deterministic firmware and relay logic; use a cheaper background model only to summarize the resulting receipts after execution has halted.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant-local stop indication within 100 ms; relay propagation target under 1 second; already-running indivisible OS/browser calls may complete, but no subsequent step may begin after revocation is observed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per stop, dominated by receipt summarization; negligible device power and storage overhead.
proposals.security_concerns: A false press could cancel useful work, so require a deliberate hold and local vibration/LED confirmation. Revocation must be authenticated, monotonic, and fail closed for queued actions. It must not claim that an in-flight irreversible operation was undone; report unknown or completed with evidence.
missing: A pendant firmware emergency-stop event and local acknowledgment path.
A relay-wide revocation sequence checked by every Mac and browser executor before each step.
Cancellation semantics for queued and in-flight jobs, including a final last-observed-step receipt.
A durable action lease/heartbeat so stale workers cannot continue after connectivity returns.

proposals.user_asks: After I approve an action, carry it out across my devices and tell me whether it actually happened—not merely that a command was sent. If a device goes offline, keep the action safe, resume when it returns, and show me the evidence or the exact point where it stopped.
proposals.why_useful: Today receipts can confirm that the Mac agent accepted work, while the browser is offline and the pendant is absent; neither proves the external world changed. This gives the owner a trustworthy boundary between requested, attempted, and externally verified, with safe recovery rather than duplicate clicks or silent failure.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the owner's approval and report urgent state; use a cheaper background worker for retries, polling, reconciliation, and evidence summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge approval in under 1 second; reversible Mac actions can complete in seconds. Offline recovery may wait for the bridge/browser heartbeat, with bounded retries and a spoken/status update rather than holding the conversation open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per action lifecycle when verification is mostly typed receipts/API reads; occasional model-based reconciliation costs more. Dominant costs are browser/Mac round trips and any screenshot or long page extraction, not the durable state machine.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser pages and Mac state leave their devices only as minimum evidence (URL/title, target identifiers, before/after hashes, timestamps), never raw page contents by default. Irreversible sends/purchases/deletions require a fresh explicit confirmation immediately before execution. Leases, idempotency keys, expiry, cancellation, and duplicate suppression are mandatory; if proof is unavailable, report unknown rather than claiming success.
missing: A durable cross-surface action transaction record with states requested/approved/leased/attempted/verified/unknown/failed
Step-level preconditions and postconditions plus typed proof adapters for AppleScript/Mac APIs and authenticated browser tabs
An offline-safe retry/resume worker keyed by idempotency and tab/session affinity
A compact owner-facing evidence receipt and pendant notification path; no pendant is currently registered
Owner-configurable expiry and confirmation policy for actions that become stale

proposals.user_asks: Give you a bounded standing permission for a kind of task—such as scheduling meetings within my working hours or reordering a specific item below a price cap—and have you carry out matching actions across my Mac and logged-in browser without asking me every time, while stopping and asking when any limit, ambiguity, or sensitive field is encountered.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must either approve every individual mutation or grant broad, opaque control. A constrained authority lets routine work happen while preserving their intent: the mind can decide and act within explicit limits, but cannot silently widen scope or improvise past a boundary.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only when obtaining or changing the owner's authority policy. Compile policies and evaluate routine actions with a cheaper background model plus deterministic checks; escalate ambiguous matches to realtime or the owner.
proposals.latency_budget: Policy evaluation should be sub-100 ms locally at the relay/Mac boundary. Routine approved actions can complete asynchronously within seconds; boundary crossings should interrupt promptly and request confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per routine action because matching, caps, time windows, and field classifications are deterministic. Model cost is reserved for ambiguous task-to-policy matching and concise exception explanations.
proposals.security_concerns: Permissions must be least-privilege, explicit, revocable, expiring, and scoped by app/site/account, action type, amount, time window, and sensitive-field class. Never infer permission from conversational tone. Show an action preview when a policy is first used; require confirmation for sends, purchases, deletions, identity/security changes, or any over-cap action. Keep credentials on the Mac/browser and record policy version plus evidence, not secrets or raw private-page contents.
missing: A typed authority-policy schema and compiler shared by judgement and action
A deterministic preflight evaluator that can inspect planned Mac/browser steps and reject out-of-scope mutations before dispatch
Per-policy leases, quotas, expiry, revocation, and an owner-visible audit/review surface
Cross-surface identity/account binding so a rule cannot accidentally apply to the wrong browser session or Mac account
A safe exception path that pauses at the exact violating step and asks for one-time approval without broadening the standing rule

proposals.user_asks: “Do this wherever it can actually be done, and tell me whether it really happened.” For example: send the prepared message, update the appointment, or submit the form—even if I leave the pendant conversation.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an action but can mistake a queued/no-op UI action for success. This capability makes action faculty a reliable hand: choose the reachable surface, execute only where the preflight says it is viable, independently read back the postcondition, and leave a durable receipt or an honest blocked/queued result. It is specifically cross-device: the pendant carries the intent and status back to the owner, the relay persists work while the Mac sleeps, the Mac uses granted AppleScript where possible, and the browser bridge handles private sessions when online.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to capture the short intent and speak status. Use a cheaper background planner/worker for multi-step execution, retries, evidence comparison, and receipt generation.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight and first spoken status under 2 seconds; reversible local actions usually 3–10 seconds; long work continues in the durable queue and reports completion or blockage later. Never say done until a postcondition read-back succeeds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per invocation: mostly Mac/relay/browser I/O and a few background planner turns. Cost is dominated by retries and page extraction, not the realtime conversation; cache preflight and evidence fingerprints to avoid resending context.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and action evidence stay on the Mac/browser session unless explicitly routed to the relay. Never expose credentials. Destructive or externally visible steps need the existing owner policy/confirmation; a failed preflight must not be silently retried through a different account. Receipts should record target, before/after evidence, timestamp, and why a fallback was or was not used.
missing: A durable cross-surface execution worker with jobId, retry/resume, and result stream (the browser router exists but its durable runner is still missing)
A mandatory execution preflight/postcondition contract that distinguishes queued, blocked, no-op, and verified-done
A verification operation that can read back the target without repeating the write
Browser extension online/pending-command drain
Owner-granted Accessibility and Screen Recording if a task truly requires GUI/computer vision; AppleScript fallback must remain usable without them

proposals.user_asks: “If part of this multi-step task fails, finish it safely or tell me exactly what is left—not just that the job failed.” For example, reschedule an appointment across my calendar and a logged-in portal, then notify the right person without duplicating or losing any step.
proposals.why_useful: The current system can receipt individual Mac actions, but the owner cannot safely ask for a consequential workflow spanning Calendar/Mail, a private browser account, and the relay: one side effect may succeed while the next times out, leaving an ambiguous real-world state. A cross-surface saga would checkpoint each effect, detect partial completion, apply safe compensations where possible, and produce a concise reconciliation listing confirmed changes, unperformed steps, and the single next action. This is not a generic durable job or undo button; it handles inconsistent external systems where rollback may be impossible.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only captures intent and reads the short checkpoint aloud. A cheaper background worker executes the saga, compares evidence, retries idempotently, and prepares reconciliation; use the expensive model only when evidence conflicts or the recovery plan is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Speak an initial checkpoint within 2 seconds. Each step can run asynchronously; after every side effect, persist evidence before advancing. On interruption, resume from the last confirmed checkpoint rather than replaying earlier writes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate background cost: mostly existing Mac/browser calls and receipts, with one cheap reconciliation pass. The dominant cost is conflict resolution when an external site has changed, not routine execution.
proposals.security_concerns: Private account data remains on its owning browser session unless the owner explicitly permits relay processing. Never infer success from a click response; require read-back evidence. Compensating actions (cancellation, deletion, sending a correction) must be classified as new externally visible effects and follow the owner’s confirmation policy. Preserve an immutable audit trail without storing credentials or full sensitive page contents.
missing: A cross-surface saga state machine with step dependencies, idempotency keys, durable checkpoints, and explicit partial-success states
A typed evidence/reconciliation record that can compare Mac receipts, Calendar/Mail reads, and browser page read-backs
Compensation adapters for safe local effects plus a recovery planner that stops when compensation would itself be risky
A durable browser job runner/result stream for private authenticated steps

proposals.user_asks: “Is my pendant audio path healthy? If not, diagnose it, switch to the safest working mode, and leave me a short report.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has no way to know whether 24 kHz playback is actually reaching the earbud/bridge. A closed-loop test would distinguish codec, timing, I2S wiring, radio loss, and battery problems, then recover without pretending the path works. It requires the worn endpoint, ESP32 bridge, Mac harness, and always-awake relay together.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic firmware/bridge DSP and threshold rules for diagnosis; use a cheap background model only to turn telemetry into a human report. Reserve realtime for the owner's spoken question.
proposals.latency_budget: 15–30 seconds for a full test; under 2 seconds to select a local fallback after a failed frame or bridge health event.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for thresholded telemetry; roughly $0.01–$0.05 only when a background model summarizes an anomalous run. Storage is a small per-run JSON receipt plus optional short waveform.
proposals.security_concerns: The test may emit an audible tone, so require a low-volume mode and owner confirmation if outside a quiet window. Send only derived metrics by default (packet loss, clock drift, underruns, RMS/SNR); retain raw audio only for an explicitly enabled diagnostic run. Any mode switch must be nonce-bound and receipt-backed.
missing: A pendant diagnostic command/event for loopback tone and microphone capture
ESP32 bridge-side I2S counters and clock-drift measurement
A relay schema for signed audio health receipts and fallback state
Mac harness job that runs the test and collects bridge/pendant telemetry
A verified postcondition tool for confirming the selected mode actually took effect

proposals.user_asks: “Make my pendant audio sound right wherever I am: run a quiet calibration, compensate for the bridge and headphones, and keep the correction until the hardware changes.”
proposals.why_useful: The current system can render 24 kHz PCM but cannot account for the ESP32 bridge’s 31,250→44,100 Hz resampling, SBC-only Bluetooth path, headphone latency, or per-device gain. The owner should hear speech that is intelligible and correctly timed without manually tuning an experimental chain. This is a new calibration-and-compensation capability, not merely a health check or delivery receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic swept-tone/MLS measurement, fixed-point DSP, and a small calibration profile; use a background model only to explain the result in one short spoken sentence. No realtime model is needed for the measurement.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial calibration 20–45 seconds while the owner explicitly invokes it; applying a stored profile adds under 1 ms of processing and no conversational latency.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; a few small telemetry records per calibration and at most a bounded diagnostic waveform. Computation runs on the ESP32/Mac, not an API.
proposals.security_concerns: Calibration emits sound and may expose nearby audio if microphone loopback is used. Require an explicit start, cap volume, offer a speaker-only mode, and upload derived impulse-response/gain metrics rather than recordings. Bind the profile to authenticated pendant, bridge, and headphone identities; never apply a profile to an unknown device automatically.
missing: A calibration command spanning pendant playback, ESP32 resampling, and headphone route
Bridge-side timestamped I2S capture and Bluetooth latency/gain telemetry
A compact profile format and authenticated storage keyed by hardware identities
A verified apply-and-postcondition acknowledgement from the pendant/bridge
A user-visible way to select or discard profiles when headphones change

proposals.user_asks: When you have prepared something that needs my approval, say what will happen, then let me approve it with one deliberate long press on the pendant; execute it on my Mac or in my logged-in browser and tell me the result, even if I walk away.
proposals.why_useful: Today approval is stranded on a dashboard while the pendant can only start/end conversation. This creates a physical, auditable handoff: judgement prepares a bounded action, the relay presents a short spoken preview, the pendant's sole button confirms the exact nonce, and faculty-action executes through the appropriate Mac/browser hand. No Accessibility is required for AppleScript/declarative actions; browser-private work remains on Safari. If the link drops, the action expires rather than running later.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the short spoken preview and confirmation exchange; background/local planner for preparing multi-step plans and summarizing receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview under 2 seconds; confirmation-to-execution acknowledgement under 3 seconds when Mac is online. Expire unconfirmed leases after 60 seconds; do not queue an approval across a disconnect.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per approval depending on preview length/model; most execution and receipt work is local. Small relay storage for nonce, plan hash, and outcome.
proposals.security_concerns: Never transmit secrets in the spoken preview. Bind approval to an immutable plan hash, target surface, account/session, and short-lived nonce; reject stale/replayed presses and any plan mutation. Require a second confirmation in the dashboard for destructive actions (send mail, delete, purchase), consistent with owner policy. Store only hashes and redacted receipts.
missing: pendant firmware button event uplink and LED confirmation state
short-lived approval lease/nonce endpoint shared by relay, Mac, and browser
device-to-relay approval acknowledgement (ideally authenticated)
executor precondition gate that refuses if the approved plan changed
audio playback completion/acceptance signal

proposals.user_asks: Make sure this actually happened: after you perform an action on my Mac or in a logged-in browser, independently verify the real-world postcondition and keep working until it is true or tell me exactly what prevented it.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can execute an action and produce a receipt, but a receipt only says what the executor attempted or observed. The owner needs closure: for example, not merely 'calendar event created,' but confirmation that it appears in the authoritative calendar; not merely 'form submitted,' but a confirmation number or changed account state. A separate perception pass prevents the acting agent from certifying its own mistake and lets the relay deliver a concise success/failure outcome to the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background/local models for polling and comparing structured postconditions; realtime only for the owner's final spoken result or an urgent failure.
proposals.latency_budget: Reversible local actions: verify within 5 seconds. Browser/account changes: retry with bounded backoff for up to 10 minutes, then deliver a failure explanation and the last evidence. Never keep retrying an irreversible action; only verify or use an explicitly approved compensating action.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per workflow because verification uses structured API/DOM evidence and local comparison; cost is dominated by any authenticated browser reads and optional realtime notification.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must be read-only by default and scoped to the same account/session and target named in the plan. Store redacted evidence (URL, timestamp, field names, hashes, confirmation IDs where safe), not page secrets. Do not treat a visually similar page or stale cache as proof. For destructive or financial actions, require an independent authoritative confirmation and preserve the uncertainty if it cannot be obtained.
missing: first-class postcondition schema in plans (target, predicate, authority, freshness window)
independent verifier route that can read Mac APIs or authenticated browser state without re-performing the action
retry/timeout state machine distinguishing verify, retry-safe action, and compensation
evidence bundle linking pre-state, action receipt, post-state, and verifier identity
pendant notification event for verified, blocked, and timed-out outcomes

proposals.user_asks: “Do the approved plan even if I leave the conversation: carry it out across my Mac and logged-in browser, but only while the facts it depends on are still true; stop safely on any mismatch and tell me exactly what happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide a multi-surface action, but execution is brittle when the voice session ends or a page changes. This gives the owner dependable follow-through without silently acting on stale information: the Mac can perform local work, the browser can use private sessions, the relay can keep the job alive, and the pendant can report completion or a blocked step.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the approval and concise status; use a cheaper background model for plan compilation, precondition re-checks, retries, and final receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge approval in under 1 second; begin execution within 5 seconds; individual checks under 3 seconds; long jobs continue asynchronously and may take minutes. A stale or ambiguous precondition must stop rather than wait indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per job depending on number of browser pages and retries; most cost is background extraction and final summarization, not the short voice acknowledgement.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser content and local Mac state leave their respective devices only to the authenticated relay/context projection. Never send or submit irreversible changes without a fresh explicit approval token. Bind each step to tab/session, URL, expected evidence hash, and an expiry; redact secrets from receipts; support cancellation and idempotent retry.
missing: A durable cross-surface job schema carrying preconditions, approval token, deadline, and compensation/cancellation state
A runner that can re-check evidence before every step and stop on mismatch
A single pendant/voice status and completion channel for jobs after the original conversation ends
Browser-online availability and owner-granted Accessibility/Screen Recording for GUI-only steps; AppleScript paths should remain the fallback

proposals.user_asks: Handle this private webpage for me: gather the details, prepare the reversible changes, and finish only after I approve the exact result.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant can capture the owner's intent while away from the Mac; the relay can keep the job alive; the browser can read the logged-in page; and the Mac can use granted AppleScript APIs to carry out non-GUI work. The owner gets one understandable preview, a physical approval point, and a durable spoken receipt instead of an untraceable click or a lost job.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the pendant conversation and final short confirmation; use a cheaper background planner for extraction, reconciliation, and queued execution. Use deterministic AppleScript/typed browser actions wherever possible rather than vision.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview within 5–10 seconds when Mac and browser are online; commit within 3 seconds after the owner's button/voice approval. If either surface drops, persist the lease and report queued/stalled status rather than guessing success.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per transaction depending on page extraction and retries; realtime speech dominates interactive cost, while deterministic actions and background planning are cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and proposed mutations leave the browser/Mac only to the authenticated relay path. Never submit mail, purchases, deletion, or other irreversible changes without an explicit final approval. Bind every step to sessionId/tabId, URL, freshness timestamp, and before-value evidence; expire the approval lease on navigation, timeout, or changed content. Accessibility-free GUI actions must be rejected, not reported as success.
missing: browser heartbeat and pending-command reconciliation so the current 10 queued commands cannot be replayed blindly
a real precondition/commit gate in the Mac executor (the existing receipt/undo implementation records effects but does not refuse stale actions)
fresh browser inspection/content provenance (current /browser/inspections is empty)
pendant approval and cancellation event delivery plus a durable cross-surface transaction state machine

proposals.user_asks: When I say ‘send this to Alex’ or ‘book it with Sam,’ resolve the right person across my Mac contacts, calendar, mail, and logged-in sites, tell me the candidates and why, and let me choose by pressing the pendant button before you prepare the action.
proposals.why_useful: Names are ambiguous across personal and work accounts. Today the system can act through separate Mac and browser surfaces, but it cannot safely reconcile identities across them or explain the match before an action is prepared. This would prevent sending private material to the wrong Alex, booking the wrong Sam, or silently mixing accounts while keeping the owner's approval small and physical.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background resolver for deterministic contact/account matching and evidence collection; reserve the realtime tier for the short spoken candidate list and the owner's selection. Use exact identifiers and scripts for lookup, not free-form model guesses.
proposals.latency_budget: Return candidate identities and confidence in 3–8 seconds while the relevant Mac/browser surfaces are online. If one source is unavailable, say which source was omitted and do not collapse to a single guess.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per resolution; most cost is a small model call to normalize names and summarize evidence, with lookups handled deterministically.
proposals.security_concerns: Contact names, email addresses, phone numbers, and account context are sensitive. Keep raw records on the Mac where possible; send only masked candidates and provenance to the relay. Never infer authorization from a name match. Require explicit pendant selection before preparing a send, booking, purchase, or other external action, and require the existing separate confirmation for irreversible submission.
missing: a typed cross-surface identity record linking contact/account identifiers with source, freshness, and confidence
Mac read adapters for Contacts, Mail, Calendar, and account profiles that return masked candidates and stable IDs
browser extraction adapters that expose logged-in account identity without leaking page contents
a pendant candidate-selection event carrying the chosen stable ID, not merely spoken text
dashboard explanation of why each candidate matched and which sources were unavailable

proposals.user_asks: Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, and only tell me it worked when an independent check proves the intended change actually happened; if anything is unreachable or only partly done, say exactly what remains.
proposals.why_useful: Today an executor receipt can say success even when Accessibility/input reachability is false. This gives the owner an honest completion answer: the Mac or browser performs the reversible steps, a separate perception pass checks the resulting app/page state, and the relay/pendant reports verified, unverified, blocked, partial, or rolled-back rather than claiming success. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant can remain the request/status channel while the relay keeps the lease alive, the Mac acts, the browser bridge reaches private tabs, and faculty-perception supplies independent proof.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background planner for decomposition and a cheap verifier for stable UI/state predicates; reserve realtime for the owner's short spoken request and the final one-sentence status. Escalate to the expensive model only when the proof is contradictory or ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge intent immediately; first action within 2 seconds; verification within 5 seconds per step. Long browser waits become resumable background jobs, with pendant status updates and a final spoken result when the lease finishes or expires.
proposals.cost_estimate: About 2–4 inexpensive model calls per multi-step job (plan, per-batch verification, reconciliation); dominant cost is screenshots/page text and repeated context, not execution. Keep evidence as hashes/snippets and send only the failing step to the expensive tier.
proposals.security_concerns: Proof must not expose private page content beyond the minimum cited snippet/hash. Never treat an executor receipt as proof. Destructive sends, deletes, purchases, or external submissions still require the owner's existing confirmation policy; verification can report them but cannot authorize them. Expired leases must stop retries and mark the job incomplete.
missing: A shared action-outcome schema consumed by faculty-action, relay, Mac, browser, and perception
Independent postcondition probes for typed Mac actions and browser commands
Lease/heartbeat expiry that stops retries and emits a pendant-visible incomplete state
A durable evidence record linking intent, actionId, before state, postcondition, and proof timestamp

proposals.user_asks: Start this on the pendant, let my Mac and private browser carry it out while I move around, and bring the exact unfinished step back to me when I reconnect—without restarting anything or guessing what already happened.
proposals.why_useful: Today a disconnected wearable, sleeping Mac, or lost browser session turns a partially completed task into an ambiguous retry. The owner should be able to walk away and return to a truthful, resumable handoff: the relay preserves a compact continuation token, the Mac/browser checkpoint the last proven state, and the pendant announces exactly where work stopped when it comes back in range.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic state-machine code and a small background model for continuation selection; use realtime only when the pendant reconnects and needs a concise spoken/tactile status. Escalate only if the saved checkpoint conflicts with observed state.
proposals.latency_budget: Instant local acknowledgment; reconnect status within 2 seconds; resume or pause decision within 10 seconds after both relay and Mac are reachable. No blocking voice turn while the task runs.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: one compact continuation record per active task and one inexpensive reconciliation call on reconnect. Dominant cost is occasional browser/Mac observation, not model generation.
proposals.security_concerns: Bind continuation tokens to the owner's authenticated pendant session and task scope; expire them and require revalidation after a long absence. Never replay external submissions from a stale checkpoint. Private browser evidence remains on the authenticated bridge, with only a digest and next-step summary sent to the relay.
missing: A signed, durable continuation-token protocol spanning pendant, relay, Mac agent, and browser session
