Checkpoint semantics that distinguish proven completion from attempted execution for every step
Reconnect reconciliation that compares the checkpoint against fresh Mac/browser observations before resuming
A pendant-visible unresolved-state UI for paused, expired, and conflict outcomes

proposals.user_asks: “Finish this across my browser and Mac, even if I leave: use the logged-in page, save the result in my workspace, and tell me only when each step is proven complete.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser action, Mac action, and relay job can each exist, but there is no single transaction tying them together. The owner can be told that a click or type returned success even when the Mac is unreachable, and a restart can cause a duplicate. This would make delegated work trustworthy: one stable task ID, explicit handoffs between private Safari and Mac storage, postcondition evidence for every step, resume after disconnects, and a spoken completion receipt that distinguishes completed, waiting for approval, and unverified.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the request and speak the final short receipt; use a cheaper background planner for decomposition, retries, evidence comparison, and reconciliation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; private-page reads and Mac work may run asynchronously. Speak only after postconditions are observed or clearly report blocked/unverified, with retry backoff rather than busy polling.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per multi-step task depending on evidence extraction and retries; dominant costs are model calls for reconciliation and any public Browser Run minutes, not the relay bookkeeping.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, extracted text, and workspace paths leave the Mac only as encrypted task evidence; redact secrets and cap evidence retention. Never cross an irreversible checkpoint (send, purchase, delete, submit) without the owner's existing confirmation policy. A proof packet must include source URL/path, timestamp, and before/after hash so a false success is visible.
missing: A durable cross-surface transaction coordinator joining browser session steps and Mac job steps under one task ID
The still-missing durable browser job runner and voice-path wiring noted in chg-16bc5dee
Read-and-enforce preconditions and postconditions (current receipt code records observations but does not gate execution, as noted in chg-5fc73ce3)
Lease/heartbeat and exactly-once action claims across relay, Safari bridge, and Mac reconnects
A typed verification/proof packet and dashboard/pendant status stream

proposals.user_asks: “Before you send, buy, delete, or submit anything, give me a compact receipt on the pendant and let me approve it there only if my Mac shows the same receipt; then carry out exactly that approved change and tell me what the other device proves afterward.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has confirmation as a policy, but not a tamper-evident, two-device approval ceremony. A spoken confirmation can be based on stale browser content, and a Mac prompt alone is not useful when the owner is away from the keyboard. This gives the owner a clear, remote approval boundary: the pendant presents the intended irreversible effect, the Mac displays the matching transaction digest, approval is bound to that exact digest and expires, and execution cannot silently substitute a changed recipient, amount, file, or form value. The final response includes independent post-action evidence rather than a generic success message.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to explain the pending receipt and collect the short approval phrase; use a cheaper deterministic service for digest creation, expiry, signature checks, and post-action comparison.
proposals.latency_budget: Receipt should reach the pendant in under 2 seconds after a plan pauses. Approval should be accepted for a short window (for example 2 minutes); execution and proof may complete asynchronously, with one concise spoken result.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.005 per approval ceremony; cryptographic signing and digest comparison are local/relay bookkeeping. Model cost is limited to summarizing unusually complex effects.
proposals.security_concerns: The digest must cover the normalized action, recipient/URL/path, amount or payload, and precondition evidence; approvals must be one-time, short-lived, replay-resistant, and scoped to the owner’s paired pendant. Do not speak secrets aloud. If Mac and pendant summaries differ, expire the approval and stop. Require a second explicit confirmation for especially high-risk categories if the owner configures one.
missing: A signed action-digest format shared by relay, Mac executor, and browser bridge
A pendant-side approval and cancellation protocol that works without keyboard focus
A Mac display/receipt channel that can be compared to the pendant’s digest
Atomic binding of approval to exactly one executor step, with expiry and replay protection
Independent postcondition proof after execution, including browser DOM/source evidence or Mac file/application evidence

proposals.user_asks: “Put me back exactly where I left off, and let me continue from the pendant.” The system should preserve a live handoff capsule: what I was trying to do, the relevant Mac app/document, authenticated browser tabs and page locations, selected text or draft state, and the next safe action. If the link drops, I can press the pendant button later and hear a concise resume brief; the Mac and browser restore only the reversible context, then wait for my confirmation before changing anything.
proposals.why_useful: Today the pendant, relay, Mac, and private browser are separate sessions. After walking away or losing connectivity, the owner must reconstruct context manually and risks acting on stale tabs or drafts. This gives them continuity across the one place they speak and the machines that hold their work, without silently submitting anything.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to compress and refresh the handoff capsule; use the realtime tier only to hear the button-triggered resume brief; use the local Mac planner for deterministic restoration and a small model only when the capsule is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture should complete in under 2 seconds while online. Resume speech should begin within 1 second of a pendant button press; restoring reversible context may take 3–10 seconds and must report partial availability rather than blocking.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.02 per capture/resume depending on capsule compression and whether page text is summarized; storage and browser/Mac round trips dominate, not realtime inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules can contain private URLs, page text, drafts, and document names. Encrypt at rest and in transit, bind each capsule to the paired device, redact secrets and passwords, give every capsule a TTL and delete control, and never restore or mutate a private page without an explicit owner confirmation. A stale capsule must be visibly labeled with age and source.
missing: A versioned handoff-capsule schema with provenance, sensitivity labels, TTL, and stale-state detection
A pendant-local offline queue and a reliable sync/replay protocol when the relay reconnects
Mac APIs to snapshot and restore reversible app/document context without Accessibility or Screen Recording
Browser bridge support for authenticated tab snapshots and reattachment, currently unavailable while home-chrome is offline
A user-facing resume/expiry/forget control and a compact spoken status path

POST /sessions and GET /sessions/:sessionId for durable conversation/session state

GET/POST /browser/sessions and the browser command/result routes for tab affinity
POST /pipeline/events and GET /briefing/latest for pendant-visible status and spoken handoff
GET /context-graph for provenance-linked entities and relations

proposals.user_asks: Prepare this action across my browser and Mac, show me exactly what will happen, and when I say “approve” execute it once—or tell me precisely why it was blocked.
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can decide and action surfaces can execute, but there is no single handoff that binds the owner's approval to the exact evidence and action. This gives the owner a trustworthy cross-surface transaction: reversible preparation can proceed, while a stale page, changed target, offline bridge, or replayed approval cannot cause an unintended irreversible effect.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture/confirm the short approval phrase; use the cheaper background planner for preparation, evidence collection, and receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation may take seconds and continue as a durable job; approval response should be acknowledged in under 500 ms, with execution status streamed and a final spoken receipt in under 5 s when surfaces are online.
proposals.cost_estimate: One background planning call plus low-cost extraction/action calls; realtime cost only for the approval turn. Dominant cost is authenticated page extraction and any vision fallback, not the approval check.
proposals.security_concerns: Approval must be single-use and cryptographically/logically bound to handoffId, canonical action hash, target tab/session, and evidence freshness window. Never send secrets to the relay unnecessarily. Destructive sends, deletes, purchases, or external submissions require explicit approval; clarification is not approval. If any precondition changes, return BLOCKED with no partial irreversible effect, retain an audit receipt, and offer undo for reversible steps.
missing: A durable handoff record/state machine (PREPARED, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVED, EXECUTING, COMPLETED, BLOCKED, EXPIRED) shared by relay, Mac, and browser
An atomic preflight that revalidates target identity and evidence immediately before the irreversible step
A one-shot approval token/action hash verifier and idempotency key across browser and Mac queues
Pendant-side concise approval/blocked speech and a dashboard showing evidence, exact mutations, and receipt/undo

proposals.user_asks: “Resume the thing that got interrupted.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a queued task can end in a browser timeout, an offline pendant, or a Mac approval gate, and the owner has to reconstruct what happened. This capability would inspect the durable job and receipts, distinguish completed from untouched steps, re-check current preconditions on the correct surface, continue only safe/reversible work, and give a concise spoken receipt. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant supplies the terse resume intent, relay owns durable state, Mac executes, and browser sessions provide authenticated continuity.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to resolve the short resume reference and speak the acknowledgment; use a cheaper background/local planner to reconcile receipts, preconditions, and retry steps. Escalate to realtime only for ambiguity or approval.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; reconcile within 2 seconds; retries may continue as a durable job and report completion later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per invocation; dominant costs are background planner tokens and any browser/page extraction, not the short realtime turn.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser URLs/content and Mac receipts leave the device only through the authenticated relay. Never retry irreversible steps automatically; require confirmation for send/delete/purchase. Persist only job IDs, step hashes, and outcome summaries, with short retention for page evidence.
missing: A first-class resume/retry route that understands step-level receipts and safe retry policy
Precondition verification and idempotency metadata per action
A durable user-facing pending/approval state that the pendant can query when the Mac or browser is offline

proposals.user_asks: “Stop everything now.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner needs a physical, immediate escape hatch when the Mac or browser is acting unexpectedly—without finding the dashboard or speaking a longer explanation. A deliberate pendant gesture would revoke the active execution lease across the relay, Mac, and browser, cancel queued reversible work, and prevent an approval-gated step from being released. It is a new cross-surface emergency control, not merely an activity log or ordinary undo.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model is needed: firmware and relay perform the stop deterministically. Use a cheap background model only to summarize what was halted after the fact; realtime speaks a brief acknowledgment if the link is live.
proposals.latency_budget: Local haptic/LED acknowledgment in under 100 ms; relay cancellation propagation under 500 ms when connected; persist the stop locally and apply it when connectivity returns.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per invocation, under $0.001 for event storage and optional summary. Hardware cost is zero if the existing button/LED can support a guarded long press.
proposals.security_concerns: A false trigger could interrupt useful work, so require a deliberate 1.5–2 second hold plus distinct vibration/LED confirmation. Cancellation must fail closed: once stopped, no queued irreversible action may run until a new explicit intent. Store only job ID, step ID, and cancellation reason; never speak private page contents.
missing: Pendant firmware gesture and durable local stop latch that survives link loss
Relay-wide revocable execution leases understood by Mac and browser workers
Cancellation propagation and acknowledgement in the Mac/browser action protocols
Dashboard view showing exactly which steps stopped, completed, or remain untouched

proposals.user_asks: Do this and only tell me it's done once you have independently verified the result—for example, that the file contains the requested text, the reminder exists, or the browser change is visible after reload. If it failed or is only queued, tell me that instead.
proposals.why_useful: Today action receipts prove that an executor accepted and returned an action, not that the outside-world postcondition is true. This gives the owner an honest distinction between queued, executed, and verified—especially when a Mac sleeps, a browser session disappears, or an app silently rejects a write.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to turn the spoken request into a compact intent and to report the result. Use the cheaper background/local planner for execution; use faculty-perception or deterministic checks for postconditions, escalating to vision only when structured verification is unavailable.
proposals.latency_budget: 1–3 seconds for normal file/reminder/app checks; up to 15 seconds for browser reload and evidence capture. Speak 'queued' immediately if needed, then update only when verified or definitively failed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: one local planner/action cycle plus a deterministic read-back. Vision/model cost only for GUI-only postconditions; relay storage is a few KB of evidence per step.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must not expose private page contents in the spoken reply or relay logs—store minimal hashes/snippets and redact secrets. Never infer success from an HTTP 200 or executor receipt. Irreversible external actions still require the existing owner confirmation gate; verification is not approval.

A verifier that can read back files, Calendar/Reminders, app state, or the authenticated browser after mutation and persist evidence.
A state machine and relay event for queued -> running -> executed -> verified/failed, with timeout and retry policy.

proposals.user_asks: Before you send or submit something important, show me the exact final payload on the pendant, let me approve that specific version with one button, then send it from the account that owns the session and bring back proof of what was submitted and where it went.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can prepare work and can execute Mac/browser actions, but the final human approval, the exact bytes or fields approved, the authenticated identity used, and the resulting submission are not one indivisible handoff. This would make consequential actions safe to delegate without forcing the owner to sit at the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short spoken approval interaction and concise result. Use a cheaper planner for assembling the payload and deterministic local/browser code for identity, field, attachment, and submission evidence. Escalate to vision only when the page exposes no structured representation.
proposals.latency_budget: Payload preview within 3 seconds; one-button approval immediately; submission and proof within 10 seconds when the relevant session is online. If the session disappears, hold rather than silently retry.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually low: one planning call and local deterministic checks. A few KB for the redacted payload hash and submission receipt; model cost rises only for GUI-only fields.
proposals.security_concerns: The approval must bind to a canonical payload hash, destination, authenticated account, and expiry—not to a vague spoken intent. Show secrets and private content only on the pendant/Mac owner surfaces, never in relay logs. Never auto-submit after a timeout; reject changed payloads, changed destination, changed account, stale pages, or missing attachment hashes.

A pendant approval protocol binding one button press to one immutable payload, destination, account, and short expiry.
Authenticated-session identity and submission-proof capture for Mail, Messages, and browser forms.
A commit coordinator that refuses execution if any bound field changes between preview and submit, then reports accepted, rejected, or indeterminate.

proposals.user_asks: If I say something while the pendant is offline, carry it out safely when it reconnects—once, with the right current context—and tell me exactly what happened or ask me to resolve a conflict.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can issue commands anywhere without guessing whether the link is alive. Reconnection should not replay stale or duplicate actions, silently apply changed context, or lose the request; this coordinates the wearable, always-on relay, Mac executor, and browser sessions.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture/acknowledge the short intent; use a cheaper background model to classify and reconcile queued intents. Deterministic relay/job logic should perform deduplication, expiry, leases, and conflict checks; invoke the model only for ambiguous natural-language conflicts.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local enqueue and spoken receipt when offline (<300 ms); on reconnect, status within 2 s and execution as soon as the Mac/browser is online. Conflicts must pause rather than guess.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per queued command; deterministic queue/receipt work dominates no model cost. Ambiguous conflict resolution may use one small background-model call, roughly $0.001–$0.01.
proposals.security_concerns: Queued intents may contain private context and must be encrypted at rest and scoped to the owner/device. Expire intents whose authorization or page session changed; never replay sends, purchases, deletes, or submissions without fresh confirmation. Show source time, target surface, and exact action receipt; allow cancellation before lease acquisition.

Per-intent idempotency plus context/session version preconditions at execution
A lease/expiry/conflict state machine that can pause and request owner resolution
A reconnect event from the pendant and a dashboard/spoken review of pending conflicts

proposals.user_asks: Put everything back the way it was before that task, across my Mac and logged-in browser, and show me what was restored and what could not be safely reversed.
proposals.why_useful: Today a multi-surface task can leave changes split across apps, tabs, files, and server jobs; a single last-job undo is not enough. The owner needs recovery from a partially successful task without manually remembering every mutation.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic action journals and typed compensating operations first; use the background model only to map an unfamiliar reversible mutation to a proposed compensation. Realtime is unnecessary except for a brief spoken status.
proposals.latency_budget: Build the recovery plan within 3 seconds for a recent task; execute reversible compensations sequentially with verification, pausing immediately on ambiguity or an irreversible step.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per recovery; journal lookup and typed compensation are deterministic. A rare model-assisted mapping costs roughly $0.001–$0.02.
proposals.security_concerns: Recovery must be scoped to one owner-approved task and never infer permission to delete, send, purchase, or overwrite. Show each before/after value and require fresh confirmation for any destructive compensation. Keep sensitive page values redacted in the journal while retaining hashes sufficient for verification.
missing: A task-level mutation journal spanning Mac and browser actions, not merely per-action receipts
Typed compensating actions with preconditions and postcondition verification for files, app state, and authenticated page fields
A dependency-aware rollback planner that stops when a later mutation depends on an earlier one
A recovery report that distinguishes restored, changed-by-owner, expired-session, and irreversible states

proposals.user_asks: “If this condition happens, carry out the bounded plan I gave you and tell me exactly what changed.” For example: if my authenticated travel page reports a cancellation, find an option under my stated limits, prepare it, and only commit automatically if every constraint and freshness check still passes; otherwise wake me on the pendant with the exact decision needed.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can ask for a check or a one-off action, but cannot safely leave a conditional, bounded plan running across a private browser session, their Mac, and an always-awake relay. This turns interruptions and changing external events into useful action without granting the system an open-ended standing mandate.
proposals.model_tier: background for polling/event normalization and constraint evaluation; planner only when the event requires multi-step option generation; realtime only to wake the owner and handle the live approval conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Event ingestion under 30 seconds when a watch changes; option preparation under 2 minutes; owner wake-up is immediate when a constraint is ambiguous or a commit boundary cannot be met.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually deterministic/background: roughly 1–3 cheap model calls per event (about $0.01–$0.08 depending on page extraction and option count). Planner escalation dominates cost only for ambiguous multi-site workflows.
proposals.security_concerns: The contract must be scoped to named accounts/tabs, allowed vendors, maximum amount/time, and an expiry. Private page contents leave the browser only as minimized fields and cited evidence. No irreversible commit may occur without a fresh exact-constraint proof; if evidence is stale, a session changes, or the Mac/browser disappears, the system pauses and asks. Every attempted mutation needs an immutable receipt and replay protection.

constraint evaluator that produces a machine-verifiable commit predicate

pendant-resume approval bound to the exact contract revision and evidence hashes
owner-configurable policy UI for limits, expiry, and which consequences may be automatic

proposals.user_asks: “Start this, and keep control of it even if I walk away.” Give me one action baton that can move between the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser: begin a reversible task, show/announce who currently owns it, let me pause or cancel from the pendant, and return a durable proof of exactly what happened—even across a dropped connection.
proposals.why_useful: Today judgement can choose an action but action execution is fragmented: browser may be offline, the Mac may be busy, and a receipt can exist without a way to stop an in-flight job. A durable, owner-visible baton makes long-running work safe and comprehensible: the relay stays awake, the Mac/browser performs the step that has reach, and the pendant remains the immediate cancel/status surface.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna for planning/recovery decisions; deterministic relay/local executors for leases, retries, receipts, and cancellation; gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the short spoken update.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgement under 500 ms; lease/state updates under 2 s; execution may run for minutes without holding the voice turn open. Reconnect reconciliation within 10 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per multi-step task depending on planner retries; deterministic state/receipt traffic dominates neither tokens nor compute. No model call for cancel, status, lease expiry, or reconciliation.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must never receive private page contents or credentials; owner-private browser legs remain on the authenticated Safari/Chrome bridge. Use a short-lived, audience-bound lease and idempotency key; reject stale workers and duplicate commits. Pendant cancel should be available without speech. Require explicit confirmation before irreversible browser/Mac actions; retain only hashes, field-level before/after evidence, and configurable audio/job retention.
missing: A single durable action-baton state machine shared by relay, Mac agent, browser bridge, and dashboard (queued/claimed/running/paused/cancel-requested/cancelled/committed/failed/expired).
Lease claim/renew/revoke and exactly-once commit endpoints with worker identity, fencing token, idempotency key, and heartbeat timeout.
Pendant event/push mapping for status, pause, and cancel, including offline event spool and replay (the requested offline_intent_spool and physical_action_confirmation skills are still absent).
A cancellation checkpoint contract in mac_run_actions/browser_run_actions/mac_delegate and a receipt schema that distinguishes acknowledged, partially applied, and committed effects.
A reconnect reconciler and dashboard timeline that can prove which surface performed each step and expose safe undo where available.

proposals.user_asks: “That partly failed—repair it without repeating anything that already happened.” After a Mac, browser, or relay action is interrupted, inspect the real state across the relevant surfaces, identify the exact boundary reached, and safely complete or roll back only the missing reversible work. Return a proof of the repaired final state, not merely a retry log.
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed multi-surface task leaves the owner to guess whether anything happened. Retrying can duplicate a message, appointment, file, or browser submission; undo is often unavailable once the worker or connection disappears. State-based repair would turn ambiguous failures into safe recovery, especially when the pendant goes offline after the Mac has already acted.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for state diff and repair-plan generation; deterministic typed probes and action receipts establish facts; reserve realtime for the short owner-facing explanation and confirmation when a repair could change external state.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial failure classification under 2 seconds; read-only reconciliation under 10 seconds; any repair requiring approval waits indefinitely for the owner rather than timing out into execution.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually $0.01–$0.05 per incident, dominated by one background planning call and surface reads; deterministic retries and receipt comparison are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Never infer completion from a timeout. Read private browser state only through the authenticated bridge and keep credentials on-device. Repairs that send, submit, delete, purchase, or alter external records require fresh confirmation with a precise diff. Store hashes and provenance rather than page contents; expire sensitive evidence.
missing: A state-invariant and reconciliation protocol: each action declares its expected postcondition and an idempotent observation method.
Cross-surface read probes that can verify those postconditions after worker loss, including authenticated browser state and Mac filesystem/app state.
A repair planner that produces a minimal diff from observed state, with explicit safe-to-repeat and must-not-repeat steps.
A durable incident record linking the original intent, every receipt, observed state snapshots, repair approval, and final proof.
Per-action compensation adapters for effects that are reversible but lack a current undo implementation.

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me the private part only when it is safe.” Route sensitive results and confirmations to the owner’s pendant only when the paired device proves it is present; otherwise leave a redacted notification on the Mac/dashboard and wait. This should cover logged-in browser findings, account alerts, and action receipts without exposing their contents to nearby people or an unattended speaker.
proposals.why_useful: The system can reach private browser sessions and produce speech, but it has no owner-presence boundary: a spoken account balance, message preview, or approval payload can be overheard when the pendant is elsewhere. Presence-bound disclosure lets the owner use the hive in shared spaces without choosing between privacy and usefulness.
proposals.model_tier: No model call for presence, pairing, sensitivity labels, or redaction. Use a background model only to summarize after the policy gate; realtime speaks only after an authenticated presence grant.
proposals.latency_budget: Presence decision under 200 ms from a valid pendant heartbeat/button nonce; redacted fallback under 1 second. Never speak sensitive content while presence is uncertain.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for gating; roughly a few hundred bytes of authenticated telemetry per heartbeat and event. Optional background summarization costs less than $0.01 per briefing.
proposals.security_concerns: Use mutually authenticated device keys and short-lived proximity/session proofs, not Bluetooth name or network address alone. Treat browser contents, messages, financial data, and action diffs as sensitive by default. Do not send raw private content to the relay when a local redacted route is possible. Require explicit owner policy for categories and provide an immediate pendant mute/lock gesture.
missing: A paired-device cryptographic presence protocol with freshness and replay protection.
Sensitivity labels propagated from browser extraction through planner, receipt, TTS, and dashboard rendering.
A relay policy gate that refuses sensitive TTS/upload when the presence proof is absent or stale.
Local redaction templates and a dashboard review queue for withheld content.
Pendant firmware support for secure presence nonce, lock/mute gesture, and offline policy cache.

proposals.user_asks: “Prepare this action on my Mac, but don’t release it until I give the pendant a deliberate physical confirmation—even if the voice link is gone; then tell me exactly what was released.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can safely authorize a consequential action while mobile, without relying on a fragile spoken yes/no or trusting that a stale browser/Mac job is still the one they intended. The pendant becomes a local second factor and a clear boundary between preparation and release.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to explain the pending action and collect conversational edits; compile the action packet and proof requirements with a cheaper planner/background tier. The pendant confirmation and release decision should be deterministic, not model-generated.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation may take seconds in the background; confirmation should release in under 2 seconds when the pendant is connected. If disconnected, retain a short-lived pending packet and never auto-release on reconnect.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one planner/background compilation plus ordinary Mac/browser execution; roughly $0.01–$0.08 depending on context size. Pendant button confirmation and relay routing add negligible API cost.
proposals.security_concerns: The packet must be content-bound (target, exact fields/recipients, proof obligation, expiry, idempotency key), signed or MAC-authenticated between relay and pendant, and invalidated on any edit or timeout. Never expose secrets in spoken prompts or LED patterns. Sending mail, purchasing, deleting, or submitting still requires this explicit confirmation; reconnect must not count as consent.
missing: A pendant-local confirmation protocol and signed pending-action display/LED state that works offline
A relay-held two-phase action packet with expiry, hash, and one-shot release endpoint
Mac/browser adapters that can prepare without committing and then release the exact prepared transaction
A durable proof receipt joining pendant confirmation, prepared state, release, and post-action observation

proposals.user_asks: When I say “send it” on the pendant, prepare the message on my Mac or logged-in browser, show me the exact recipient and content, wait for a deliberate physical button confirmation, execute once, then verify and report what actually happened.
proposals.why_useful: It turns a spoken intention into a safe, auditable real-world action across the wearable, relay, Mac, and private browser. The owner gets convenience without the system ever silently sending a message or submitting a form.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture the short spoken intent and confirmation; use the cheaper background/local planner to gather data and prepare the draft; deterministic code performs the final commit and verification.
proposals.latency_budget: Draft in 3–8 seconds; confirmation response under 500 ms; commit and receipt within 5 seconds, with background polling for slow sites.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per invocation depending on draft complexity; most cost is one planner call, while confirmation, commit, and verification are deterministic.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page content remains on the Mac/browser unless explicitly sent to the relay. Never commit without a fresh confirmation bound to a draft hash, recipient, tab/session, and short expiry. Require an extra confirmation for destructive, financial, or external-send actions; redact secrets from receipts.
missing: A durable cross-surface action state machine (draft → presented → physically confirmed → committed → verified)
A pendant-local confirmation skill and confirmation event API
Proof-producing postcondition checks for Mac and browser actions
Browser bridge online and Mac Accessibility/Screen Recording grants for GUI-only steps

proposals.user_asks: If an online action is interrupted halfway—such as a booking, purchase, form submission, or account change—tell me whether it actually happened, reconcile the browser, Mac, relay, and pendant state, and give me one safe recovery action instead of making me start over or risk a duplicate.
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped bridge, timeout, or reconnect can leave the owner unsure whether an external side effect occurred. This would turn ambiguous failures into a trustworthy answer and a safe continuation, which no single node can establish alone.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic state reconciliation and cheap background polling first; invoke the realtime model only to explain the result or ask a concise clarification when evidence conflicts.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial determination in 2–5 seconds from existing receipts and browser state; allow up to 60 seconds of background reconciliation for a slow site, with the pendant announcing interim status.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per incident; storage and polling dominate, with model use only for conflict explanation.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser evidence stays on the Mac unless the owner permits relay sharing. Never retry an uncertain external mutation automatically. Match account, tab, target, and idempotency key; redact payment and secret fields. Require confirmation before any compensating or duplicate-risk action.
missing: A cross-surface transaction ledger that records intent, observed side effects, and evidence independently of a single job
Site-specific postcondition and duplicate-detection adapters for browser and AppleScript actions
A reconciliation worker that survives Mac/browser disconnects and reports confidence plus next safe step
A pendant notification channel for pending, resolved, and owner-confirmation-needed states

proposals.user_asks: “Do this everywhere it needs to happen, and tell me one honest result: completed, waiting for me, or unable — with proof of what changed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a plan can span the relay, Mac AppleScript/shell, and authenticated Safari, yet each surface reports its own success and stale pipeline runs can remain processing. This gives the owner one cross-surface execution contract: faculty-judgement supplies a typed plan, faculty-action leases and executes each step on the only reachable hand, faculty-perception verifies the postcondition from an independent read, and the pendant receives a concise result. UI actions that cannot reach the screen are reported unable rather than receiving a false success receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background/local planner for decomposition and reconciliation; reserve realtime for the owner's live request and the final one-sentence spoken outcome. Do not spend the realtime tier on polling or verification.
proposals.latency_budget: Reversible one-surface actions: under 3 seconds. Multi-surface work: stream step states immediately, verify each completed step within 5 seconds, and finish or explicitly block within 30 seconds; long work becomes a durable job with relay_job_status.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly one local/background model call per ambiguous plan plus one short realtime response; most deterministic steps and checks are zero model cost. Dominant cost is private-page extraction or GUI vision, which is skipped when AppleScript/browser DOM reads suffice.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated tab contents and Mac state leave the device only through the existing bearer-protected relay paths; redact secrets from receipts and never persist page bodies by default. Require owner confirmation immediately before send/delete/purchase or any irreversible browser step. A lease expiry, duplicate request ID, failed postcondition, missing Accessibility, offline bridge, or stale tab must end as blocked/unknown—not success.
missing: A shared typed action contract linking planId, stepId, idempotency key, target surface, precondition, postcondition, approval class, lease expiry, and evidence reference.
An independent postcondition verifier that can read state without trusting the executor's success receipt, including browser tab/session affinity and AppleScript-readable Mac state.
A cross-surface receipt reducer that collapses step outcomes into completed/waiting-for-owner/unable and marks stale processing jobs.
Physical pendant pairing/telemetry so the final receipt and approval can be delivered and acknowledged on-device.

proposals.user_asks: “Pause this private browser task and let me resume it from the pendant when I’m away from my Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a logged-in browser task is tied to the Mac and its live tab; leaving the desk loses the conversational handoff or tempts unsafe re-authentication. The owner should be able to park the exact tab, draft state, and next safe step, then resume from the worn device using a short-lived, device-bound confirmation—without transmitting the page contents into the voice context. This is a new physical handoff, not a page watch, morning brief, durable job runner, or generic approval queue.
proposals.model_tier: Use no expensive model for parking, pairing, or state transfer. Use a cheap background/local model only to summarize the next step and redact it; use realtime only when the owner asks to resume or needs the short spoken prompt.
proposals.latency_budget: Parking under 2 seconds; resume prompt under 1 second after the pendant button; reattach and independently verify the tab within 5 seconds. Expire an unattended handoff after 10 minutes or the configured owner limit.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for deterministic session transfer and cryptographic checks; one small local-model call only for a redacted task label. Storage is a compact encrypted handoff record, not page content.
proposals.security_concerns: Never copy authenticated page bodies, cookies, or credentials to the pendant or relay. Bind a single-use resume capability to the paired pendant, Mac bridge, browser session, tab identity, and owner confirmation; invalidate it on tab navigation, logout, session change, or expiry. Irreversible submission still requires a fresh confirmation and independent before/after verification. If pairing or verification fails, report unable and leave the browser untouched.
missing: A paired, connected pendant with a hardware button/LED protocol and secure device identity; no pendant is present in the live device table today.
An encrypted, single-use handoff token service in the relay and a Mac-side session lease that can reattach the exact Safari tab without exposing its contents.
Browser Bridge support for freezing a tab's semantic checkpoint (URL, tab/session ID, redacted next-step label, and form-diff hash) and refusing resume after unexpected navigation.
A pendant-side confirmation/expiry state machine and a faculty-action verifier that proves the resumed tab and intended precondition are still the same before any mutation.

proposals.user_asks: “Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, but don’t leave me half-done: check everything first, make the reversible changes, ask once before the final commit, and recover cleanly if one side fails.”
proposals.why_useful: Today faculty-judgement can decide a goal, but faculty-action has no cross-surface transaction boundary. A calendar update plus browser form, or a drafted Mail message plus an authenticated submission, can partially succeed and leave the owner guessing. This gives one human-readable approval and a durable outcome instead of silent half-completion.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed action bundle with preconditions, reversible steps, irreversible commit steps, and compensation hints
relay persists the bundle and approval token, routes Mac steps to the online Mac bridge and browser steps to the authenticated Safari bridge, and survives a dropped pendant link
mac-planner/mac_run_actions performs AppleScript-backed reversible Mac steps and returns typed before/after receipts
browser-extension/browser_run_actions performs tab-affine reads and staged mutations, stopping at the declared commit gate
pendant speaks a compact 24 kHz approval summary and receives success, compensated-partial, or needs-owner-intervention status; Mac receives a local notification and a detailed receipt
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for precondition checking, step ordering, and receipt compression; reserve realtime only for the pendant approval exchange. No model should invent a commit step: the typed bundle is authoritative.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight under 3 seconds when both bridges are online; approval response under 1 second after the owner presses the button; execution may run asynchronously with status pushed to the pendant and queryable later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 in model/API cost, dominated by one short background planning/verification call; browser and Mac execution are local/relay work. Audio costs are dominated by the existing 24 kHz encode/decode path, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser contents and potentially sensitive Mail/Calendar fields cross the relay only as scoped step inputs and receipts. Irreversible steps require an approval token bound to the exact normalized bundle hash, tab/session, and expiry; a changed page or stale precondition invalidates it. Compensation must never claim success when an external side effect cannot be undone.
missing: A durable transaction coordinator with idempotency keys, precondition checks, compensation records, and explicit partial-failure states
A single approval-token protocol shared by Mac and browser bridges
Owner-defined compensation policies for actions such as sent messages, bookings, and payments
The already-requested verification/proof tools and physical confirmation skill, or an equivalent server-side implementation

proposals.user_asks: “Make my contact details consistent everywhere I use them.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can discover information in one place and edit another, but cannot safely reconcile the same personal fact across native Mac apps and authenticated websites. This capability finds conflicting values, identifies which sources are authoritative, stages the necessary edits, and presents one concise conflict report before changing anything. It is not a watch or a one-off form fill: it resolves a named fact across multiple systems.
surfaces: Pendant captures the spoken target fact and reads back the proposed canonical value and conflict count for confirmation.
Relay creates a reconciliation job, keeps a source-by-source provenance record, and resumes it if the pendant link drops.
Mac agent reads and stages changes in Contacts, Calendar, Mail signatures, and other AppleScript-granted native stores.
Browser bridge inspects authenticated profile/account pages, identifies matching fields, and stages edits without submitting them.

Faculty-perception verifies each current value; faculty-judgement chooses or asks the owner to choose the canonical value; faculty-action applies only approved, field-specific mutations and returns before/after receipts.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for field matching, conflict clustering, and provenance summarization. Use realtime only for the brief pendant confirmation and ambiguity questions.
proposals.latency_budget: Collect and compare sources in 5–15 seconds; present a short conflict summary; apply staged edits asynchronously and report completion or blocked sources.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically under $0.03 per reconciliation, dominated by authenticated page extraction and one background reasoning call; native Mac reads are local.
proposals.security_concerns: Contact details are sensitive and may include private account data. Never infer authority from frequency alone; require explicit canonical-source selection when values disagree. Bind approval to the exact field/value/source set, redact values in relay logs, and require a fresh confirmation if a page changes before mutation.
missing: A reconciliation data model for normalized personal fields, source authority, provenance, and conflicts
Field-level staged mutation support across AppleScript and browser sessions
A shared approval payload that covers multiple heterogeneous targets without allowing extra fields to be added
A privacy-preserving receipt format that shows enough evidence to audit changes without retaining full page contents

proposals.user_asks: When I tell you to change something across my Mac and a logged-in website, carry it through as one transaction: show me what changed, recover safely from a dropped connection or partial step, and tell me exactly what still needs my hands.
proposals.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an outcome but execution can split across browser, Mac, relay, and absent pendant. This gives the owner one accountable result instead of silent partial completion or duplicate clicks.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to collect intent and deliver a short status; use the cheaper background planner for step decomposition, reconciliation, and receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; reversible steps may run asynchronously for up to 2 minutes; stop immediately at an irreversible checkpoint and wait for owner approval.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per transaction, dominated by background planning and browser evidence extraction; realtime status should be a few cents or less.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page data and action evidence cross the Mac/relay boundary. Store redacted signed receipts, bind every step to tab/session and an idempotency key, and require explicit confirmation for sending, deleting, purchasing, or external side effects. Never replay an unacknowledged step after reconnect.
missing: A durable transaction coordinator that understands partial completion and compensating actions (the current receipt/undo work has no gates or preconditions)
Signed step proofs and a reconnect-safe pendant acknowledgement protocol
A deterministic reconciliation worker that compares intended, observed, and completed state across Mac and browser
A clear dashboard timeline for pending approval, completed, compensated, and needs-owner states

proposals.user_asks: Let me approve a prepared Mac or logged-in-browser action with one physical press on the pendant, but only when the pendant is demonstrably near my Mac; show me the exact action on the pendant first, and keep it paused if the pendant, relay, or browser session is not the same one that prepared it.
proposals.why_useful: Today approval is logically possible but not strongly tied to the owner’s physical presence or to the exact prepared browser state. This would let the owner safely approve from the pendant without opening the laptop, while preventing a stale, replayed, or remotely substituted transaction from executing.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to parse the spoken approval and provide a brief status; use deterministic firmware/relay verification and a cheaper background model only for explaining a blocked or changed transaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant should display the prepared action class within 500 ms, accept the press in under 1 second, and have the Mac execute or report a mismatch within 3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per approval; cryptographic verification and BLE/proximity checks dominate, with model cost only when a human-readable mismatch explanation is needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Bind approval to a transaction hash, Mac bridge identity, browser session/tab identity, expiry, and one-time nonce. Do not treat BLE presence alone as authorization for high-risk actions; require a distinct long press and retain the existing confirmation policy for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other irreversible effects. Keep page contents off the pendant and relay except for a short redacted summary.
missing: A pendant hardware identity and authenticated proximity channel to the Mac
A signed transaction envelope containing action hash, target session/tab, expiry, and risk class
Firmware rendering of a short redacted action summary and a distinct approval gesture
Relay verification that rejects stale, replayed, cross-device, or session-changed approvals
Mac/browser execution hook that consumes the one-time approval atomically

proposals.user_asks: “I’m holding the pendant—commit the prepared transaction now, but only if I press its button within the next 10 seconds.”
proposals.why_useful: Makes an irreversible browser or Mac action require a physical, time-bound presence signal, while still letting the mind prepare everything hands-free. The owner gets a clear spoken before/after summary and the action expires safely if the pendant is absent or the link drops.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the short confirmation exchange; background/local code for expiry, receipt, and delivery.
proposals.latency_budget: Prepare in the background; commit within 1 second of the button event; spoken result within 3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost: one realtime turn only when committing; local serial and relay receipt work dominate, not model tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: The button is a possession factor, not identity proof. Require an explicit transaction digest spoken/displayed before arming, bind the nonce to the exact tab/action, enforce 10-second expiry and idempotency, and never send secrets from the pendant.
missing: pendant button event bridged over USB/LTE
a commit-lease endpoint binding nonce, tab/session, and exact action digest
firmware LED/audio acknowledgement for armed/expired/committed states

proposals.user_asks: “I plugged in the pendant—run a safe end-to-end health check and tell me whether the microphone, 24 kHz playback path, ESP32 bridge, and headphones each work.”
proposals.why_useful: Turns today’s USB-connected prototype into something the owner can trust before relying on it. One command would exercise the actual serial devices and audio chain, isolate failures, and leave a timestamped report instead of guessing whether silence is caused by codec, I2S, bridge, Bluetooth, or relay.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background/local diagnostic logic; realtime only to narrate the concise result if requested.
proposals.latency_budget: 15–30 seconds for the full test; immediate progress LED/status is preferable to a silent wait.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; serial probes and a short generated test tone are the dominant work.
proposals.security_concerns: Use a generated tone and synthetic recording only—never upload ambient microphone data. Require explicit opt-in before any cloud echo test; redact serial logs and retain only pass/fail plus firmware/bridge versions.
missing: mac_read_build_and_devices or equivalent USB serial enumeration
audio_path_probe with a synthetic loopback/latency test
a protocol command in both firmwares for deterministic tone, mic loopback, and bridge acknowledgements

proposals.user_asks: “If the Mac finishes an action while my pendant is disconnected, save the result and tell me exactly once when I reconnect—without rerunning anything.”
proposals.why_useful: Prevents the worst real-world failure mode: the owner cannot tell whether a remote action happened and repeats it. The Mac/relay would escrow a signed receipt while offline, and the pendant would announce the outcome on reconnection with the target, timestamp, and undo option where available.
proposals.model_tier: No model for storage/deduplication; cheap background summarization for a short spoken receipt.
proposals.latency_budget: Store receipt immediately; deliver within 2 seconds of reconnection; no polling burden on the owner.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal storage and relay invocation cost; one short TTS/realtime turn per queued receipt.
proposals.security_concerns: Encrypt receipts at rest, retain only action metadata and a redacted summary, bind each receipt to an idempotency key, and require button confirmation before any undo. Never replay page contents or credentials over the audio link.
missing: a durable per-device receipt inbox with exactly-once acknowledgement
USB/LTE reconnect identity and monotonic event cursor
pendant reconnect event plus a small spoken-receipt playback queue

proposals.user_asks: “When I’m in the middle of something, protect my attention: pause background work, suppress non-urgent alerts, and bring back only the one item that truly needs me when I’m free.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can act across the Mac, browser, relay, and pendant, but it cannot coordinate those surfaces around the owner’s changing availability. This would make the wearable an attention boundary rather than another notification stream: a button gesture or spoken state pauses queued browser/Mac work, while the always-awake relay triages urgent exceptions and restores the work at a deliberate moment.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background classifier/rules for urgency and queue management; realtime only for the owner’s brief state change and urgent announcement.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause within 1 second of the pendant event; urgent exception within 2 seconds; resume only on explicit owner release or scheduled window.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low ongoing cost: event-driven relay state and local queue operations; model calls only for ambiguous urgency classification.
proposals.security_concerns: Availability state is sensitive behavioral data. Store coarse states with short retention, do not infer from microphone continuously, and require explicit opt-in for calendar/browser-derived urgency. Paused actions must not silently expire into execution.
missing: a shared attention-state protocol across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
queue pause/resume semantics that preserve idempotency and deadlines
an urgency policy that can distinguish an exception from ordinary notification

proposals.user_asks: “Handle this until you hit a decision only I can make; ask me that one question on the pendant, then continue from the exact step without starting over.”
proposals.why_useful: Current delegation either finishes a predefined action or leaves the owner to reconstruct a half-completed browser task. This would let the Mac and authenticated browser do long, messy workflows while the pendant becomes a narrow decision channel: the owner answers one constrained question, and the system resumes with the same tab, draft, and evidence instead of repeating or guessing.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background/local planner for deterministic steps and state serialization; realtime only for the short blocking question and answer.
proposals.latency_budget: Continue automatically until blocked; deliver a blocking question within 5 seconds; resume within 2 seconds of the answer.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate but bounded: model calls only at step boundaries or ambiguity; browser execution and state snapshots dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Never convert an unanswered question into a guess. Persist only redacted form state and a locator/step ID, encrypt private page snapshots, and require explicit confirmation for financial, legal, or outbound communication decisions.
missing: a resumable workflow state machine with durable browser checkpoints
a typed blocking-question protocol with constrained answers and expiry
tab/session reattachment that verifies the page is still the same before resuming

proposals.user_asks: Do this for me, safely: carry out my spoken goal across my Mac and logged-in browser, and use a physical button press on the pendant as the final confirmation whenever the action would send, submit, delete, or buy. Then tell me exactly what happened.
proposals.why_useful: This is the clearest path from a voice decision to a trustworthy real-world action: the Mac/browser can reach private sessions, while the worn button is a deliberate confirmation channel that cannot be triggered by an accidental spoken phrase. Receipts make the result auditable.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the short spoken goal and confirmation prompt; background/cheap model for plan validation and receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to show the pending confirmation on the pendant after planning; under 10 seconds for reversible actions, with long browser jobs continuing asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per invocation; realtime turn dominates, while receipt and precondition checks should use a cheaper model.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents stay in the browser/Mac boundary. The relay receives only a redacted action summary and nonce. Require a fresh short-lived nonce, visible LED/button state, state hash precondition, and explicit confirmation for send/delete/purchase; never treat a stale button press as approval.
missing: pendant registration and button/LED command path
physical confirmation firmware skill
action lease and state-proof verification
planner-to-action protocol that carries irreversible checkpoints

proposals.user_asks: Save what I am looking at for later.

proposals.user_asks: “Even with no LTE registration, let me use the pendant today: press the button, speak through the USB-connected pendant/ESP32, and hear the response, with the Mac relaying it to the same conversation.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can wear and use the actual hardware now instead of waiting for cellular registration; a dropped relay link can fall back to the Mac USB path and resume the same session.

proposals.user_asks: “When a Mac or browser job fails, don’t just tell me it failed: inspect the receipt, logs, browser heartbeat, and current Mac state, repair transient problems, retry safely, and tell me exactly what was fixed or why you stopped.”
proposals.why_useful: Long-running work becomes dependable: stale browser bridges, expired tabs, temporary network errors, and interrupted Mac jobs are recovered without making the owner re-explain the task.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background planner for diagnosis and deterministic retry policies; invoke realtime only to speak the final result or ask for a decision.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect within 10 seconds of a failed receipt; recover common transient failures within 60 seconds; never loop more than three attempts.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one small background planning call per failure, with deterministic checks dominating; negligible cost for healthy jobs.
proposals.security_concerns: Retries must be idempotency-keyed and limited to reversible steps. Any send, delete, purchase, or external mutation pauses for confirmation. Logs may contain private content and should remain on the Mac unless a redacted diagnostic is needed.

proposals.user_asks: “Do the private parts on my Mac, but still coordinate everything for me: use my logged-in browser and local files without sending their contents to the relay, then give me a concise answer or execute the approved next step.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets the reach of private browser sessions and local files without turning the relay into a copy of their secrets; this makes cross-surface action safe enough for everyday use.
proposals.model_tier: A local Mac planner performs extraction, redaction, and action planning; the relay realtime model receives only typed claims, hashes, and the minimum excerpt needed for the conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Local private inspection under 3 seconds for routine pages; relay response under 2 seconds after the redacted result arrives.
proposals.cost_estimate: Lower than sending full pages: small local planning call plus the existing spoken turn; token savings grow with large authenticated pages.
proposals.security_concerns: Define a deny-by-default field policy for credentials, tokens, health/financial identifiers, and message bodies. Keep raw evidence local with short retention; dashboard must show what crossed the boundary. External mutations still require the owner’s existing confirmation policy.
missing: A local redaction/typed-result protocol with sensitivity labels and provenance
Relay enforcement that rejects raw private payloads rather than trusting the planner
Dashboard evidence showing local-only fields versus fields shared with the relay

proposals.user_asks: “Repeat the last thing I had you do, but adapt it to what is on screen now, and show me the exact differences before you run it.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can safely reuse successful workflows without reconstructing them from memory: the system replays the intent and structure, not stale clicks or private page contents, then presents a current-state diff.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background planner reconstructs the prior typed action graph; realtime is used only for the owner’s spoken request and concise approval summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Reconstruction in under 5 seconds; current-state inspection and diff in under 15 seconds; no execution until approval.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small planning call plus local browser/Mac inspection; no cost when unused.
proposals.security_concerns: Never replay credentials or hidden fields. Bind replay to the original account/session, re-resolve targets semantically, and stop on changed recipients, amounts, destructive effects, or missing evidence. Keep prior raw evidence local.
missing: A semantic action-graph recorder distinct from low-level receipts
Current-versus-prior field diff renderer with provenance
A replay engine that re-plans against the live browser/Mac state and requires approval at mutation boundaries

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me whether the pendant is truly usable right now—not merely connected—and, if it isn’t, run a safe loopback test and explain the failing part.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets an immediate, trustworthy answer about button capture, microphone input, speaker playback, serial transport, and relay reachability instead of guessing from a USB icon or LED.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic hardware probes and signal checks do the work; use realtime only to explain the result in one short spoken response.
proposals.latency_budget: Basic status under 2 seconds; full loopback under 10 seconds; never transmit captured test audio beyond the local Mac unless explicitly requested.
proposals.cost_estimate: No model cost for healthy checks; negligible local CPU and a few seconds of generated test tone.
proposals.security_concerns: Use synthetic tones and discard them immediately. Do not open the owner’s microphone or record environmental audio. Device identity must be allowlisted and tests must not flash or alter firmware.
missing: A read-only serial/I2S diagnostic protocol
A deterministic audio loopback and button/LED test runner
Typed health evidence that distinguishes attached, authenticated, audio-ready, and relay-reachable

proposals.user_asks: “Put this page, quote, or result from my private browser onto my phone as a secure handoff, and let me pick it up later on the pendant without making me copy or expose the whole page.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can move a useful fragment between the browser they are using and the device they are wearing without email, clipboard leakage, or losing the source context; the handoff remains useful even when the browser tab is later closed.
proposals.model_tier: Local Mac extraction and redaction are deterministic/cheap; background model normalizes the selected fragment and title; realtime only speaks confirmation or retrieval.
proposals.latency_budget: Create a handoff in under 3 seconds; retrieve it from the pendant in under 2 seconds when cached.
proposals.cost_estimate: Tiny background-model call per handoff, dominated by local extraction; no call for plain URL-only transfers.
proposals.security_concerns: Handoffs inherit source sensitivity and expire by default. Do not send whole authenticated pages; require explicit selection or a narrowly scoped excerpt, encrypt in transit and at rest, and show the destination/device and expiry before creation.
missing: A cross-device handoff object with encrypted payload, expiry, source URL, and sensitivity label
Browser command to select/clip a bounded excerpt with provenance
iOS/pendant retrieval and deletion protocol

proposals.user_asks: “I’ve approved this on my pendant—carry out the prepared action now, but only if the physical confirmation is fresh.”
proposals.why_useful: Turns the worn device into a possession-bound approval key. A prepared browser/Mac action cannot be accidentally triggered by a stale voice transcript, remote replay, or an unattended Mac; the owner gets a fast tactile commit path while the system keeps evidence of exactly what was approved.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model interprets the short approval and binds it to a pending action; deterministic relay/Mac code validates a nonce, expiry, device identity, and action hash; no expensive model call is needed to execute.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 500 ms from button/voice confirmation to relay acknowledgment; execution latency is the underlying Mac/browser operation.
proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.001 per approval after implementation; dominant cost is any original planning call, not the nonce validation.
proposals.security_concerns: The approval must be a one-time nonce bound to action hash, account/session, and 10-second expiry; never transmit or log secrets. Require explicit confirmation for irreversible actions and show a compact spoken summary before arming. Missing today: pendant identity/serial approval protocol and a server-side pending-action gate.
missing: pending-action approval ledger with nonce/action hash/expiry
USB-serial pendant confirmation bridge usable today and LTE transport later

proposals.user_asks: “If that computer task partially succeeded, find out what actually changed, finish only the missing parts, and tell me exactly what you repaired.”
proposals.why_useful: Most dangerous automation failures are ambiguous outcomes: a form may have submitted while the receipt timed out, or a calendar event may have been created before the browser crashed. This capability makes the action system outcome-oriented rather than retry-oriented, preventing duplicate submissions and giving the owner a trustworthy final state.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background reconciliation compares typed receipts and fresh observations; realtime is used only to explain the result to the owner. Deterministic idempotency and state checks precede any repair.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial ambiguity notice within 2 seconds; reconciliation within 30 seconds for normal Mac/browser tasks, with a durable job continuing after disconnect.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.003–$0.02 per ambiguous task depending on observation/model extraction; most successful tasks incur no extra model call.
proposals.security_concerns: Never blindly retry mutations. Re-observe the exact account/tab/object, require idempotency keys, preserve before/after evidence, and escalate if identity or destination differs. Data leaving device is limited to necessary page/action metadata. Missing today: a typed postcondition/reconciliation engine and cross-surface receipt ledger.

proposals.user_asks: “Walk me through this checklist one step at a time; do the safe computer steps, pause for my pendant confirmation at the risky steps, and let me cancel without touching the Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: Makes long real-world workflows usable while the owner is away from the screen: the Mac/browser handles navigation and data gathering, while the pendant provides an unmistakable checkpoint and emergency stop. The owner can complete tasks such as returns, travel changes, or account recovery without surrendering control of the final commits.
proposals.model_tier: Background/local planner decomposes and executes reversible steps; realtime model speaks only current step and interprets brief responses. Deterministic checkpoint state machine handles pause, timeout, cancel, and resume.
proposals.latency_budget: Spoken next-step update under 1 second; safe steps proceed automatically; risky-step confirmation expires after 60 seconds and cancellation takes effect within 1 second.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.08 per multi-step workflow, dominated by initial planning and occasional browser extraction; checkpoint turns are cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: Each checkpoint displays action, target, and expected effect in speech/pendant LED pattern; cancel must be local and work through USB even if relay is unreachable. Do not expose page contents on audio unless requested. Missing today: durable workflow state machine, pendant button/LED protocol, and action-specific risk classifier.
missing: checkpointed workflow executor with pause/resume/cancel

proposals.user_asks: “Move this appointment to the best available time, but don’t cancel the current one unless the replacement is confirmed.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets safe multi-system transactions instead of brittle sequences that can leave them with no appointment, duplicate bookings, or a missing reservation. The system can negotiate a replacement, hold it, and commit only when the complete transition is evidenced.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background planner searches and compares options; deterministic transaction orchestration handles holds, commit ordering, compensation, and timeouts. Realtime is used only for presenting the choice and receiving a final preference.
proposals.latency_budget: Show viable options within 60 seconds where the site permits; commit confirmation within 2 seconds after the owner’s pendant approval; retain the old booking until the replacement has a durable confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.15 per transaction, dominated by authenticated-page extraction and any negotiation/planning calls.

proposals.user_asks: “While the pendant is USB-tethered to my Mac, let its button and tiny status light control my current action: press once to capture a thought, press twice to mark it urgent, and hold to cancel the last unsent capture—then read the result back to me.”

Store URL, timestamp, tab ID, selected text hash, and extraction confidence; redact passwords, tokens, and hidden form fields. Never overwrite an existing project file without a versioned diff.

proposals.user_asks: “Close out my last meeting.”

The pendant gives a concise spoken recap while the Mac keeps the evidence packet.
