proposals.why_useful: Today a multi-surface task can continue in inconsistent fragments if the owner is interrupted. A real checkpoint lets them safely switch contexts, sleep, or disconnect without losing the state of work in progress.
proposals.model_tier: Use a background model to summarize external changes and reconstruct the checkpoint; realtime only handles the short pause/resume commands.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 1 second; checkpoint captured within 5 seconds; resume diff available within 10 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.08 per checkpoint, dominated by diffing browser/file state; storage is small structured metadata plus selected local snapshots.
proposals.security_concerns: Checkpoint contents may include private pages and drafts. Encrypt at rest, bind to the owner/session, redact secrets from spoken diffs, and require confirmation before applying any external changes discovered during the pause.
missing: A cross-surface checkpoint schema with immutable state hashes
Mac file/draft snapshot adapters and browser DOM/session snapshot adapters
Conflict analysis that distinguishes owner edits from agent edits
A restore planner that can resume without replaying already-completed side effects

proposals.user_asks: When I say “show me what you would do,” give me a dry-run of the complete Mac-and-browser action: the exact files, tabs, fields, and messages that would change, plus a spoken summary through the pendant. Let me edit the plan by voice, then execute only the approved version and produce a machine-checkable before/after record.
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets the confidence of seeing a complete action before it happens, including hidden cross-tab dependencies that a simple confirmation misses. Voice remains sufficient even when the owner is not looking at the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper planning model builds the dry-run; realtime converts only the final diff and voice edits into a concise interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial plan under 8 seconds for ordinary tasks; voice edits acknowledged under 1 second; execution starts only after the final plan hash is approved.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.03–$0.15 per dry-run depending on number of tabs and files; local diffing dominates latency, not audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Never send or submit during simulation. Include source URLs, file paths, field-level before/after values, and sensitivity labels. Approval must bind to the final plan hash so later mutations cannot silently alter the approved action.
missing: A side-effect-free action simulator for Mac and browser operations
A plan-hash approval protocol shared by relay, Mac, and browser bridge
Field/file-level diff extraction and spoken redaction
A typed execution proof tied to the approved plan

changes.change: Add a readiness-bound intent escrow protocol rather than treating queued work as a generic job. Each intent stores an encrypted payload reference, owner/device identity, monotonic idempotency key, expiry, required surface capabilities, precondition/readiness snapshot, and a resumable step cursor. Readiness events from the Mac bridge and browser extension wake only eligible intents; the action executor must atomically claim a cursor, return typed blocked reasons, and reconcile duplicate/unknown outcomes before advancing. Emit pendant-readable state transitions (queued, blocked with exact reason, resumed, completed, expired, canceled).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: An instruction given while walking away will not silently disappear or run against a changed page. The owner gets a truthful pending status and a completion receipt, while recovery from browser-offline or missing Mac permissions happens automatically when safe.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay schema/state machine, signed readiness events, executor claim/reconciliation, pendant sync, and fault-injection tests for disconnects and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A bad eligibility rule could delay work or resume it unexpectedly. Mitigate with conservative expiry, changed-precondition pause, explicit reapproval for consequential actions, append-only transition receipts, and an operator cancel endpoint. If relay storage is unavailable, pendant keeps only the bounded local spool and reports unsynced.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and queue overhead; background model calls only for normalization/reconciliation, roughly cents per complex resumed task. No new inference on every heartbeat.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local ack; resume typically within one heartbeat (seconds), with extra latency only when fresh browser state or reconciliation is required.
changes.security_impact: Adds sensitive queued-command retention, so encrypt payloads, minimize metadata, bind claims to device/session keys, use short TTLs, and redact command content from ordinary logs.
depends_on: Typed Mac/browser readiness snapshots, including Accessibility/Screen Recording and browser extension/session state
Durable job records with idempotency and receipts
Pendant offline_intent_spool firmware skill
A signed bridge event or authenticated polling mechanism
A policy hook from faculty-judgement for actions requiring renewed approval

changes.change: Introduce a signed cross-surface execution-causality record. Every action step emits a compact envelope containing goal version, step ID, selected surface, readiness snapshot, locator/target identity, evidence hash, side-effect classification, and outcome (including unknown). When a step fails, the relay freezes the cursor and fans the envelope to perception, judgment, and the appropriate Mac/browser executor; a repair proposal must reference the failed evidence and prove target equivalence before action can resume.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When an automation task breaks halfway through, the owner can recover without guessing whether anything was already sent, changed, or duplicated. The system can explain the exact break and safely continue instead of abandoning the whole task.
changes.effort: High: shared event schema and signing, adapters in Mac/browser/relay, cursor freeze/reconciliation, repair proposal API, and fault-injection tests.
changes.risk: More instrumentation can create false confidence if an adapter reports success incorrectly. Treat unknown outcomes as a hard stop, retain raw evidence hashes, and provide a cancel/review path. Schema rollout needs backward-compatible envelopes.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay storage and serialization overhead; modest background inference only on failures. No cost added to ordinary successful steps beyond telemetry.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible on successful steps; failed steps gain one evidence-upload round trip and bounded repair analysis.
changes.security_impact: Authenticated-page and UI evidence becomes sensitive operational data. Encrypt payloads, store hashes rather than raw evidence by default, use short retention, and bind records to the owner/device session.
depends_on: A shared typed event schema across relay, Mac planner, Mac vision, and browser extension
Existing action receipts and idempotency support
A judgment policy for target equivalence and renewed approval
Executor support for frozen/resumable cursors

changes.change: Implement an operation journal and commit state machine shared by judgement, action, and perception. Persist Operation {operationId, manifestHash, requester/session, status}; Step {stepId, dependency IDs, lease token/expiry, precondition result, executor receipt, postcondition result, evidence refs, compensation}; and append-only events. Expose claim/heartbeat/complete/verify/resume endpoints with idempotency on operationId+stepId, optimistic version checks, and a reconciler that marks disconnected leases as paused rather than replaying them. Completion must require an independent verifier result for every postcondition; otherwise status is needs-review. Add a deterministic verifier adapter for common Mac/browser facts and a signed final receipt consumed by relay-realtime and the dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks for a chain of changes across private browser tabs and the Mac, the system can resume safely after sleep or a dropped connection and can distinguish 'executor returned' from 'the intended result is visibly true.' Failures become one actionable exception with a safe resume/undo path instead of silent partial completion.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and D1 migrations, relay endpoints and worker reconciler, local-agent claim/heartbeat adapter, browser bridge evidence adapter, and perception verifier integration; then fault-injection tests for duplicate delivery, stale pages, lease expiry, and partial completion.
changes.risk: A bug in dependency or version handling could pause valid work or, worse, duplicate a side effect. Default all unknown/stale/conflicting states to pause; require idempotency keys and manual approval for irreversible steps. Keep the current executor path as a compatibility fallback and migrate one reversible workflow first.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/event-storage increase; evidence should be content-addressed and short-lived in R2. Background model calls for semantic verification are the main API cost; hashes, URL checks, and typed field comparisons are effectively free.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one verification read after each mutation and heartbeat traffic for long steps; no added latency to simple read-only replies. Relay acknowledgement remains immediate while execution is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability and limits replay, but manifests and evidence become sensitive durable records. Bind leases to authenticated device/session, sign final receipts, encrypt sensitive evidence, redact page text by default, and enforce per-step approval policy before dispatch.
depends_on: A typed action receipt format that includes provenance and before/after references
A perception endpoint/tool able to request fresh Mac and browser observations
Durable browser job runner and authenticated browser session affinity
A server-push/result path to relay-realtime and a pendant approval interaction

changes.change: Add a privacy-preserving place-trigger service spanning the iOS client, relay, Mac agent, browser bridge, and pendant: iOS converts approved geofences into coarse signed place-arrival events (never uploads continuous coordinates); relay deduplicates and starts a staged, allowlisted preparation job; Mac/browser run read-and-draft-only actions; relay creates a short-lived approval token bound to the exact manifest; the pendant displays a minimal ready state and requires a deliberate button event before the final action is released. Expire or cancel the token on departure, timeout, stale private-page evidence, or changed manifest.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can walk into a place and have the relevant work ready without needing to remember to ask, while retaining a clear physical boundary before anything consequential is sent or changed. It makes the wearable, phone, always-on relay, private browser, and Mac cooperate in a way no single device can provide.
changes.effort: High: iOS native geofence/background delivery, relay event and token persistence, staged Mac/browser execution mode, pendant result/approval protocol, dashboard configuration UI, and end-to-end spoofing/offline/timeout tests.
changes.risk: False or spoofed location could start private preparation or cause notification fatigue; it must never authorize the final side effect. Use coarse place IDs, signed events, deduplication, quiet hours, per-trigger budgets, and default cancellation. If the pendant is disconnected, leave the packet staged and do not auto-commit.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing storage and event cost; approximately $0.01–$0.05 per preparation run for background extraction, with no realtime call unless the owner engages. iOS implementation and QA are the dominant engineering cost.
changes.latency_impact: Background geofence delivery is platform-dependent; target 10–60 seconds from arrival to ready packet. Button approval is immediate, and final dispatch acknowledgement should be under 2 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Introduces location and trigger metadata, so store coarse place identifiers only, expire event details, encrypt staged private evidence, bind approval tokens to a manifest hash and device/session, and audit every trigger and approval. Require explicit setup and per-trigger scope; no silent external communication.
depends_on: iOS background location/geofence integration
Relay staged-job and expiring approval-token state
Pendant firmware/server-push status and local confirmation handling
Mac/browser read-and-draft-only preparation mode
Per-place privacy/action policy and dashboard configuration

changes.change: Add an Action Manifest/Checkpoint service shared by judgement, perception, and executors. Persist a versioned manifest containing action steps, assumption IDs with observedAt/validUntil, sensitivity, reversibility, idempotency key, and required confirmation. Before every irreversible or externally visible step, atomically compare current perception versions and field hashes; if any dependency is expired or invalidated, transition the job to paused_stale, cancel downstream steps, and emit a redacted pause event to the pendant. Store append-only evidence receipts and support resume only with a new manifest or explicit owner confirmation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request made at breakfast cannot accidentally send the wrong email, submit an outdated form, or act on a changed price while the owner is away. The owner gets a precise explanation of what changed and can resume safely instead of restarting the whole task.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema, D1/R2 persistence, compare-and-swap state transitions, adapters in browser and Mac runners, and pendant notification plumbing. Build with feature flags and replay tests for disconnects/races.
changes.risk: A false invalidation may pause harmless work; recover by allowing resume from the last verified checkpoint. A missed event is more serious, so the executor must re-read critical state immediately before irreversible steps and fail closed on missing evidence. Prevent duplicate actions with idempotency keys and receipt reconciliation.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay storage and background polling cost; approximately 1–5 KB manifest plus receipts per job, with model spend near zero except summarizing a pause. No new per-invocation realtime spend.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local/relay state check (tens of milliseconds) before each guarded step; external page/file re-read may add 0.5–2 seconds only at irreversible checkpoints.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by keeping secrets out of spoken events and storing hashes/redacted deltas. Requires authenticated device-to-relay event signing and strict tenant/job isolation; never log raw form fields or message bodies by default.
depends_on: faculty-judgement emits stable assumption IDs and required-confirmation policy
faculty-perception publishes versioned invalidation events
browser and Mac action runners return typed before/after evidence
pendant push/confirm transport
durable relay job runner

changes.change: Add a cross-surface operation-state reconciler that derives terminal job status from append-only pipeline events and relay acknowledgements, rather than trusting the current `processing` field. It should validate event ordering, mark runs completed/failed/expired, detect orphaned uploads and stale pending browser commands, and emit one signed owner-facing receipt with the evidence IDs. A reconnecting pendant must receive only the receipt delta it has not acknowledged, keyed by pipelineId plus event sequence.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The live pipeline currently contains runs that have `done` events but remain `processing`; the owner cannot reliably tell whether an offline alert, spoken response, or Mac action actually finished. This prevents safe follow-up and can cause duplicate work. Correct terminal receipts make 'what happened?' trustworthy across dropped links.
changes.effort: Medium: define event-schema/state reducer, migration for existing pipeline records, relay/Mac reconciliation endpoint, pendant ACK cursor, and dashboard diagnostics; add crash/reconnect and duplicate-delivery tests.
changes.risk: A reducer could prematurely close a job when events arrive late. Use a bounded settling window, explicit `expired/unknown` instead of success, and retain the raw event log for replay. On migration, preserve all records and label old runs `legacy-uncertain` rather than rewriting history.
changes.cost_impact: Small background compute and D1/local JSON writes; roughly <$0.001 per operation. No new model call required.
changes.latency_impact: Receipts become available within one event cycle (target <500 ms online); a 5–10 second settling window applies only when the link is unstable.
changes.security_impact: Receipts should contain metadata and provenance IDs, not raw private page/audio contents. Sign relay acknowledgements and scope each receipt to the paired pendant/Mac identity.
depends_on: A shared typed event envelope with sequence numbers and idempotency keys
Relay persistence and pendant acknowledgement cursor
Action/browser runners emitting explicit per-step terminal evidence

changes.change: Introduce an evidence-gated Action Lease protocol across judgement, relay, Mac, browser, and pendant. A lease contains an action-plan hash, intended surface/session, preconditions, risk class, expiry, and checkpoint index. The executor must return preflight evidence before each checkpoint and postcondition evidence after it; the relay rejects stale or duplicate leases and records reconnect-safe state. For UI actions, accessibility/screen-recording reachability is a hard gate; queue acceptance is never an effect. The pendant button acknowledges only the explicitly named irreversible checkpoint, with the spoken target and hash rendered in the receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks the system to act, they either get proof that it happened or a clear explanation of what blocked it. They stop losing trust to fake “done” messages when the Mac lacks permission or Safari is disconnected, while still being able to approve a real send/submit from the device in their hand.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine, relay persistence/idempotency, Mac/browser observers, pendant event handling, and end-to-end fault-injection tests.
changes.risk: A false-negative preflight could pause a harmless action; recover with a retry/recheck path and allow read-only actions to proceed under a lower risk class. A lease bug could duplicate a side effect; enforce unique action IDs, atomic relay transitions, and require postcondition evidence. Never auto-fail over private browser work to a public backend.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible inference cost for typed checks; modest D1 writes and telemetry. Engineering cost is in protocol and test coverage, not hardware.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–2 seconds for preflight and postcondition checks; avoids long waits and unsafe retries when a surface is unavailable. Pendant confirmation adds only human decision time at irreversible checkpoints.
changes.security_impact: Improves security: short-lived, session-bound, single-use leases and explicit physical confirmation reduce replay and accidental side effects. Evidence must be redacted and private-page payloads remain on the owning surface.
depends_on: Mac Accessibility and Screen Recording must be granted to the actual AI Pendant Agent binary for UI control
Durable browser job IDs and reconnect reconciliation
A shared typed context/provenance service so lease evidence carries source, timestamp, and sensitivity
Pendant firmware event/state support for awaiting-confirmation and blocked states

changes.change: Add a mandatory execution preflight for any screen-dependent action (ui_click, ui_menu, type_text, press_keys, vision/computer-use steps): read the live permission/input-reachability snapshot immediately before dispatch. If uiActionsWillReachTheScreen is false, do not dispatch the event; return a typed blocked result with the exact missing grant, host bundle identity, and a recovery instruction. For non-UI actions, continue normally. Include preflight state and timestamp in the action receipt so faculty-judgement can distinguish blocked, dispatched-but-unverified, and verified outcomes; re-check after dispatch when possible.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing “done” when nothing happened. A failed Mac permission setup becomes an honest, actionable response instead of a misleading success receipt, while safe shell/API actions keep working.
changes.effort: Moderate: central executor guard plus typed result/receipt schema, tests for UI-vs-non-UI routing and stale permission snapshots; coordinate with faculty-perception’s evidence envelope.
changes.risk: Some existing UI jobs will become blocked rather than silently ineffective; this is a deliberate safety improvement. Recovery is to grant Accessibility/Screen Recording to the exact AI Pendant Agent binary, then retry the blocked action by job/action ID. A race between preflight and OS permission changes is handled by post-action evidence marking the result unverified.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local status read per UI action and small receipt metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly tens of milliseconds for local preflight; avoids long wasted vision loops.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing UI input when the OS cannot accept it; exposes only permission state and bundle identity, not screen contents.
depends_on: faculty-perception’s cross-surface evidence envelope
A stable local permission/input-reachability status API

changes.change: Make every Mac action receipt reachability-aware and evidence-graded. At dispatch, attach the current /observe snapshot (Accessibility trusted, eventsPost, uiActionsWillReachTheScreen, Screen Recording, browser-online/session state). For UI actions, if uiActionsWillReachTheScreen is false, mark the step attempted_unverified rather than success, preserve the exact reason and affected step range, and require a later verified re-run to close the job. For browser actions, distinguish queued, bridge_offline, executed, and result_verified. Never let a syntactically successful API response overwrite an unverified physical outcome; expose a compact receipt suitable for pendant speech and a detailed audit record.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today the agent can say it completed a click or typed text even though macOS reports synthesized events do not reach the screen. The owner gets an honest answer immediately, knows exactly what needs fixing, and can safely retry later instead of trusting a false completion.
changes.effort: Medium: central receipt schema plus pre/post observation capture, status transitions, tests for inaccessible UI and offline browser, and relay speech formatting.
changes.risk: Some existing jobs will appear less successful because false positives become attempted_unverified; recover by retaining raw responses and offering explicit retry after permissions/bridge return. Observation itself is read-only.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a small local JSON receipt and one read-only observation call per UI job/step batch.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–150 ms for local observation; no model call required.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety and auditability. Snapshots should exclude window contents/URLs unless already part of the action receipt; do not upload screenshots or page text.
depends_on: A stable typed receipt schema shared by /execute, jobs, and relay completion messages
The existing /observe endpoint and inputReachability probe
A retry/continuation endpoint that preserves idempotency keys

changes.change: Implement an Action Handoff Contract shared by judgement, relay, Mac, and browser: every intent carries intentId, idempotencyKey, requiredHands, preflight predicates, approval lease, retry budget, and evidence schema. The relay persists an append-only lifecycle (planned→preflight_blocked/queued→running→verified or failed/cancelled/expired), consumes bridge/browser reconnect events, and only emits completed after typed evidence verification. Existing receipts link to lifecycle events but cannot imply success alone.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say a goal once and trust that it will either happen or clearly explain the exact missing access/device. Requests survive closing Safari or temporarily losing the Mac, without duplicate sends or the dangerous illusion that an attempted action succeeded.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared TypeScript contract, D1/local persistence migration, reconnect hooks, preflight adapters for Mac and browser, verifier library, dashboard and pendant status plumbing, and failure-injection tests for disconnects between side effect and receipt.
changes.risk: A bad verifier could delay a genuinely completed action or a retry could duplicate an external side effect. Recover with idempotency keys, per-action irreversible gates, explicit unknown outcome state, conservative expiry, and a manual reconciliation view. Roll out read-only/preflight mode first.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic state transitions and hashes; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per lifecycle for occasional cheap reconciliation, excluding vision. Storage is small append-only records plus bounded evidence metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 0.5–2 seconds for preflight and evidence checks; avoids 20–45 second doomed browser waits observed in failed jobs. Reconnect resume is event-driven rather than polling.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by scoping retries to a session/tab and approval lease, minimizing private page contents in relay logs, and making cancellation/expiry auditable. Requires careful encryption/access control for evidence metadata.
depends_on: Browser bridge reconnect and typed completion events
Mac bridge readiness endpoint that reports permissions without exposing unrelated screen content
Durable relay job runner
Per-action evidence schemas and irreversible-action approval policy
Pendant status/cancel protocol

changes.change: Add an execution preflight barrier and resumable handoff protocol before any action job runs. The relay creates a durable job with a step-level idempotency key, required-surface contract, and approval class. Mac agent reports signed readiness (bridge/browser online, accessibility/screen-recording state, tab/session affinity, network) within a short TTL. The scheduler refuses doomed browser/computer-use steps immediately with a structured blocked receipt, parks the job, and resumes only after a heartbeat satisfies the contract. Reversible steps may retry with leases and bounded backoff; irreversible steps become approval checkpoints and are never auto-replayed. On reconnect, reconcile receipts by idempotency key before continuing, then push a concise result to the pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets fewer mysterious failures and no duplicate clicks, sends, or purchases. A command given while walking away from the Mac remains alive and finishes later, or clearly says 'waiting for Safari' instead of pretending to work.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine across relay/local agent, readiness endpoint and heartbeat, receipt reconciliation, scheduler, pendant notification, and dashboard views; integration tests for disconnect/reconnect and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A stale readiness claim could still cause a failed step, and incorrect idempotency classification could skip needed work. Use short TTLs, explicit terminal states, per-step receipts, and manual recovery for uncertain outcomes. Roll back by disabling parked-job retries while preserving receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage/queue cost; background model calls only for human-readable summaries. No realtime call per retry.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 0.5–2 seconds preflight when healthy, but avoids current ~45-second dead waits and makes offline cases immediate.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by enforcing local execution for private data, scoped leases, approval gates, and no replay of irreversible actions; relay sees metadata rather than page contents.
depends_on: Durable job runner and browser queue primitives
A readiness/heartbeat contract emitted by Mac bridge and browser extension
Persistent receipt ledger with idempotency-key lookup
Pendant push or polling for job status

changes.change: Add a dependency-aware cross-surface action coordinator. Accept an action graph whose nodes declare required surface, reachability/permission prerequisites, reversibility, expiry, and approval. Run deterministic preflight probes before dispatch; execute ready nodes, persist blocked nodes with reason and retry policy, resume when heartbeats/permissions return, and emit one signed receipt containing per-node status and evidence. Reconcile and expire orphaned browser commands instead of leaving pendingCommands stranded.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request will either finish, continue safely while they are away, or explain the exact blocker immediately. The owner no longer has to know whether to open Safari, grant a Mac permission, or repeat a command.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema, relay D1 state machine, Mac/browser adapters, receipt UI and pendant event mapping; staged rollout can begin with read-only preflight and no new execution powers.
changes.risk: A bad fallback could perform work on an unintended surface or retry twice. Require idempotency keys, tab/session binding, explicit approval inheritance, node-level leases, and dead-letter state; recover by canceling the graph and exposing receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and request overhead; deterministic probes dominate, with no extra LLM call for ordinary routing. Optional background planner call only for ambiguous fallback.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <1 s preflight, but removes current long timeout failures; retries happen asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by refusing actions when permissions/session identity are uncertain; receipts must redact URLs, page text, and tokens. Never treat browser-online as authorization for irreversible actions.
depends_on: Shared typed context/action schema
Durable relay job runner
Browser request IDs and session affinity
Mac readiness/permission status endpoint
Pendant event delivery and owner-facing receipt

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface action envelope and lease protocol. Each spoken intent becomes a durable record {intentId, idempotencyKey, sensitivity, requiredCapabilities, approvalState, expiry, currentStep, ownerDevice}; executors (Mac, browser bridge, pendant) claim short leases and heartbeat them. Every step writes a typed receipt with input hash, target surface/session, before/after evidence, retryability, and undo reference. On reconnect, reconcile by idempotency key rather than replaying blindly; on lease expiry, pause steps marked irreversible and resume only after fresh capability/session checks.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A task will not vanish or run twice when the Mac sleeps, Wi‑Fi drops, or Safari reconnects. The owner gets an honest answer—done, paused for approval, or safely awaiting a device—instead of a vague failure, and can resume from the pendant without repeating completed work.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and D1/R2 persistence, relay scheduler, adapters in Mac and browser harnesses, pendant notification protocol, dashboard timeline, and failure-injection tests.
changes.risk: A bad reconciliation rule could duplicate an external action or falsely report completion. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit irreversible checkpoints, lease expiry pauses, append-only receipts, and a kill switch. Recover by marking the envelope conflicted and requiring owner review rather than guessing.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and periodic heartbeat traffic; background model calls only for decomposition/receipt compression (~$0.01–$0.08/task). No realtime call during waiting or retries.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; 0–30 seconds to resume after a device reconnect depending on polling/heartbeat. Extra preflight checks add roughly 100–500 ms before each external side effect.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding work to device/session identity, limiting data to the executor that needs it, expiring stale approvals, and recording provenance. Requires careful protection of intent records and approval tokens.
depends_on: Pendant offline intent spool
Durable job runner and browser command queue
Typed context projection with sensitivity/TTL
Mac/browser capability and session-health handshake
Owner approval and undo UI

changes.change: Add a cross-surface Action Commit Protocol between faculty-judgement, faculty-action, faculty-perception, relay, Mac, and browser: every delegated intent becomes a versioned action bundle with (1) required capabilities and live readiness snapshot, (2) explicit preconditions/evidence fingerprints, (3) an idempotency key and short execution lease, (4) a prepare phase that gathers reversible edits/drafts without committing, (5) a commit phase routed to the physically appropriate hand, and (6) mandatory postcondition verification by perception before reporting success. If readiness changes or evidence is stale, action pauses and returns a typed 'needs replan' packet rather than attempting blind GUI work. Relay persists bundles/checkpoints while the Mac is asleep or disconnected; the pendant receives only concise approval/blocked/completed prompts. This is not another receipt/undo log: it closes the judgement-to-action-to-perception loop and gives each side a shared contract.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say 'do it' and trust that the system either completes the real-world change or clearly says what blocked it. They will stop hearing success for work that merely queued, hit an offline browser, or lacked Accessibility/Screen Recording; drafts and reversible preparation can survive leaving the Mac, and a changed page or stale calendar entry triggers re-check instead of a wrong submission.
changes.effort: High: shared JSON schema and state machine in relay/local-agent, capability/readiness adapters for Mac and browser, durable D1 checkpoints, perception verification hooks, pendant push states, and migration of existing execute/jobs/routines. Start with reminders and browser form drafts before irreversible transactions.
changes.risk: A stuck lease could leave an action paused; recover with lease expiry, explicit cancel, and idempotent replay. Verification can fail after a successful external side effect, so report 'committed but unverified' and retain evidence rather than retrying automatically. Do not expose page contents or secrets to the relay unless required; browser private data stays on the Mac bridge. Require fresh owner confirmation at commit for sending, purchasing, deleting, or publishing.
changes.cost_impact: Small per-action D1 writes and Mac/relay network traffic; background verification uses a cheap text model, with realtime used only for the spoken clarification/approval. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for readiness and postcondition checks on local actions; browser tasks may add one page read. Long jobs remain asynchronous with pendant push updates.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety through capability declarations, freshness bounds, least-privilege routing, commit gating, and auditable evidence. Treat action bundles as sensitive; encrypt or minimize private page fields and never put auth cookies in relay state.
depends_on: A typed readiness/reconciliation contract for Mac Accessibility, Screen Recording, and browser bridge health
Shared provenance/evidence capsule IDs usable by perception and action
Durable delegated-job checkpoints and pendant push notifications
A confirmation policy for irreversible commits

changes.change: Add a cross-surface ActionProof protocol. At planning time, faculty-judgement emits an immutable action_id and a typed postcondition (surface, locator or query, expected normalized value/hash, deadline, and privacy class). faculty-action records pre-state, dispatches to Mac or browser with idempotency_key=action_id, and returns executor_result without labeling completion. faculty-perception performs a fresh read on the declared surface, compares it to the postcondition, and emits signed proof or contradiction. Relay owns a durable state machine with bounded retries and an offline pendant notification queue; dashboard renders the evidence chain and exposes retry/undo where supported.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets honest, low-noise completion: “calendar event moved to 3pm—verified” rather than “I tried.” If the browser closes, Mac sleeps, or a site silently rejects a form, the pendant reports “not verified” and keeps working instead of leaving the owner to discover the failure later.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine, adapters for typed Mac/browser reads, relay persistence and retry scheduling, privacy-aware evidence storage, and pendant notification integration. Start with reminders and one browser form flow before generalizing.
changes.risk: A stale cache or weak locator could produce a false proof; require fresh reads, timestamps, surface affinity, and an explicit unknown state. Retries could duplicate side effects, so only retry operations carrying an idempotency key or a verified undo path. If verification is unavailable, preserve the executor receipt but say unknown. Recovery is a bounded retry or owner-directed recheck.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay/database/storage cost; approximately $0.005–$0.03 per verification-heavy job, dominated by ambiguous page interpretation. Evidence retention should default to hashes/snippets and expire quickly.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one fresh read, typically 0.5–3 seconds on Mac/browser; background retries do not block the initial acknowledgement. Complex pages may take up to the declared deadline.
changes.security_impact: Action proofs can reveal private values. Encrypt evidence in transit and at rest, minimize to normalized fields/hashes, apply sensitivity TTLs, and require explicit confirmation before any retry that might be externally visible.
depends_on: A durable browser command queue with request IDs and tab/session affinity
Typed readiness/reconciliation for Mac and browser surfaces
A pendant completion-notification and offline queue path
A provenance-aware context/evidence projection rather than raw page dumps

changes.change: Add an ActionLease service implementing a two-phase commit for owner-approved actions. A lease stores actionId, target/surface affinity, precondition digest, expected postcondition, privacy class, reversibility, confirmation nonce, deadline, and attempt number. The relay durably queues only the redacted lease, sends it to the pendant, rejects replay/late confirmations, and forwards a commit token to the Mac/browser executor. The executor must acquire the token, re-perceive the same target, execute, then submit before/after evidence; a verifier returns VERIFIED, FAILED, or UNKNOWN. On timeout, disconnect, target drift, or UNKNOWN, the lease expires without action and the pendant receives a durable alert.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: An instruction like “send this to Alex” cannot accidentally go to the wrong Alex or a changed web form while the owner is away. The owner gets a clear pending confirmation and a trustworthy answer about what actually happened, rather than a success message based only on a click.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and verifier, relay D1 tables/expiry worker, Mac/browser gate integration, pendant notification protocol, and end-to-end fault-injection tests.
changes.risk: A false precondition match could still permit a wrong action; mitigate with target identity plus content/DOM digests and mandatory postcondition verification. Lost acknowledgements must be idempotent. If verifier cannot establish truth, report UNKNOWN and never claim success. Roll out first for reversible Mac actions and drafts, then gated browser writes.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible relay/D1 overhead; one compact background verification call when semantic comparison is needed, typically <$0.01. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for fresh perception and verification; confirmation delivery should be sub-second on LTE/Mac-online paths. Offline actions wait for reconnect and lease expiry rather than running blind.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding confirmation to nonce, target, and expiry and minimizing relay data. Requires careful redaction and secure storage of nonce/evidence; never put private page contents in push payloads.
depends_on: Typed ActionProof contract agreed with faculty-judgement and faculty-perception
Durable relay job/notification delivery and pendant push acknowledgement
Browser command queue with tab/session affinity and Mac executor receipt APIs
A fresh observation endpoint that can verify target and postcondition

changes.change: Add a challenge-aware execution protocol shared by browser bridge, Mac job runner, relay, and pendant: jobs become checkpointed state machines; the browser emits auth_challenge {jobId, tabId, sessionId, origin, kind, nonce, expiresAt} before any mutation, relay presents only a redacted prompt, the pendant returns signed approve/cancel for that nonce, and browser emits auth_resolved without secret contents. Resume requires same tab/session/origin, a fresh idempotency key, and a final receipt; timeout or navigation invalidates the lease and invokes cleanup.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A long task can survive the exact moment a private website asks the owner to prove identity, instead of failing, looping, or asking them to paste a secret into the AI. The owner handles the sensitive step locally and gets the finished result with a trustworthy record.
changes.effort: Medium-high: protocol types and persistence, extension event/UI, relay prompt plumbing, pendant interaction, and integration tests for 2FA/passkey/CAPTCHA/timeout/duplicate submission.
changes.risk: A stale or forged completion could resume the wrong tab or submit twice. Mitigate with origin+session binding, nonce expiry, signed pendant response, idempotency keys, and mandatory final receipt. If any check fails, abort rather than continue; recovery is an explicit retry from the last checkpoint.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible inference cost; modest durable event/receipt storage and browser polling. No credential data leaves the browser.
changes.latency_impact: Adds less than 1 second for challenge detection and roughly 1–3 seconds after local completion to resume.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by keeping OTPs, passkeys, and CAPTCHA contents local. Adds a new signed control path that must be nonce-bound and origin-bound; redact challenge screenshots/text by default.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner and authenticated tab/session affinity
Typed action receipts and idempotency/undo ledger
Pendant local button/prompt protocol
Browser extension heartbeat and command/result queue

changes.change: Add an execution-admission and evidence chain in the action runner. Before each step, compile a typed preflight from live /ops/status + /observe (surface, permissions, online state, target/session, reversibility), and reject or reroute any step whose actuator is not reachable: UI clicks/typing/keys are refused when Accessibility/inputReachability is false; screenshot-dependent steps are refused when Screen Recording is absent; browser work is parked with a durable retry receipt when the extension is offline; AppleScript/shell alternatives are selected only when their declared postcondition is independently observable. Require each write step to carry the signed Evidence-to-Effect envelope (scope, expiry, idempotency key, expected postcondition, revocation reference), then append preflight, effect, independent observation, and recovery/expiry records to the existing job journal. Never report success for an unobserved UI effect.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will stop claiming that something happened when the Mac or browser could not physically receive the action. Instead it will say exactly what is blocked, preserve the work, retry when the required surface returns, and provide a verifiable before/after receipt—especially important for messages, forms, reminders, and other real-world changes.
changes.effort: Medium-high: action-runner admission middleware, typed envelope verifier/revocation lookup, readiness watcher, durable retry state machine, and adapters for /observe and /browser/status; add fault-injection tests for permission loss, disconnects, duplicate retries, and stale leases.
changes.risk: A conservative gate may defer legitimate actions and existing callers may lack postconditions. Recover by allowing explicitly declared non-UI actions with their own evidence provider, exposing a reason-coded blocked receipt, and replaying only idempotent steps after readiness returns. Keep the current journal and undo endpoints backward-compatible.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; mostly local CPU/storage. A slower model is unnecessary—the planner supplies the envelope and deterministic middleware verifies it.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly one local status/observation read per step (tens to hundreds of ms); disconnected work returns immediately as queued rather than waiting 45 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety and auditability: least-scope, expiry, idempotency, and revocation are checked before writes; sensitive page data remains on the Mac/browser bridge. Must protect signing keys and avoid logging raw form/email contents in receipts.
depends_on: faculty-judgement's signed Evidence-to-Effect envelope schema and revocation/explain endpoint
a durable non-blocking browser command poller (replace the current 45-second wait)
mac_readonly_inspect implementation or equivalent typed observation provider
readiness transition events from the Mac bridge and browser extension

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface Action Envelope and blocked-state protocol. The relay accepts a plan only as versioned, step-scoped records containing idempotency key, target surface/session, side-effect class, preconditions with freshness TTL, checkpoint receipt, expiry, and resume policy. It transitions parked→leased→running→blocked→resumed→completed/expired, publishes readiness-triggered wakeups, and rejects stale or duplicate leases. Mac and browser bridges must acknowledge each checkpoint before the next step is dispatched.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a reliable answer instead of a mysterious timeout: 'waiting for Browser Bridge; nothing changed' followed by automatic continuation when it is back. Completed work is never repeated, and a dropped Mac or browser connection does not lose the request.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and migration, D1 state machine, heartbeat-to-event adapter, bridge checkpoint APIs, and dashboard/pendant status. Add fault-injection tests for disconnects between every step.
changes.risk: A bad resume policy could repeat an external write or resume against a changed page. Default all writes to non-resumable, require stable target fingerprints and idempotency, expire envelopes, and provide cancel. Recover orphaned leases by timeout and mark uncertain effects for inspection rather than retrying.
changes.cost_impact: Low relay storage/CPU; roughly a few D1 rows and events per step. One cheap model call only when a failed step needs re-planning; no model cost for normal wakeups.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second park acknowledgement; wakeup on the next heartbeat rather than a blocking 45-second request. Additional checkpoint round trips add roughly 100–500 ms per step.
changes.security_impact: The envelope must exclude secrets and page bodies, bind to the paired device/session, enforce capability scopes, and cryptographically correlate receipts to the originating intent. Dashboard should redact sensitive target values.
depends_on: A readiness-event contract from faculty-perception
A durable resumable job runner (not just the current jobs JSON)
Non-blocking browser progress/resumable polling
An owner policy defining which side-effect classes may auto-resume

changes.change: Add a cross-surface compensation ledger rather than extending the existing last-job undo. Every action adapter must publish an effect record with stable target fingerprint, before/after capsule reference, inverse operation (or explicitly irreversible), dependency edges, and confidence. A coordinator computes a previewable compensation DAG, pauses on uncertain effects, and executes only owner-approved inverse nodes in dependency-safe order across Mac, browser, relay storage, and generated pendant artifacts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can recover an entire multi-device task coherently instead of being left with a browser draft, a changed Mac file, and an orphaned relay artifact after undoing only one step.
changes.effort: High: adapter contracts for each surface, encrypted receipt/capsule storage, dependency-aware compensation engine, fingerprint validation, and pendant/dashboard preview plus approval.
changes.risk: An incorrect inverse could destroy newer user changes or create duplicate external effects. Require exact target/version matching, preserve current state as a recovery snapshot, stop on any mismatch, and treat irreversible or uncertain effects as manual follow-up rather than auto-compensating.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate storage for encrypted before/after capsules and receipts; low compute. Planner-model cost only for explaining or resolving ambiguous inverse candidates.
changes.latency_impact: Normal actions gain a small receipt-write overhead (tens of milliseconds). Undo preview is seconds; execution is asynchronous so it does not block the voice session.
changes.security_impact: Receipts may contain sensitive browser and file metadata; encrypt capsules, minimize retention, bind them to the paired owner identity, and redact values in spoken/dashboard summaries.
depends_on: Typed effect adapters for Mac, browser, relay artifacts, and pendant output
A durable cross-surface job identity and receipt correlation mechanism
Owner policy for irreversible effects and compensation approval

changes.change: Add an append-only Action Truth Ledger and verifier coordinator. Each planned step gets a stable job/step id, idempotency key, intended mutation, deadline, and machine-readable postcondition. The coordinator records dispatch, receipt, verification, retry, blocked, and unknown states separately; after every mutation it schedules a read-back through browser or Mac and stores minimal evidence references (surface, URL/path, timestamp, hash, short quote). A job is complete only when all required postconditions are verified; otherwise it remains partial/unknown and is safely resumable.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing “done” when only a command was sent. They get a precise answer—verified, partially verified, blocked, or unknown—with enough evidence to continue safely after a disconnect, without duplicate submissions.
changes.effort: Medium/high: schema and durable storage, adapters for browser/Mac typed reads, verifier rules, retry/recovery semantics, receipt API, dashboard/pendant rendering, and integration tests using forced disconnects and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A verifier may miss a valid change or a site may expose stale cached state; use bounded re-read attempts, freshness timestamps, and explicit unknown status. Ledger growth needs retention and redaction. Recovery is replay from the last durable step, never blind whole-job replay.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2/storage and network overhead per step; occasional cheap background-model call only for unstructured confirmation text. No realtime-model requirement.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one read-back round trip per mutation (typically 0.5–5 seconds); can verify independent steps in parallel while preserving dependencies.
changes.security_impact: Evidence is minimized and redacted; private page text remains local where possible. Irreversible actions require a fresh consent lease checked by the coordinator, and ledger access must be authenticated/audited.
depends_on: durable relay job runner
typed browser/Mac action and read adapters
cross-surface consent lease
fresh reachability/permission probes
pendant receipt/status transport

changes.change: Add a reachability-and-proof preflight barrier to every faculty-action job. Before dispatch, query Mac readiness (Accessibility/Screen Recording), browser bridge heartbeat/tab affinity, relay connectivity, and pendant link; classify each planned step as executable, queueable, or blocked. For blocked steps, fail in under 2 seconds with the exact missing surface and a one-tap recovery instruction instead of waiting 45 seconds. On reconnect, resume only idempotent queued steps under a short action lease, then attach before/after evidence and an honest receipt; never emit success from a plan or an unverified GUI attempt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today a browser request can burn nearly a minute and still report only that the extension is offline, while GUI permissions can make a visual result untrustworthy. The owner gets fast, truthful answers, automatic continuation after a dropped link, and no accidental duplicate actions.
changes.effort: Medium: typed readiness contract in Mac agent/relay, preflight middleware in job runner, browser heartbeat integration, idempotency/lease persistence, and pendant LED/voice status mapping; add integration tests for offline, reconnect, and permission-denied cases.
changes.risk: A stale readiness result could incorrectly block or resume work. Use short TTLs, recheck immediately before each side effect, persist lease ownership, and default to blocked on uncertainty. Recovery is cancel/retry from the receipt UI; irreversible steps still require explicit confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost (small status probes); roughly 1–2 KB metadata per job/receipt in local JSON or D1.
changes.latency_impact: Adds ~100–400 ms when surfaces are healthy, but turns current 45-second browser timeouts into <2-second actionable failures.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing untrusted GUI success and duplicate retries; readiness metadata must not include page contents or secrets, and leases must be scoped to the paired owner/device.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo storage
chg-14accc01 browser request IDs and tab affinity
browser heartbeat/poll route
relay-to-Mac authenticated pairing

changes.change: Design the production pendant with a small haptic actuator and a secure element alongside the button/LED. The relay issues a one-time transaction challenge; the pendant verifies the challenge, renders a distinct vibration pattern, and signs the owner's deliberate button gesture with a device key. Mac/browser actions accept the signature only when it matches the exact preview hash and expiry, while the relay records the signed authorization and final receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can safely approve a consequential action while walking, driving, or away from a screen: a tactile pattern tells them this is an approval request rather than ordinary conversation, and a physical gesture cannot be forged by replaying audio. The same pendant can prove which exact action they approved.
changes.effort: High: choose a production wearable MCU/secure-element design, add haptic and power drivers, implement challenge signing and anti-replay firmware, expose verification through relay and Mac/browser executors, and validate usability and battery life.
changes.risk: A lost pendant or compromised pairing could authorize actions. Require physical re-pairing, key revocation, short-lived challenges, local lockout after repeated failures, and server-side confirmation of preview hash, owner/device pair, and expiry. Firmware update and recovery-key procedures are required.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 incremental BOM for secure element, haptic motor, driver, and mechanical changes; modest battery impact from brief haptic pulses and cryptographic operations; negligible per-action API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–300 ms for challenge verification/signature validation, with immediate tactile feedback before network execution.
changes.security_impact: Moves high-risk authorization from replayable voice to hardware-backed user presence, without sending private page contents to the pendant. Requires secure manufacturing, key provisioning, revocation, and signed firmware updates.
depends_on: A typed transaction preview and risk classifier
Relay challenge/nonce service
Mac/browser executor verification gate
Signed firmware update and device-pairing infrastructure

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface Reachability Contract and blocked-job coordinator. Mac emits signed, expiring proofs for input posting (host bundle + executable identity + probe result), screen capture, and browser heartbeat/tab ownership. The relay stores an approved job as held when any required proof is absent, while the Mac/browser layers stop claiming success and attach a machine-readable blocker. A repair transition (owner-guided permission deep link or extension-open instruction) causes re-probe; only a fresh proof matching the original session/tab and idempotency key permits replay. Irreversible steps remain approval-gated and are never auto-replayed.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing “done” when nothing happened, and a dropped browser extension or mismatched macOS grant no longer loses a multi-step task. They get a clear pendant explanation, can fix one thing, and the exact safe portion resumes without duplicate sends or clicks.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine in relay/Mac agent, browser heartbeat changes, pendant status events, dashboard diagnostics, and failure/replay tests across offline transitions.
changes.risk: A stale or incorrectly scoped proof could permit an action on the wrong tab or binary; mitigate with short TTLs, tab/session binding, nonce probes, fail-closed defaults, and manual approval for writes. Recovery is to expire the held job and present its plan rather than replay.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible relay/D1 storage and local polling; one short realtime explanation when blocked. Engineering cost is the main cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local probe/heartbeat round (typically <1 s) before action execution; held jobs resume within a few seconds after proof transition.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making identity and reachability explicit; no permission is silently granted and no private page data leaves the Mac for diagnosis.
depends_on: Mac inputReachability proof API
browser heartbeat with command/session acknowledgements
durable relay-to-Mac job state and idempotency keys
pendant blocked/resume event protocol

changes.change: Extend the implemented action-receipt system with a provenance-aware stale-plan precommit gate. For every irreversible or externally visible step, persist draft provenance (source URL/tab or file/app, extraction timestamp, normalized field/value hashes, and plan fingerprint). Immediately before execution, faculty-action asks faculty-perception to re-read only those sources; compare fingerprints and required fields. If any source is unavailable or changed, pause the job, mark the step stale, retain the draft and evidence, and send the owner a one-sentence delta plus an approve/rebuild choice. Only an explicit approval on the unchanged fingerprint may pass the gate; receipts record the checked sources, comparison result, and approval token. Keep reversible local actions executable without the gate, and make paused jobs resumable without replaying completed action IDs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A prepared email, form, purchase, or settings change will not silently use yesterday's price, recipient, appointment time, or page state. The owner gets a concise explanation and can approve the exact unchanged transaction or have it rebuilt.
changes.effort: Medium: typed provenance schema and persistence, precommit hook in executor, perception refresh RPC, pause/resume job states, dashboard/pendant prompt, and tests for changed/unavailable sources and retry idempotency.
changes.risk: A flaky source could pause a legitimate action; fail closed and offer rebuild. Never send the original draft after a mismatch. Recovery is resume after explicit approval or discard the paused job; completed reversible steps remain undoable via existing receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Small extra storage and one bounded perception/read request per gated step; use a cheaper text model for fingerprint comparison and reserve realtime only for the spoken alert.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly one source-read round trip (typically 1–3 seconds) only immediately before irreversible/external actions; no impact on read-only or reversible steps.
changes.security_impact: Provenance stores hashes and minimal snippets rather than full private page contents; source access remains in the existing authenticated browser/Mac boundary. Approval tokens are single-use and bound to job, step, and fingerprint.
depends_on: faculty-judgement emits durable draft provenance and requests the gate
faculty-perception supports targeted re-read with source identity and freshness
job state machine supports paused/stale/resume states
existing actionReceipts.js and undo.js remain the receipt/compensation layer

changes.change: Add a proof-carrying action contract between faculty-judgement and faculty-action. Each decision is compiled into a typed ActionPlan containing target surface, ordered steps, reversibility class, preconditions, expected postconditions, freshness TTL, idempotency key, and required evidence (API response, filesystem hash, app state, or browser DOM citation). Before execution, faculty-action performs a cheap live preflight across the relevant hands: Mac reachability/Accessibility, browser heartbeat and tab affinity, relay/pendant connectivity, and permission state. It routes around unavailable hands only when the plan explicitly permits a fallback; otherwise it returns a structured blocked receipt without attempting no-op GUI actions. After each step it verifies postconditions and emits a signed receipt chain linking plan hash, observed evidence, and timestamps; stale leases or lost reachability automatically stop subsequent steps. Reversible plans remain proactive; irreversible plans execute only with a judgement-issued approval token, not an action-agent guess.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing 'done' when Mac UI actions actually did nothing (the current machine reports Accessibility=false and input reachability failed), and gets an exact explanation of what was executed, what was proven, and where the plan stopped. Multi-step work can safely span pendant, relay, Mac, and logged-in browser without silently continuing after a disconnected or stale hand.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared ActionPlan/receipt schema, preflight adapters for Mac/browser/relay, lease and idempotency storage, verification implementations for common action types, and dashboard/pendant-readable blocked receipts. Requires coordination with judgement and each surface.
changes.risk: Over-strict postconditions could falsely stop useful work; recover by classifying evidence as required vs best-effort and allowing explicit plan-level fallback. Network loss may leave an external action committed but receipt delayed; idempotency keys and reconciliation scans handle retries. Never treat a tool's success boolean as proof. Approval tokens must be scoped, single-use, and expiry-bound.
changes.cost_impact: Small background-model/worker overhead for compiling and verifying contracts; avoids expensive realtime retries and duplicate external actions. Storage is a few KB per action chain plus optional evidence hashes (raw private page content should remain local).
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for preflight and per-step verification on healthy local surfaces; blocked actions return faster than futile GUI loops. Long browser work remains asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves least privilege and auditability: plans declare surfaces and evidence, receipts omit secrets, approval tokens are scoped, and private browser evidence stays on the Mac unless explicitly requested. Prevents acting through an untrusted/offline extension or false GUI receipt.
depends_on: A shared schema/versioning owner across faculty-judgement and faculty-action
A relay event/receipt channel that can deliver blocked/completed status to the pendant
Browser bridge heartbeat plus durable command idempotency and tab/session affinity
Mac permission/reachability probe exposed as a machine-readable preflight result
A policy defining which action classes are reversible and which require owner approval

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface ActionTransaction protocol shared by faculty-judgement, faculty-action, Mac agent, browser bridge, relay, and pendant. Each transaction contains an immutable plan hash, step dependency graph, lease owner/expiry, idempotency key, precondition snapshot, and typed receipt (queued/running/blocked/completed/verified/unknown) with evidence and trust. Relay persists it; late or duplicate receipts reconcile deterministically; pendant receives progress and blocked reasons. Irreversible steps cannot transition to verified without fresh before/after proof and the required owner confirmation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A single request that spans private browser tabs, Mac apps, and a long-running relay job will stop appearing mysteriously half-done. The owner gets one truthful spoken status, can leave and return, safely resume after a dropped connection, and know exactly which step happened and which did not.
changes.effort: Medium-high: protocol/types, D1 persistence, adapters in Mac/browser/relay, pendant progress states, test fixtures for duplicate/late/permission-loss receipts.
changes.risk: A schema or reconciliation bug could suppress a needed retry or falsely merge two actions. Mitigate with append-only events, plan-hash/idempotency validation, lease expiry to blocked (never automatic replay of irreversible steps), and migration behind read-only shadow logging first.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay storage and bandwidth increase per step; deterministic processing is negligible. One concise background summarization call per completed multi-step transaction if a spoken brief is needed; no realtime call per receipt.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local queued state; relay push under 1 second normally. Verification waits for evidence rather than timing out into a success claim.
changes.security_impact: Evidence is scoped to its surface and sensitivity; private page text stays local unless explicitly allowed. Leases expire, confirmation tokens are one-time and bound to plan hash/step, and untrusted receipts are visible as such.
depends_on: faculty-judgement preflight verdict contract
common evidence envelope and verify_action_proof tool
relay durable job/event persistence and push to pendant
Mac Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions
live authenticated browser extension bridge

changes.change: Add an Action Lease Coordinator between judgement and all execution surfaces. Persist a lease record keyed by jobId/actionHash with owner approval timestamp, exact action scope, target surface/session, expiry (default 10 minutes), one-use nonce, risk class, and state (issued/claimed/running/committed/succeeded/failed/expired/revoked). Require Mac and browser workers to claim with a readiness attestation; reject claims when the bridge is offline or Mac permissions are not ready. Stream state transitions to the pendant and dashboard, and make every transition idempotent.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: An action they approved will either finish predictably or stop safely with a clear reason instead of timing out after 45 seconds, sitting in a stale browser queue, or being retried after circumstances changed.
changes.effort: Medium: D1 schema/API and relay tests; adapters in local-agent job runner and browser bridge; pendant notification messages; dashboard timeline. Add fault-injection tests for disconnects, duplicate claims, expired leases, and commit/retry races.
changes.risk: A too-short lease could interrupt a legitimate long task; use progress heartbeats without extending the absolute deadline. A lost completion packet could make the pendant say 'unknown'; receipts remain queryable and the relay replays terminal state. Never treat a worker heartbeat as owner reapproval.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; a few D1 writes per action and tiny telemetry payloads. Optional background summarization remains bounded.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one deterministic claim/preflight round (typically <200 ms locally, <1 s relay round trip) but avoids long doomed execution attempts.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by binding execution to the approved action hash, target session, nonce, and deadline; lease records must avoid storing secrets and support owner revocation.
depends_on: Structured readiness endpoint from Mac agent (Accessibility, Screen Recording, browser bridge polling, and target session)
Shared action/receipt schema across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant
Pendant firmware notification and offline approval event support

changes.change: Introduce a resumable Human-in-the-loop Checkpoint protocol spanning local-agent jobs, browser sessions, relay, and pendant. A worker can emit a checkpoint containing a stable job/action hash, bounded question, typed choices or a redacted input schema, evidence capsule, continuation token, deadline, and safe rollback point. Relay persists and delivers it; pendant returns a nonce-bound response; the worker resumes only if the checkpoint hash and target session still match. Add crash recovery, duplicate-response handling, expiry, cancellation, and a dashboard timeline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave the Mac during a difficult task and answer only the one decision that genuinely requires them, rather than babysitting the screen or restarting the entire workflow after a harmless ambiguity.
changes.effort: High: define a serializable continuation contract for shell, GUI, and browser steps; implement relay storage and pendant transport; add resume adapters and fault-injection tests for worker/relay/device disconnects.
changes.risk: Some actions cannot safely resume after a crash; those checkpoints must be marked non-resumable and restart from a verified boundary. A malformed or stale response must fail closed. Never expose raw passwords or page contents in a prompt unless explicitly classified and encrypted.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring cost while waiting; one compact background-model call per checkpoint to phrase choices, plus small durable storage. Reusing evidence capsules avoids resending full context.
changes.latency_impact: Adds sub-second deterministic checkpoint persistence and response validation; resumption depends on the worker's next preflight, typically a few seconds.
changes.security_impact: Responses are scoped to a checkpoint nonce, action hash, target browser session, and expiry. The relay stores redacted prompt metadata and encrypted sensitive input only when required; every pause, response, and resume is auditable.
depends_on: A common typed job/evidence schema shared by Mac and browser workers
Pendant transport supporting push notifications and compact response events
Relay durable state and replay of pending checkpoints
Worker-specific safe-boundary and continuation adapters

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution-readiness handshake and lease. Before any approved action, the relay asks Mac agent for a signed preflight containing Accessibility/Screen Recording readiness, browser-heartbeat freshness, target tab/session affinity, and current queue capacity. If a required surface is unavailable, persist the approved intent as a paused job with an expiry and cancellation token; the relay retries on heartbeat recovery, while the pendant announces 'waiting for browser' and a long-press cancels. Emit one terminal receipt with preflight failures, retry timestamps, and the exact action outcome—never a client-side timeout masquerading as failure.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A spoken request will either complete across the Mac and private browser or clearly wait and recover when the missing surface comes back. The owner no longer has to guess whether an action happened, repeat it after a timeout, or discover stale browser commands later; they can cancel from the pendant.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight schema and signed lease in relay/Mac agent, heartbeat-triggered retry worker, pending-job UI/status, pendant notification/cancel mapping, and failure-injection tests for permissions/browser dropouts.
changes.risk: A paused approved action could execute later than expected; enforce short leases, action-class expiry, idempotency keys, and require reconfirmation for destructive actions after any suspension. Recover by cancellation and receipt audit; never auto-retry send/delete/purchase classes.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic checks and retry orchestration; only invoke a model for ambiguous recovery messaging. Small D1/JSON state growth per pending job and heartbeat.
changes.latency_impact: Adds sub-second preflight when healthy; unavailable surfaces return immediately as paused instead of waiting ~45s for a browser timeout. Recovery latency is heartbeat cadence plus action execution.
changes.security_impact: Signed, scoped leases prevent replay and bind intent to a specific Mac/browser session; receipts must avoid page secrets. Requires explicit owner policy for which reversible classes may resume automatically.
depends_on: Enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent
Bring Browser Bridge extension online and polling
Durable job runner and receipt/undo storage

changes.change: Add a durable deferred-action envelope and reconnect executor spanning pendant→relay→Mac/browser. Envelope fields: jobId, idempotencyKey, origin, typed steps, required capabilities, confirmation class, lease/deadline, dependency IDs, redacted target fingerprint, and status. Relay claims exactly once, Mac bridge heartbeats capability readiness, local agent executes only when prerequisites are true, and each step emits proof-of-effect or an explicit unverifiable result. Reconnect drains in dependency order; expired or capability-blocked jobs remain visible rather than being silently retried.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request made while wearing the pendant no longer disappears when LTE drops, the Mac sleeps, or Safari is unavailable—and the owner hears the difference between completed, skipped, and merely attempted.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay D1 schema/worker, local-agent queue and typed proof adapters, pendant compact spool protocol, dashboard state UI, and end-to-end fault-injection tests for duplicate delivery and sleep/reconnect.
changes.risk: A retry could duplicate a side effect; prevent this with idempotency keys, per-step leases, and no automatic execution of confirmation-class actions. If proof fails, stop and report unverified. Recover by exposing cancel/undo where supported and retaining receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible relay storage/compute; background planner calls only for ambiguous plans. Optional vision verification adds screenshot/model cost per difficult step.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on live conversation; offline capture is immediate. Reconnect adds queue polling (target <30 s) and proof latency (typically <10 s).
changes.security_impact: Encrypted paired-device transport, least-privilege capability claims, redacted targets, short retention for proof artifacts, and confirmation gates for send/delete/purchase.
depends_on: durable browser runner and authenticated session reattachment
Mac bridge heartbeat exposing readiness/permission state
typed action receipts plus proof adapters
pendant offline envelope storage

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface Action Lease + Attestation protocol. Relay creates a nonce-bound lease containing plan hash, target surface/session, allowed effect class, expiry, and approval transcript hash. Before every write, Mac/browser return signed (or HMAC-authenticated) preflight evidence: online heartbeat, entitlement state, target identity, and expected-state digest. Executor refuses on stale/mismatched evidence. After execution, faculty-perception submits independent postcondition evidence; receipts become succeeded, refused, or unknown rather than treating dispatch as success. Pendant announces the exact reason and offers retry only after readiness changes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely say “do it” while walking away and trust that the system either changed the intended thing or clearly said it could not. It prevents today's known failure mode where GUI actions are dispatched while Accessibility/Screen Recording are off and the browser is offline.
changes.effort: Medium-high: protocol schema and durable lease store, relay propagation, browser heartbeat/result changes, Mac preflight adapters, verifier library, dashboard states, and integration tests for stale leases, wrong tabs, offline devices, and ambiguous outcomes.
changes.risk: A false negative may refuse a legitimate action, which is recoverable by refreshing readiness and asking again. A false positive is more serious; mitigate with nonce binding, short TTLs, target hashes, independent read-back, and default unknown on missing proof. Roll out read-only/preflight telemetry first, then reversible writes, then irreversible actions behind explicit confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage/compute overhead; deterministic checks dominate. Background reconciliation is cheap; no extra realtime model call beyond the owner's approval.
changes.latency_impact: Adds ~100–500 ms for preflight and ~1–3 s for postcondition read-back, preferable to silent incorrect execution.
changes.security_impact: Improves least privilege and replay resistance. Do not store raw approval audio or secrets; store transcript hash, lease metadata, and redacted evidence. HMAC keys must remain device-specific and rotate.
depends_on: Fresh readiness/entitlement state from faculty-perception
A relay-visible durable lease/approval record
Browser bridge heartbeat and typed result support
Mac action receipts (already implemented, but currently lack gates/preconditions)

changes.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor (or piezo haptic actuator) with a dedicated GPIO driver and a simple three-pattern status vocabulary: short pulse = lease accepted, double pulse = blocked/refused, long pulse = verified completion.
