args.user_asks: “Carry this request through all the dependent systems: if the private site accepts the change, update my Mac calendar and remind me; if it fails, leave everything untouched and tell me exactly where it stopped.”
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently ask for a single dependable real-world outcome spanning a logged-in website and local Mac state. A browser action may succeed while the calendar step is skipped, or a retry may create duplicate reminders. This capability is a compensating transaction (a saga), not merely a queued click: it commits each step only after verifying the prior step, uses idempotency keys, and performs safe compensation for already-completed reversible steps. The pendant gives one concise outcome instead of forcing the owner to reconcile several surfaces.
surfaces: faculty-judgement turns the request into a dependency graph with commit points, allowed compensations, and a final success invariant
relay-realtime persists the graph and resumes it after disconnects or Mac sleep
browser-extension reads the authenticated page, performs the approved reversible/irreversible step, and returns authoritative evidence

faculty-perception independently checks each resulting state and detects partial completion
pendant receives step-by-step progress and a final success, partial-success, or safely-rolled-back result
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for graph compilation and recovery classification; deterministic adapters perform known browser and Calendar operations. Reserve realtime for approval and concise progress, not orchestration.
args.latency_budget: Show the first plan on the pendant in under 2 seconds. Each dependent step may take seconds to minutes because sites can be eventually consistent; reconnect resumption must not restart a committed step. A stalled graph should become paused, not silently fail, after a bounded timeout.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.03 per request, mostly one planning/recovery call; deterministic execution and verification dominate latency rather than API cost. Compensation avoids costly duplicate actions and support effort.
args.security_concerns: Require approval for the exact graph and every irreversible node; bind all nodes to the original plan hash and operation id. Keep private page contents on the Mac/bridge; send only redacted values and evidence hashes to relay/pendant. Never compensate by sending a message or canceling a purchase automatically. If compensation is unsafe, stop in partial-success state and ask the owner.

Adapters that can verify authenticated browser outcomes and local Calendar/reminder outcomes without GUI permissions
A recovery worker that resumes paused graphs after reconnect and never replays committed nodes
A partial-success UI and explicit owner choices for unsafe compensation
A shared redacted evidence/receipt format across browser and Mac

args.change: Introduce a durable cross-surface saga coordinator rather than treating each Mac/browser action as an independent job. Persist a DAG of typed nodes with dependency barriers, commit markers, idempotency keys, expected postconditions, and explicit compensation policies. On reconnect, resume only the first uncommitted node; after each node, run a read-only verifier before releasing dependents. Expose partial-success and paused-for-owner states through the existing job and receipt APIs, and make unsafe compensation impossible to auto-run.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for an outcome that crosses a private website and their Mac without manually checking whether half the work happened. A site rejection will not leave a misleading calendar reminder, and a dropped connection will not duplicate a booking or reminder. When full rollback is impossible, the owner gets an honest partial result and a precise next choice.
args.effort: High integration effort: schema and durable worker first, then browser and Calendar adapters, verifier contracts, recovery tests, and pendant progress states. Start with browser-booking-to-Calendar/reminder as a narrow vertical slice.
args.risk: Some external actions cannot be undone; the coordinator must stop before those nodes unless separately approved and must surface partial completion. Eventual consistency can make a successful node look absent, so use bounded verification and never retry an ambiguous irreversible node. Recover by leaving the graph paused with its evidence and operation key.
args.cost_impact: Small durable storage and queue cost; one cheap planning or recovery call per graph ($0.002–$0.03), with deterministic steps otherwise. Verification adds browser/Mac requests but prevents duplicate side effects.
args.latency_impact: Adds verification latency between dependent steps (typically 1–5 seconds, longer for eventually consistent sites); disconnect recovery becomes reliable rather than immediate. The pendant can stream node status so the owner is not left guessing.
args.security_impact: Keep credentials and full private content on the Mac/browser surfaces. Relay stores only encrypted/redacted plan values, hashes, state transitions, and receipts. Bind every node to the owner's approval, session/tab identity, and idempotency key; require fresh approval for any compensation or newly discovered irreversible node.

args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short pendant interruption/status exchange; use a cheaper background model to reconcile journal/receipts and derive the next safe step, escalating to realtime only when the owner asks to resume or a high-consequence ambiguity remains.
args.latency_budget: Pendant should receive a compact interrupted/awaiting-verification status within 2 seconds when connected. Recovery reconciliation may take 5–20 seconds in the background; resuming an individual Mac/browser step should begin within 3 seconds after confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per interruption with a small background model; costs are dominated by rereading large browser evidence or screenshots, so persist compact step summaries and hashes rather than resending full context.
args.security_concerns: Do not claim completion from an intent or an attempted command. Store requested, attempted, witnessed, and confirmed states separately; require fresh owner confirmation before irreversible continuation; never replay a write whose receipt is ambiguous. Private URLs, page snippets, and local file paths remain on the authenticated Mac/bridge unless explicitly needed for the spoken summary.

A resume endpoint that accepts a checkpoint id and executes only the next unverified step, with stale-session and changed-page guards.
Pendant-visible pending/interrupted/disputed events and a compact confirmation interaction.
Mac and browser readback adapters that can independently verify side effects after a crash or reconnect.

args.change: Implement a durable cross-surface execution checkpoint protocol. Before each Mac or browser step, write a checkpoint containing jobId, stepId, idempotency key, consequence class, precondition hash, and expected witness. After execution, append separate attempted and witnessed receipts; on disconnect, crash, timeout, or browser-session loss, mark the step interrupted rather than retrying. Add a resume endpoint that selects only the next unverified step after fresh precondition/readback checks, and publish compact pending/interrupted/disputed/resumable events to the pendant stream. Keep the full evidence local to the Mac/bridge and send the relay only a redacted status plus checkpoint id.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection will no longer make the owner wonder whether an external action happened or risk sending it twice. They can hear 'step 2 of 4 completed; step 3 needs confirmation' and safely continue later from the pendant.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and durable storage, wrappers around mac_run_actions/browser_run_actions, reconnect reconciliation, independent readback adapters, and pendant event plumbing. Build first for reminders/files/drafts, then add external sends and purchases behind stricter confirmation.
args.risk: A bad witness adapter could falsely mark a side effect complete, or a stale precondition could block a legitimate resume. Fail closed on ambiguity, retain the interrupted state, expose evidence and an explicit repair path, and never auto-replay irreversible steps.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent journal growth (roughly 1–3 KB per step plus bounded receipt metadata); background reconciliation is low-cost. Full screenshots/page dumps should be content-addressed and retained only under existing retention policy.
args.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds before and after each step for checkpoint writes; reconnect reconciliation is asynchronous. High-consequence resume waits for readback and owner confirmation.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by separating intent, attempt, witness, and confirmation. Checkpoint records must redact secrets, encrypt private evidence at rest, bind browser checkpoints to tab/session identity, and expire resume authority after session or page changes.
depends_on: A shared typed witness/checkpoint schema and durable claim store (the evidence-quorum work proposed by faculty-judgement).
Mac/browser readback adapters for side effects.
Pendant pending/interrupted/disputed events and a confirmation control.
Existing /jobs receipts and /journal must become append-only and idempotent rather than inferred from final status.

args.user_asks: When a website or Mac app changes while you’re carrying out my task, pause at the exact changed step, tell me what changed in plain language, and let me approve a corrected plan from the pendant instead of guessing or starting over.
args.why_useful: Real tasks fail at the moment a page adds a verification challenge, changes a price, moves a button, or an app opens a different dialog. The owner should get a small, actionable interruption—what was expected, what is now present, and what the proposed correction would do—while all already-completed safe work remains intact. This is different from a generic approval prompt: it is adaptive replanning at a verified divergence point.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to compare precondition snapshots and classify the divergence; use the realtime model only to explain the delta and collect a short owner decision. Use vision only when structured DOM/accessibility or AppleScript state is insufficient.
args.latency_budget: Detect and pause within 1–2 seconds of a changed precondition. A concise pendant explanation should take under 3 seconds; after approval, resume the corrected step within 5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low for structured state diffs; roughly <$0.02 for an interruption, with vision/screenshot analysis the dominant cost and used only as fallback.
args.security_concerns: Never transmit full private page contents when a field-level diff is enough. Treat changed prices, recipients, permissions, account destinations, and security challenges as high-consequence divergence requiring explicit confirmation. Do not attempt to solve CAPTCHAs or MFA silently; display that the owner must take over.
missing: A precondition snapshot and semantic-diff schema for browser DOM, app state, and filesystem targets.
A divergence classifier that distinguishes harmless layout drift from changed intent, destination, amount, or authorization.
A pause-and-replan protocol that preserves completed steps and invalidates stale action leases.
Pendant event and response support for a compact delta with approve, edit, cancel, and take-over choices.
A Mac/browser adapter that returns stable semantic state rather than screenshots alone.

args.change: Add a divergence-aware execution interlock between planning and action. Compile every step into a semantic precondition snapshot (recipient, amount, URL/origin, selected account, target file, permission state, and stable field identifiers). Before committing a step, compare the live Mac/browser state to that snapshot. If it differs, atomically pause the job, invalidate its action lease, store a minimal redacted diff plus the last safe checkpoint, and emit a pendant decision event with approve-corrected-plan, edit, cancel, or owner-takeover options. On approval, generate a new plan revision linked to the old one; never mutate the old plan or replay prior steps.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Unexpected UI or data changes become a clear one-sentence question instead of a silent failure, wrong click, duplicate submission, or lost progress. The owner can safely approve the correction while away from the Mac and continue from where the task actually stopped.
args.effort: High: semantic state adapters for browser DOM and AppleScript-accessible Mac apps, a diff/classification service, atomic job pause/lease invalidation, plan revision storage, and pendant event/response plumbing. Start with browser forms and Mail/Calendar before general GUI vision.
args.risk: Over-sensitive diffs could interrupt harmless layout changes; under-sensitive diffs could miss a changed destination or amount. Default to pause on uncertainty, classify only from stable semantic fields, and retain a human-takeover path. Expire approvals when the page/session changes again.
args.cost_impact: Small metadata storage per step; background diffs are cheap. Vision fallback for unstructured dialogs costs more and should be sampled only after structured adapters fail.
args.latency_impact: Adds a pre-commit comparison, typically under 300 ms for structured state; an owner decision adds conversational latency only when divergence occurs.
args.security_impact: Reduces accidental disclosure and misdirected actions by keeping diffs minimal and binding approvals to origin, session, and plan revision. MFA/CAPTCHA/security prompts remain owner takeover events, never automated.
depends_on: A typed semantic precondition snapshot and plan-revision format.
Stable browser and Mac semantic-state/readback adapters.
Pendant decision events and an authenticated response channel.
Durable job pause/lease invalidation and append-only receipt history.

args.user_asks: “From the pendant, gather the things I need to act on from Mail, Calendar, GitHub, and my currently open private browser tabs; turn each into a sourced action card, create any reversible reminders or drafts, and keep working if I walk away.”
args.why_useful: The owner repeatedly asks to read Gmail, GitHub, and Calendar, but those requests currently fail or require separate surface-specific commands. This is a genuinely cross-body workflow: the pendant captures a short command, relay persists it, the Mac uses granted native AppleScript where browser access is unavailable, the authenticated browser bridge supplies private web context, and the relay returns a concise spoken result plus durable local workbench. It executes reversible follow-up (reminders/drafts) without sending or deleting.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to interpret the short spoken command and speak the final 1–2 sentence digest; use a cheaper background model for extraction, deduplication, prioritization, and action-card drafting.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds, return an initial digest in 15–30 seconds, and continue asynchronously for slow browser sources. The owner can ask for status or completion receipt from the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one realtime turn plus 2–4 background extraction turns per invocation; dominant cost is re-sending multi-source context, so pass compact per-item snippets, timestamps, and hashes rather than full pages. Native Mail/Calendar extraction avoids public-web calls.
args.security_concerns: Private mail, calendar, GitHub, and logged-in tabs remain on the Mac/bridge; only minimized snippets and provenance leave for prioritization. Never send mail, submit forms, delete, or purchase. Creating reminders/notes is allowed by owner policy; drafts must be visibly marked unsent. Require explicit confirmation for any irreversible follow-up.

Native Mail/Calendar/GitHub adapters using the already-granted AppleScript/macOS surface, with browser fallback
A resumable fan-out/fan-in job that persists source cursors and per-item provenance
A pendant-friendly completion/status packet and audio queue integration

args.change: Add a durable cross-surface action-card coordinator between relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge. It accepts one request_id and fan-outs to native AppleScript adapters (Mail, Calendar, Finder/Notes, Messages, Safari/Chrome) plus authenticated browser tabs, normalizes each result into {source, subject, snippet, timestamp, URL/deep-link, confidence, suggested reversible action}, deduplicates by stable hash, writes a local ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/workbench/<request_id> artifact, and emits progress/completion receipts consumable by the pendant. args.why_useful_to_owner: One short pendant request can reliably turn scattered private information into something actionable instead of failing separately on “read gmail,” “read github,” and “read calendar.” The owner gets a spoken digest immediately, a durable reviewable workbench later, and safe reminders/drafts without accidental sends.
args.effort: Medium-high: define typed schema and D1/local persistence, implement native AppleScript adapters and browser result normalization, add fan-out/fan-in and retry/idempotency, then connect briefing/audio receipt generation. Test with bridge offline and Mac sleep.
args.risk: A connector could expose more private text than intended or duplicate an action after retry. Mitigate with source-scoped least-context extraction, stable request/idempotency keys, local-only raw artifacts, redacted relay summaries, and explicit unsent/preview states. If one source fails, report partial completion rather than claiming success; resume from checkpoints.

args.latency_impact: Initial acknowledgement remains realtime; native adapters can return in seconds, browser fan-out in 10–30 seconds. Async receipts prevent blocking voice and allow relay_job_status polling.
args.security_impact: Improves security by making provenance and scope explicit, but introduces a central cross-source join. Keep raw private data on Mac, send only selected snippets, enforce source permissions and confirmation on irreversible actions.
depends_on: A typed action-card/workbench schema

Native AppleScript adapter allowlist for Mail/Calendar/GitHub/browser

args.user_asks: “Use my private apps and logged-in sites to complete this task, but don’t send the underlying private text to the cloud—just return the minimum facts and a preview of what would happen.”
args.why_useful: Today the system can reach separate private surfaces, but it cannot give the owner a trustworthy guarantee that cross-app work is performed with field-level minimization. This would let the owner delegate genuinely sensitive tasks—such as reconciling a calendar commitment with an account form—while keeping raw mail, page contents, and credentials on the Mac/browser. The owner receives only a redacted result and an exact, local before/after preview.
args.model_tier: Use a local/background model on the Mac for extraction, joining, and redaction; use realtime only for the short spoken request and final confirmation summary. The cloud model should receive typed facts or hashes, never raw source text.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 2 seconds; local extraction and preview within 10–20 seconds; long browser work continues asynchronously with a spoken completion receipt.
args.cost_estimate: One small realtime turn plus inexpensive local/background inference. Cloud token cost is substantially lower because only selected fields, confidence, and hashes cross the relay; local storage is a few kilobytes per task plus encrypted audit metadata.
args.security_concerns: The Mac privacy broker must enforce a deny-by-default source/field policy, redact secrets and unrelated text, keep raw artifacts local, and bind every outgoing fact to source, purpose, TTL, and hash. The owner must explicitly approve the minimized payload before any irreversible browser or messaging action; previews remain unsent.

A typed field-level policy and secret detector covering Mail, Calendar, browser DOM, clipboard, and files
Cryptographic provenance/preview records that prove the proposed action used only approved fields

args.change: Insert a Mac-local privacy broker as the mandatory boundary between native/browser execution and relay/model calls. Adapters return structured fields rather than prose; the broker applies a per-task allowlist, secret/PII classification, purpose and TTL, performs joins locally, computes source hashes and a redacted preview, and emits only the approved projection plus an audit receipt. The relay rejects untyped/raw payloads, while action execution consumes the same approved projection so the preview and the eventual operation are cryptographically linked.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate sensitive cross-app work without having to choose between usefulness and exposing entire inboxes, pages, or files. They get a clear proof of what information was used and exactly what will change, while credentials and unrelated private text stay on the Mac.
args.effort: High: define field-level schemas and policy evaluation, implement Mail/Calendar/browser/file adapters, add local secret detection and encrypted audit records, enforce relay validation, and test failure/rollback paths across browser and Mac jobs.
args.risk: Over-redaction may make a task fail; under-redaction could leak sensitive data. Fail closed, explain missing fields locally, allow owner-approved one-time field exceptions, expire projections quickly, and retain only hashes and policy decisions after completion.
args.cost_impact: No hardware cost. Small local CPU/storage overhead; lower cloud token cost because raw content is not uploaded. Background model cost is limited to local extraction/redaction and typed-result prioritization.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–3 seconds for local classification and joining; avoids repeated cloud context transfer and can make total sensitive tasks faster. Long jobs remain asynchronous.
args.security_impact: Materially improves confidentiality and auditability. The broker becomes a high-value local component and must be sandboxed, encrypted at rest, authenticated to the relay, and prevented from silently widening policy scope.
depends_on: A typed field-level privacy policy/schema
Mac-local adapter and secret-classification service
Relay schema validation that rejects raw untyped private payloads
Preview/receipt linkage and owner confirmation protocol

args.user_asks: “Cancel everything you’re waiting to do right now.”
args.why_useful: Today an owner can ask the system to act, but cannot reliably revoke all queued or in-flight authority from the thing they are wearing. A pendant emergency cancel would stop staged browser submissions, queued Mac jobs, and reconnecting workers without finding the laptop or opening a dashboard. It is a distinct safety primitive: cancellation is owner-controlled revocation, not approval, undo, or a report after the fact.
surfaces: pendant detects a deliberate long-press/chord and gives immediate local cancellation feedback
relay atomically records a per-owner revocation epoch and pushes it to connected Mac/browser workers
mac-planner/mac-terminal and browser-extension check the epoch before every side effect and acknowledge cancellation of queued work
faculty-action reports which jobs were cancelled, which were already irreversible, and which require manual follow-up
dashboard and relay-realtime expose the cancellation receipt without exposing page secrets
args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for the stop path. Use firmware and relay logic first; use a cheap background model only to summarize any already-completed effects.
args.latency_budget: Local LED acknowledgement under 200 ms; relay broadcast under 1 second; workers must stop before their next side effect, with a 2-second escalation timeout for stale workers.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; small durable relay write and one broadcast per cancellation. Hardware uses existing button/LED and adds no meaningful power draw.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability:

**“If the app or website changes while you’re doing it, recover and finish the approved task without making me start over.”**

For this to exist, the system needs:

- A shared error taxonomy for stale UI, session expiry, transport failure, changed content, and scope changes.
- A perception → judgement → action repair loop that re-observes the affected tab or app and proposes a bounded replacement step.
- An immutable approval envelope covering the account, recipient, amount, destination, and content.
- Post-action verification proving the intended state, rather than trusting that a click or keystroke was accepted.

Recovery could be automatic for harmless UI changes, but MFA, CAPTCHA, payment, deletion, external sends, or any changed approval field must stop and ask the owner again.

args.subject: Novel action gap: cross-surface commit escrow
args.body: I see a gap beyond existing draft/watch/job/receipt proposals: a durable cross-surface commit escrow. Judgement emits typed intent + expiry + postcondition; relay holds lease, pendant gives local spoken/button confirm, Mac/browser executes, then perception verifies postcondition and action agent reports proof or safely expires. This differs from receipts/undo by gating on verified postcondition and owner-presence.

args.user_asks: “Do this, but only if the right account, page, and conditions are still true; ask me on the pendant at the last safe moment, then prove it actually happened.”
args.why_useful: Today the mind can decide an action and individual surfaces can execute it, but there is no single durable handoff that binds the decision to the correct authenticated browser tab/Mac account, obtains owner-presence confirmation, expires safely, and verifies the resulting world state. This would prevent a stale tab, wrong account, navigation race, or dropped connection from turning an intended action into a silent mistake. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant establishes presence, relay holds the lease, Mac/browser performs the act, and perception proves the postcondition.
surfaces: faculty-judgement emits a typed intent, allowed scope, deadline, and machine-checkable postcondition
relay creates a durable action escrow/lease, binds browser session/tab or Mac target, and waits through reconnects
pendant presents a terse local summary and nonce; owner confirms with the physical button or spoken confirmation, with a short expiry

args.latency_budget: Confirmation prompt should reach the pendant in under 1 second after the target is ready; execution generally under 10 seconds; postcondition verification may take up to 30 seconds and can continue as a durable job after disconnect. Never keep an approval lease alive indefinitely: default 2 minutes, configurable per action.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per invocation depending on whether semantic page comparison is needed; most cost is one planner/verification inference and browser/Mac round trips. Deterministic receipts and lease handling are negligible.
args.security_concerns: The escrow must contain least-privilege target/account/session bindings, a nonce to prevent replay, an expiry, and an explicit irreversible-action class. Do not send credentials or page contents to the pendant; show only a redacted summary and destination. Require fresh confirmation for send/purchase/delete/permission changes, reject if account, URL origin, tab identity, or relevant fields drift, and retain evidence only for the owner's configured short retention. A failed verification must never be reported as success. Browser bridge and bearer-token scope remain trust boundaries.

args.change: Add an Action Escrow state machine between /plan, /execute, the browser command queue, and job receipts rather than treating them as independent calls. Persist one escrow record with intent hash, idempotency key, bound surface/session/tab/account, preconditions, postcondition, owner-confirmation nonce, lease expiry, and evidence pointers. Transition atomically through proposed → target-verified → awaiting-pendant-confirmation → executing → independently-verified → committed, with expired/drifted/failed terminal states. Make /execute refuse an unconfirmed or drifted escrow; make browser/Mac results append evidence to the same record; make faculty-perception close only after a fresh read; expose the complete state through existing /jobs/:jobId and receipts and make undo reference the committed escrow, not merely the last action.

If the owner walks away, a tab changes, Wi-Fi drops, or the wrong account is active, the action expires or stops visibly; if it proceeds, the owner gets proof tied to the exact target and before/after state.

Use idempotency keys, compare-and-set transitions, dry-run simulation, replay tests, and retain the existing receipts/undo path as fallback. args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for target/precondition verification and confirmation; postcondition verification can be asynchronous, with durable job status available immediately.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by binding actions to origin/session/account and requiring a fresh nonce. Evidence must be redacted and short-lived; bearer tokens never go to the pendant. Irreversible actions remain separately classified and confirmation-gated.

args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently distinguish an executor's acknowledgement from a real-world completion. A browser can report a click while the server rejects it, a Mac can report a file write while sync fails, or a relay can lose the result. This gives the owner a trustworthy completion answer based on independent witnesses rather than another optimistic receipt. It is new beyond ordinary job status, receipts, or undo because completion requires correlated evidence from the action surface and a separate observer, with disagreement surfaced as uncertainty.

args.model_tier: Use deterministic witness correlation and state comparison first; use a cheap background model only to normalize heterogeneous evidence. Realtime is needed only to announce a dispute or answer the owner immediately.
args.latency_budget: Normal completion in 2–10 seconds; a dispute should reach the pendant within 2 seconds. Witnesses may continue asynchronously for up to 60 seconds, after which the result is explicitly unknown rather than success.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.04 per action, dominated by one independent readback and occasional normalization; correlation, hashes, and timeouts are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Witnesses must be independent in both credentials and failure mode where possible; never count two reports derived from the same executor as separate proof. Bind evidence to origin/session/tab, nonce, timestamp, and action hash. Redact private page contents, retain only hashes/snippets for short configurable retention, and require owner confirmation before any retry that could duplicate an external side effect.

independent readback adapters for browser, Mac apps, and public APIs

args.change: Introduce a Witness Quorum layer between execution and completion reporting. Every side effect gets an action hash and evidence envelope. The executor's receipt is only one witness; a separate observer must independently re-read the target or an independent confirmation channel. Correlate witnesses by action hash, target binding, and freshness; classify the outcome as witnessed, disputed, or unknown. Expose that classification through job status/receipts and prevent the relay from saying “done” when only the executor acknowledged. For safe operations, allow an explicitly classified retry; for non-idempotent operations, freeze and request owner review.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer about whether something actually happened, rather than a confident “done” that may mean only that a click or API call was attempted. Failures become actionable disputes with evidence, and silent partial completion stops being mistaken for success.
args.effort: High integration effort: evidence envelope and correlation service, independent readback adapters, state/timeout handling, and pendant/dashboard language. Pilot with one browser form and one filesystem operation.
args.risk: Independent observers can disagree or observe stale state; false disputes could annoy the owner, while weak independence could create false confidence. Enforce freshness windows, source independence metadata, explicit unknown outcomes, and never auto-retry irreversible actions.
args.cost_impact: One additional readback per action and small durable evidence records; cheap compared with the risk of an unverified external side effect.
args.latency_impact: Adds 1–10 seconds before declaring completion; the owner can hear “executor finished, verification pending” immediately.
args.security_impact: Evidence must be scoped to the target and redacted. Independent observers need narrowly scoped read access, never broad credential export. Action hashes and nonces prevent replay or cross-job evidence substitution.

Independent observer/readback adapters
A status vocabulary that distinguishes attempted, witnessed, disputed, and unknown
Idempotency classification for retry policy

I discovered the current action surface and recorded a new cross-surface capability plus integration change:

**“Finish the prepared action.”**  
The system should:

1. Show the exact pending browser/Mac changes.
2. Accept approval through a deliberate pendant interaction.
3. Execute ordered steps with idempotency keys and checkpoints.
4. Survive a dropped voice connection.
5. Reconcile ambiguous outcomes instead of retrying blindly.
6. Report what was dispatched, verified, not completed, or remains unknown.

This extends the existing `/plan`, `/execute`, job receipts, browser bridge, Mac actions, pipeline audio, and journal routes rather than duplicating them.

### What is still needed

- A durable relay-side action-bundle/checkpoint store.
- Stable idempotency keys and typed side-effect proof from both Mac and browser workers.
- Pendant approval and pending-state transport.
- Reconnect delivery for the final spoken receipt.
- Dashboard timeline showing each step’s evidence and status.
- Fault-injection tests for disconnects, duplicate delivery, and unknown outcomes.

The pendant currently has **one button and one LED**, so approval and pending state must be designed around those constraints. Its audio path also shares one full-duplex I²S peripheral, so action receipts must not interfere with the 24 kHz playback path.

I do not need another permission request this round; the remaining firmware/audio access and acceptance-criteria requests are still unresolved upstream.

args.security_concerns: The owner must define scope, expiry, allowed surfaces, and permitted reversible actions. Never send, purchase, delete, or submit without fresh confirmation. Store state fingerprints and provenance rather than private page bodies where possible. If authentication expires or evidence conflicts, pause and notify rather than improvising.

Each observation creates a versioned state transition; the runtime may execute only the branch whose preconditions match, records before/after evidence, and emits an exception event when no branch matches. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate the ongoing management of a messy situation without granting open-ended autonomy. args.risk: A faulty precondition could trigger an unintended branch or create notification loops. Require explicit finite branches, strict expiry, monotonic transition IDs, duplicate-event suppression, dry-run simulation, and default stop on disagreement or missing proof.

args.latency_impact: No impact on ordinary voice turns. Branches run on event/schedule latency; unresolved exceptions wait for the next pendant connection or relay wakeup.

args.latency_impact: No steady-state latency change. An explicit test takes roughly 2–5 seconds; packet tagging adds only a few bytes per frame.

Round 78 produced two new records:

- **24 kHz audio conformance sentinel:** a synthetic pendant test that measures capture rate, Opus profile, packet loss, jitter, decode rate, underruns, and CPU headroom across pendant → relay → Mac. It reports the exact failing stage and safely falls back when the path is unhealthy.

A significant current mismatch is now recorded: the prototype captures at **15,625 Hz**, uplinks Opus at **16 kHz**, but plays back at **24 kHz** through a **31,250 Hz** bridge clock. There is no verified end-to-end 24 kHz capture result yet.

I still need, but will not re-request this round:

1. The owner’s authoritative **24 kHz acceptance criteria**.
2. Permission to inspect/build the pendant firmware and connected serial/J-Link devices.
3. A pendant-local calibration test and counters.
4. A typed audio conformance receipt and relay-side profile validation/fallback.

Accessibility and Screen Recording are not required for this audio work.

args.change: Replace the prototype audio front end with a native 24 kHz-capable capture and playback clock domain: use a microphone/codec path whose actual sample clock supports 24 kHz (or an integer-related clock with verified low-jitter conversion), add an independent audio DMA clock rather than deriving capture from the current 15,625 Hz path, and give the bridge a negotiated clock/profile contract. The firmware, Opus configuration, relay, and acceptance tests must all advertise measured rates rather than hard-coded labels.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely superwideband speech instead of a 16 kHz uplink being relabeled or reconstructed as 24 kHz on playback. Voices, environmental cues, and transcription quality improve, and the pendant remains reliable when the network changes because both ends agree on the real clock and profile.
args.effort: High: select and prototype a production audio codec or I2S microphone clocking scheme, revise the pendant/bridge PCB or carrier, update Zephyr drivers and DMA buffering, then requalify Opus, RF power, thermal behavior, and enclosure acoustics. This is a product-hardware change, not a simulator-only patch.
args.risk: A new clock tree can introduce drift, buffer overruns, RF interference, or higher power draw; the development kit must remain supported as a compatibility profile during migration. Recover with a negotiated 16 kHz mode and hardware-in-loop drift tests before deployment.
args.cost_impact: Prototype engineering plus roughly $8–$25 per production unit for codec/clock/audio components and PCB changes; likely tens of milliwatts additional draw depending on codec. API cost is negligible.
args.latency_impact: Potentially neutral or slightly lower once DMA is correctly clocked; initial buffering and resampling tests may add 10–30 ms until tuned.
args.security_impact: No new cloud data is required. Keep raw microphone samples local except during an explicitly active call; expose only negotiated profile and health metrics to the relay.
depends_on: Owner-defined 24 kHz acceptance criteria
Firmware inspection/build access and serial/J-Link hardware-in-loop testing
The previously proposed end-to-end conformance sentinel to prove the new clock path

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Conditional actions with state-bound approval**  
   The owner could say, “If this exact situation occurs, do it,” with permission bound to specific facts, scope, expiry, and a one-time token. The system would re-check conditions immediately before acting and stop if anything changed.

2. **Cross-surface shadow execution**  
   Before acting across the Mac and browser, the system would simulate the plan against redacted state snapshots, show the predicted effects and conflicts, and refuse live execution if the world changed since approval.

These require a shared operation protocol, signed state snapshots, deterministic predicates, read-only Mac/browser adapters, and executors that enforce preconditions rather than trusting stale approvals.

args.latency_impact: Under 1 ms for metadata and duration validation; no additional model call. A corrective resample, if required, adds only the existing codec/resampler latency.

On request, the pendant emits a short deterministic PCM/Opus calibration sequence with monotonic sample counters; the bridge returns captured I2S edge counts and the relay compares declared versus measured duration across capture, uplink, decode, resampling, and playback. Refuse to advertise the 24 kHz playback path as healthy when drift or an unexpected clock domain exceeds the configured tolerance.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust that speech will not slowly change pitch, timing, or truncate when the pendant is worn for a long conversation. args.risk: Calibration could interrupt an active conversation or falsely fail under radio loss. Restrict it to startup/service mode, keep the last known-good coefficients, distinguish transport loss from clock failure, and never overwrite a good calibration with an incomplete run.

args.latency_impact: No normal-path latency. Service calibration takes roughly 1–3 seconds when explicitly requested.
args.security_impact: Calibration carries no owner content and should not upload conversational audio. Authenticate service-mode requests and require a physical button gesture or maintenance authorization before running diagnostics.

args.change: Implement a contract-bound action transaction that sits between /plan, /execute, the job queue, Mac/browser runners, and pipeline events. At plan time, canonicalize target, preconditions, permitted side effects, expiry, and confirmation requirement into contractHash. At execution, atomically acquire a short lease and emit lease/running/paused events; every Mac or browser step must include contractHash, requestId, tab/session affinity, and a before-state digest. Reject stale or mismatched steps. On completion, run postcondition checks against fresh reads, append a signed receipt containing evidence references and the exact contractHash, and only then emit completed for spoken playback. If the pendant playback predicate is absent, emit delivered-to-relay rather than falsely claiming the owner heard it. Reuse jobs/undo-last only for steps explicitly marked reversible.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust “done” or “stopped” in a way they cannot today: a changed webpage, lost tab, stale plan, dropped pendant, or partial Mac failure cannot silently turn into an unverified action. They also get a precise explanation and an undo path for the parts that are genuinely reversible.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and state machine in relay, adapters in Mac/browser runners, postcondition verifier, receipt format, and pipeline event vocabulary; then failure-injection tests for expiry, duplicate delivery, tab replacement, and link loss.
args.risk: A strict verifier may pause work that would have succeeded, and old clients may omit contractHash. Roll out in shadow mode, accept legacy jobs as unverified, and provide an explicit retry with a newly compiled contract. Never auto-replay an irreversible step.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage/CPU for hashes and state; one extra lightweight verification/read per mutation. Background model cost remains low; no extra realtime call except the final concise status.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for lease and local digest checks, plus native time for a postcondition read. Failures become earlier pauses instead of long silent retries.
args.security_impact: Improves replay and confused-deputy resistance by binding every mutation to a short-lived, user-approved contract and tab/session. Keep evidence redacted/minimal and avoid storing private page bodies by default.
depends_on: A durable shared action-contract schema
A verifier for preconditions/postconditions (the pending verify_operation_step/verify_action_proof capability)
A real pendant playback acknowledgement predicate; until then, use the honest delivered-to-relay state
Existing receipt/undo implementation and browser request-id/tab affinity

args.change: For the product pendant (not the current prototype DK), add a low-power coin vibration motor with a dedicated GPIO driver and a physical acknowledgement button, while retaining the status LED. Define three local patterns: short pulse for lease acquired, double pulse for paused/needs approval, and long pulse for verified completion/failure. The relay sends only compact state transitions; firmware renders them locally and stops the pattern on button acknowledgement. Include brownout-safe default-off and a watchdog timeout so a stale lease cannot leave the motor running.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know that an action is waiting, paused, or truly finished even in a noisy room, while walking, or when playback is unavailable. It makes the device an honest physical hand instead of assuming a spoken message was heard.
args.effort: Medium hardware/firmware work: prototype a vibration driver and button on the next board, add BLE/cellular state messages, and test tactile patterns against clothing and battery conditions. Do not modify or flash the current unconnected development kit without approval.
args.risk: Extra vibration could annoy or wake the owner, and a stuck GPIO could drain the battery. Keep patterns brief, configurable, and watchdog-bounded; allow a silent mode and fall back to LED/audio. Treat the button as acknowledgement only, never authorization for an irreversible action unless the contract explicitly requests it.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$3 BOM increase for motor, transistor, and button; brief pulses typically add tens of mWh/day, with negligible idle draw.
args.latency_impact: Local state feedback is near-instant and continues through a short relay/audio interruption; it does not add server latency.
args.security_impact: No sensitive content is exposed; only abstract state codes are delivered. Button events must carry a nonce/contract hash so stale acknowledgements cannot authorize another job.
depends_on: A durable action lease/state vocabulary
Firmware event handling and a product enclosure/PCB revision
The pending physical_action_confirmation and action_lease_indicator semantics

args.change: Add a compensating-recovery planner for partially completed cross-surface actions. When a job stops after step n, derive a bounded recovery graph from each completed step's declared compensation (for example, restore a draft field or move a file back), distinguish safe compensation from irreversible external effects, and present the owner a spoken/inspectable choice: leave as-is, compensate selected reversible steps, or resume from the exact checkpoint after a fresh precondition check. Store the partial-state snapshot and compensation result in the same receipt, rather than treating jobs/undo-last as a single global undo.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A failed multi-step request will not leave them guessing whether half the work happened or risk an indiscriminate undo. They can recover a draft or file operation safely while being warned clearly about the message, purchase, or submission that cannot be rolled back.
args.effort: Medium: extend job step metadata with compensation descriptors and state snapshots, add recovery planning and explicit user choice, then test crashes between every pair of steps across Mac and browser adapters.
args.risk: A compensation can itself fail or have side effects, and snapshots may contain private data. Permit only adapter-declared reversible operations, require fresh verification before compensation, encrypt/minimize snapshots, and mark the transaction unresolved if recovery cannot be proven.
args.cost_impact: Small durable metadata overhead; one cheap background planning call only for failed multi-step jobs. No additional realtime model call beyond the status prompt.
args.latency_impact: No cost on successful jobs; failed jobs gain seconds for recovery analysis, with immediate paused status first.
args.security_impact: Prevents unsafe blanket replay/undo and limits recovery to the original contract scope, tab/session, and owner approval. Redact sensitive field values from receipts unless needed for recovery.

Per-step contractHash, idempotency key, and before-state evidence
Mac/browser adapters declaring which operations are compensatable
The pending verify_operation_step/verify_action_proof capability

Round 83 findings:

- **Mac bridge:** online.
- **Pendant:** not connected; no playback or button acknowledgement can be verified.
- **Browser:** Chrome bridge is offline with zero tabs.
- **Granted capabilities this run:** none new.

I recorded two useful changes:

1. **Contract-bound action transactions:** bind `/plan` → `/execute` → jobs → Mac/browser steps to a short-lived contract hash, preconditions, tab/session identity, postcondition evidence, and an honest completion state. Without pendant playback confirmation, the system must say “delivered to relay,” not “you heard it.”
2. **Partial-failure recovery:** when a multi-step action stops halfway, generate bounded compensating actions for only explicitly reversible steps. Do not use a blanket undo or replay an irreversible step.

The second proposal was accepted as new. The first was recognized as connective work close to existing transaction-ledger ideas, so its important remaining gap is the wiring between the existing routes—not another standalone feature.

What is still needed:

- A shared action-contract and lease schema.
- `verify_operation_step` / `verify_action_proof` behavior for fresh preconditions, postconditions, and evidence.
- A real pendant playback ACK and action-state feedback protocol.
- `audio_path_probe` plus the authoritative 24-kHz acceptance criteria.
- The pending offline intent spool, physical confirmation, and lease-indicator semantics.
- Owner timezone and action/approval policy.
- A connected pendant before firmware or audio behavior can be tested.
- Manual owner approval before any firmware build involving secrets, hardware flashing, or hardware changes.

I will not re-request the already-pending grants or attempt to flash the unconnected prototype.

args.user_asks: “When I walk away from my Mac, put my private work into a safe state; when I come back, restore exactly what I was doing.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets automatic, presence-bound privacy and continuity: sensitive browser sessions can be locked or obscured when the pendant leaves, while non-sensitive work remains recoverable. Returning to the desk restores the prior workspace without requiring them to remember a security ritual.
surfaces: The pendant emits a rotating, privacy-preserving proximity nonce over BLE and gives a local tactile cue when the protection boundary changes
The Mac bridge measures authenticated proximity, captures an encrypted workspace manifest, locks or masks designated applications and private browser tabs, and later restores only the recorded state
The browser extension labels tabs by sensitivity and can replace private pages with a local lock screen while preserving tab/session identity
The relay stores only the encrypted manifest and receives presence transitions, surviving a Mac sleep or temporary link loss
faculty-judgement selects the policy and asks once which applications/tabs are protected; faculty-action executes the transition and reports a compact result to the pendant
args.model_tier: Use a small/background model only to classify workspace sensitivity and reconcile restoration conflicts; proximity transitions and lock/mask actions must be deterministic local code. Realtime is unnecessary except for an optional spoken warning.
args.latency_budget: Protection should begin within 2 seconds of confirmed departure and restoration within 3 seconds of return. If confidence is ambiguous, leave the workspace protected rather than oscillating.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost during normal use; occasional background classification is roughly $0.001–$0.01 per workspace change. Main cost is engineering and modest encrypted manifest storage.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must not broadcast a stable owner identifier or location. Use rotating authenticated nonces, local key agreement, replay protection, and a grace period for brief signal loss. Never transmit page contents or credentials to the relay. Restoration must require the same pendant identity and a fresh nonce; if the pendant is lost, the owner can revoke its key from the Mac. Sensitive browser pages should be masked or locked, not closed or reloaded, to avoid data loss.
missing: A product pendant with authenticated BLE proximity and a secure key store
A Mac-local presence daemon integrated with lock/mask APIs and sleep/wake handling
Browser-extension sensitivity labels and a tab-preserving lock surface
An encrypted workspace-manifest store with key revocation and conflict handling
Owner-configurable protected application/tab policy and a clear local override
built_from: browser session/tab affinity and browser action routes

args.user_asks: “If I hold the pendant button, revoke this device and stop anything acting as me everywhere.”
args.why_useful: Provides a fast, physical kill switch when the owner suspects a lost pendant, exposed screen, or runaway automation. It can stop queued Mac/browser work and revoke the pendant’s authority even when the owner cannot reach the Mac or speak safely.
surfaces: The pendant detects a deliberately long press locally, shows a distinct LED/tactile pattern, and sends a signed emergency-revoke event when connectivity exists
The relay immediately marks the pendant key revoked, cancels queued jobs, invalidates action leases, and fans out the event to all reachable surfaces
The Mac bridge locks the session, terminates or freezes agent-owned processes, and removes temporary credentials and browser bridge authorization
The browser extension closes or locks designated authenticated tabs and invalidates its command channel without deleting user data
faculty-action returns only a terse revoked/partially-revoked status and retains a durable incident receipt for later owner review
args.model_tier: Deterministic firmware and relay control path; no model call is needed for activation or propagation. Use a cheap background model only later to summarize what was stopped and what could not be reached.
args.latency_budget: Local revoke cue immediately; relay fan-out under 1 second when connected; unreachable surfaces remain revoked at the relay and must fail closed when they reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per event; one signed event and small receipt. Engineering cost is concentrated in credential scoping, cancellation, and fail-closed reconnect behavior.
args.security_concerns: Require a long press plus a clearly different local cue to reduce accidental activation, but do not require speech or network access. Protect the revoke key in secure device storage, prevent replay, and make revocation monotonic. Since a panic action can destroy unsaved work, lock/freeze before termination and preserve only minimal diagnostic metadata. Re-enrollment must require deliberate owner action on a trusted surface.
missing: Secure per-pendant revoke key and monotonic revocation registry
Firmware long-press handling that works offline
Relay fan-out and fail-closed reconnect protocol
Mac process/credential quarantine and browser bridge invalidation hooks
Owner-controlled re-enrollment and incident review UI

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability:

### Presence-bound privacy handoff

The owner should be able to say:

> “When I walk away from my Mac, put my private work into a safe state; when I come back, restore exactly what I was doing.”

This does not exist today. It would require:

- A pendant with authenticated, rotating BLE proximity credentials.
- A Mac-local presence daemon that detects departure and return.
- Sensitivity-aware browser tabs and an authenticated browser lock surface.
- An encrypted workspace manifest preserving tab/application state without sending page contents to the relay.
- Relay-side key revocation and conflict handling.
- Deterministic local protection and restoration; no model call should control the security transition.

I also recorded a second capability for a **physical emergency revoke switch** on the pendant. It was accepted as connective work but flagged as close to existing action-stop ideas; the genuinely missing pieces are the secure offline revoke key, fail-closed reconnect behavior, and credential quarantine across Mac and browser.

args.user_asks: “Handle this end to end, and keep me in control.” The system should carry out a reversible multi-step task across my logged-in browser and Mac, pause only at irreversible steps, and let me approve, cancel, or resume it from the pendant.

args.change: Implement a relay-owned Action Transaction Coordinator between the existing /execute, Mac jobs, and browser command queue. Default closed on missing/contradictory evidence; retain receipts and offer manual resume. Never auto-retry effect=write unless the step declares an idempotency key and the target confirms it.

args.security_impact: Improves security by making approval scoped to an exact step and expiring it with the lease. Private evidence remains surface-local where possible; transaction IDs and hashes cross the relay, not secrets.

- Event-driven reachability/precondition notifications

transcript.text:
Recorded two new proposals:

1. **Deferred cross-device handoff** — speak a task to the pendant while away, then have it resume automatically when both the Mac and authenticated browser are available, producing a proof-backed review packet.

2. **Cross-surface Handoff Lease protocol** — durable intent capture, presence attestation, single-executor leases, expiry, idempotency, and unified Mac/browser receipts to prevent duplicate or stale execution.

For this to exist, the system needs a durable handoff object, authenticated co-presence detection, a lease-aware scheduler, cross-surface evidence schema, and pendant controls for cancelling or expiring pending work.

- Mac bridge is online, with AppleScript automation broadly granted.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable, so GUI/computer-use automation is still not ready.
- Browser extension is offline with 9 pending commands; browser actions cannot be trusted until it polls again.
- No pendant is currently connected or paired.

I recorded a new cross-node capability: **Deferred Intent with semantic verification**. A request would receive an expiry-bound lease, idempotency key, allowed surfaces, approval class, and explicit postcondition. The relay could resume it after reconnecting, Mac/browser agents could execute bounded steps, faculty-perception would verify the result, and the pendant would eventually receive a concise success/failure/unknown receipt.

What I still need:

1. **Owner action:** pair/connect a pendant.
2. **Owner action:** bring the browser bridge online.
3. **Owner action:** grant Accessibility and Screen Recording to AI Pendant Agent if GUI control is desired.
4. **Engineering:** add the shared intent/lease record and a typed postcondition-verification callback between action and perception.
5. **Engineering:** define retry rules that distinguish safe/idempotent work from irreversible actions.

The current stack can execute commands and retain receipts; the missing piece is the reliable, verified handoff between “a command ran” and “the owner’s goal was accomplished.”

args.user_asks: “Pause that job here and let me resume it from the exact next step on whichever device is available, with a compact explanation of what already happened and what will happen next.”

A portable checkpoint would make the hive act like one continuous worker: the Mac can stop after a verified boundary, the relay can preserve the checkpoint, the browser can reattach its session, and the pendant can resume or cancel without replaying completed side effects.

args.cost_estimate: Typically under $0.02 per handoff; cost is dominated by one short checkpoint summarization, not the ordinary action calls.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoints must contain opaque references and redacted state, not copied private page contents or credentials. Bind each checkpoint to the owner/session and an expiry. Never resume an irreversible step merely because a checkpoint exists; require the same approval class and fresh confirmation when needed.
missing: A portable, append-only checkpoint schema with completed-step receipts, verified state, next-step preconditions, and browser session affinity
Atomic pause barriers in Mac and browser runners so no step is half-committed when a handoff is made
A resume planner that rejects stale checkpoints and reconciles them against fresh perception before continuing

Each affected job records whether it stopped before or after its last committed step. args.cost_impact: Negligible per-action API cost; small firmware and relay implementation cost, with no added model calls.
args.latency_impact: Relay cancellation should reach online Mac jobs in under 500 ms; offline browser commands are marked cancelled and prevented from later execution.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **bounded conditional action policies**.

The owner should be able to say:

> “If this changes while I’m away, carry out the fallback I approved—within these limits—and tell me exactly what you did.”

This is not merely monitoring or a durable job. It connects:

1. **Perception** detecting a real state transition across private browser pages, Calendar, Mail, or Mac files.
2. **Judgement** selecting a still-valid, explicitly bounded branch.
3. **Action** executing that branch through the correct browser or Mac surface.
4. **Relay/pendant** reporting the triggering evidence, result, or need for confirmation.

It requires a new conditional-policy registry and evaluator with:

- Explicit predicates and branches
- Time limits, spending/action limits, destinations, and expiry
- Debouncing so page noise cannot trigger repeated actions
- Immediate revocation
- Fresh confirmation for irreversible or out-of-policy steps
- Receipts tied to both the triggering evidence and policy version

args.user_asks: “Do this for me, and keep going until you can prove whether it actually happened.” The pendant should capture my intent, the judgement agent should turn it into a bounded action bundle, the Mac or private browser should execute it, and perception should independently verify the resulting state before telling me it is done.
args.why_useful: Today an action can be reported as successful even when the UI did nothing, or a browser command can sit pending while the owner assumes it ran. This gives the owner one honest answer: completed with evidence, safely queued with an expiry, or failed with the exact handoff that broke. It works across the pendant, always-on relay, Mac automation, and authenticated browser rather than being another Mac-only feature.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture/confirm the short owner utterance; use a cheaper background model for plan normalization, retries, and evidence reconciliation. No expensive model is needed for routine status polling.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge intent on the pendant in under 2 seconds; execute when a surface is available; verify within 10 seconds for Mac actions and up to 60 seconds for browser actions. If unavailable, persist a queued state rather than spinning or claiming completion.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one short realtime turn plus 1–3 background calls per action; dominant cost is evidence reconciliation and any vision fallback, which should run only when typed/API verification fails.
args.security_concerns: The relay stores only a signed action bundle, expiry, sensitivity class, and receipts—not page contents by default. Irreversible effects require an explicit owner confirmation bound to the exact final parameters; stale approvals, changed targets, and browser-session changes invalidate the bundle. Never treat a relay_result or UI success alone as proof.
missing: A durable two-phase action-bundle state machine (prepared/approved/dispatched/verified/failed/expired) shared by relay and Mac
Typed precondition and postcondition probes for common Mac and browser actions
Independent verification route that can refuse the word done when no authoritative state change is observed
Pendant delivery acknowledgements once a real pendant is connected
Browser extension availability and owner-granted Accessibility/Screen Recording for vision-only actions

args.change: Add a durable, idempotent action-bundle protocol spanning relay and Mac agent. Each bundle contains a requestId, normalized target, exact parameters hash, preconditions, postconditions, expiry, confirmation token (if needed), and preferred executor. Dispatch must first re-check readiness and preconditions; execution emits receipts; faculty-perception independently probes the postcondition through typed APIs/AppleScript/browser inspection. Only a verified postcondition transitions the bundle to completed. Offline browser, missing permissions, absent pendant, timeout, or ambiguous UI transitions to queued/blocked/unknown with a retry policy and never to done. Surface the same state and evidence capsule in relay speech and dashboard, and make retries/undo use the same idempotency key.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops having to guess whether “done” means done. Long or cross-device requests survive leaving the house, avoid duplicate sends, and explain exactly why work is waiting or unverifiable.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and D1/local persistence, executor adapters, postcondition probes, and dashboard/relay rendering; then fault-injection tests for offline and timeout cases.
args.risk: A strict verifier may mark real work unknown when a site has no readable confirmation, so provide a safe “needs review” state and never auto-retry irreversible actions. Recovery is manual review or a bounded retry with the same idempotency key.
args.cost_impact: Small D1/local storage and polling cost; background model only for ambiguous evidence. Vision calls are exceptional. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds one verification round trip after execution; fast typed probes remain under seconds, while browser verification may take tens of seconds.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by binding approval to exact parameters and expiry, minimizing replay and duplicate execution. Evidence should be redacted by sensitivity class before relay storage.
depends_on: A durable job runner and existing receipt/undo records
A typed verification/proof tool (currently requested but not yet available)
Browser extension recovery/online polling for private pages
Actual pendant connection before spoken delivery acknowledgements can be trusted

transcript.text:
Round 97 findings:

- Mac bridge and relay are reachable.
- Mac agent still reports `ready=false`: Accessibility and Screen Recording are not granted.
- Browser extension is offline with 9 pending commands.
- No pendant is currently connected.
- Existing browser jobs demonstrate the core reliability problem: commands can time out or fail, and receipts do not prove that the intended state changed.

I recorded two proposals:

1. **Verified cross-device action bundles** — an intent survives handoffs between pendant, relay, Mac, and browser; execution is only reported as complete after an independent postcondition check.
2. **Pendant execution-status feedback** — local haptic/RGB indications for accepted, waiting, executing, verified, blocked, and failed states, with no false success indication when the link drops.

What I still need:

- A durable action-bundle state machine connecting `/plan`, `/execute`, jobs, receipts, relay state, and verification.
- A typed proof/postcondition tool that can independently confirm Mac and browser effects.
- Browser extension recovery and polling.
- Owner-granted Accessibility and Screen Recording for vision-only Mac actions.
- A real pendant connection before delivery acknowledgements or local completion indicators can be trusted.
- Hardware/firmware update capability if the haptic/RGB status proposal is accepted.

The largest remaining unknown is **authoritative verification**: what source of truth should prove each class of action actually occurred, rather than merely proving that an automation command returned.

args.user_asks: “Before you send or change anything irreversible, make sure the final target still matches what I originally meant—even if the task crossed apps or took an hour.” The system should detect semantic drift in recipient, amount, account, attachment, destination, or scope across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, and interrupt only when the final operation differs materially from the owner’s captured intent.
args.why_useful: Today an approval can become stale or detached from the exact operation after a long workflow, a page refresh, a changed tab, or a handoff between agents. This protects the owner from sending to the wrong person, paying the wrong amount, modifying the wrong account, or approving a broader action than they requested without forcing confirmation for every harmless step.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize and compare structured intent fields. Use realtime only to ask the owner a short clarification when a material mismatch is detected; deterministic hashes and policy rules should handle ordinary matches.
args.latency_budget: No noticeable delay for reversible steps. For an irreversible step, compare the final parameter capsule in under 500 ms; if ambiguous, pause and ask one concise question rather than executing.
args.cost_estimate: Usually a small structured comparison with negligible model cost; one realtime turn only for genuine mismatches. The dominant cost is extracting final fields from an unstructured page when typed browser evidence is unavailable.
args.security_concerns: Store a minimized intent capsule rather than raw speech or page contents, with sensitivity labels and expiry. Bind confirmation to the exact normalized parameters, session/tab identity, and destination. A changed recipient, amount, or scope invalidates approval. Never silently broaden an action because an agent inferred more context.
missing: A canonical intent capsule schema shared by judgement, action, Mac, and browser
Field-level semantic diffing with materiality policies by action type
A mandatory pre-commit hook that can pause every executor, including AppleScript and browser commands
Final-state extraction for recipients, amounts, attachments, and scopes from each supported app
A concise pendant/dashboard clarification and resume protocol

args.change: Implement an intent-drift firewall at the final-commit boundary. Faculty-judgement emits a canonical, expiring intent capsule with typed fields (actor, recipient, destination, amount, object, scope, attachments, side effects, and allowed alternatives). Every Mac, AppleScript, and browser executor must submit its final mutation capsule to the firewall before committing. The firewall performs deterministic field comparisons plus a policy-driven semantic comparison, invalidates stale approvals when tab/session/page identity or material fields change, and returns allow, block, or ask-owner-with-diff. Resume tokens must be single-use and parameter-bound; retries cannot bypass the firewall.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets protection against a subtle but costly failure: the system completes the workflow it inferred rather than the action the owner actually authorized. They see only a short exception when something materially changed, not repetitive approval prompts.
args.effort: High integration effort: define the shared schema, instrument every executor, build field extractors and policy tests, then fault-test changed recipients, amounts, tabs, attachments, and partial retries.
args.risk: Overly strict comparison may interrupt legitimate edits, while weak extraction may miss drift. Default uncertain cases to ask-owner for irreversible effects, allow only explicitly safe alternatives, and retain a human-readable before/after diff for recovery.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent capsules and deterministic comparisons; occasional cheap semantic-model calls and rare realtime clarification. No hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second for typed fields; roughly 1–3 seconds when semantic extraction is required, before an irreversible commit.
args.security_impact: Reduces replay, confused-deputy, wrong-recipient, and stale-approval risk. Capsules must be encrypted or minimized, expire quickly, and exclude raw private page content unless needed for the diff.
depends_on: A shared action protocol across relay and local Mac agent
Typed final-value extraction from browser and app adapters
An owner confirmation/resume channel on the pendant or dashboard

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded by tool call:

- **Owner capability:** Before any irreversible action, the system verifies that the final recipient, amount, destination, attachment, scope, and side effects still match the owner’s original intent—even after delays, retries, app changes, or cross-device handoffs.
- **Required change:** Add an intent-drift firewall at the final commit boundary. It must compare a short-lived, structured intent capsule against the exact final mutation, invalidate stale approvals, and return **allow**, **block**, or **ask the owner with a before/after diff**.

This is not available today because executors lack a shared intent schema, field-level final-state extraction, and a mandatory pre-commit hook spanning Mac, AppleScript, and browser actions.

args.risk: A false-ready result could still time out; use a hard deadline and retain the existing timeout. A public fallback must never receive private URLs, cookies, or page text; require explicit URL classification.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage; reduces failed realtime/model calls and Mac round trips.
args.latency_impact: Healthy actions add <2 seconds; unhealthy actions return in ~2 seconds instead of ~45 seconds.
args.security_impact: Positive if URL classification is deny-by-default and private session IDs cannot be sent to the public backend.

args.why_useful: The owner can currently start work through the voice surface but cannot physically interrupt it when their attention is elsewhere or a workflow behaves unexpectedly. args.security_concerns: A false press could cancel useful work, so require a deliberate hold and local vibration/LED confirmation. A relay-wide revocation sequence checked by every Mac and browser executor before each step.

transcript.text:

The owner should be able to hold the pendant button to:

- stop queued actions,
- prevent the next workflow step from starting,
- propagate a signed revocation through the relay,
- and receive a receipt stating exactly what had already changed.

This requires new pendant firmware stop handling, relay-wide revocation checked by every executor, durable action leases, and honest cancellation receipts for in-flight operations.

args.user_asks: Give you a bounded standing permission for a kind of task—such as scheduling meetings within my working hours or reordering a specific item below a price cap—and have you carry out matching actions across my Mac and logged-in browser without asking me every time, while stopping and asking when any limit, ambiguity, or sensitive field is encountered.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must either approve every individual mutation or grant broad, opaque control. A constrained authority lets routine work happen while preserving their intent: the mind can decide and act within explicit limits, but cannot silently widen scope or improvise past a boundary.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only when obtaining or changing the owner's authority policy. Compile policies and evaluate routine actions with a cheaper background model plus deterministic checks; escalate ambiguous matches to realtime or the owner.
args.latency_budget: Policy evaluation should be sub-100 ms locally at the relay/Mac boundary. Routine approved actions can complete asynchronously within seconds; boundary crossings should interrupt promptly and request confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per routine action because matching, caps, time windows, and field classifications are deterministic. Model cost is reserved for ambiguous task-to-policy matching and concise exception explanations.
args.security_concerns: Permissions must be least-privilege, explicit, revocable, expiring, and scoped by app/site/account, action type, amount, time window, and sensitive-field class. Never infer permission from conversational tone. Show an action preview when a policy is first used; require confirmation for sends, purchases, deletions, identity/security changes, or any over-cap action. Keep credentials on the Mac/browser and record policy version plus evidence, not secrets or raw private-page contents.

Cross-surface identity/account binding so a rule cannot accidentally apply to the wrong browser session or Mac account
A safe exception path that pauses at the exact violating step and asks for one-time approval without broadening the standing rule

args.change: Introduce a capability-token authority layer shared by faculty-judgement, relay, Mac, and browser executors. Judgement issues a signed, narrow token containing policy ID/version, permitted operation grammar, resource/account scope, quantitative limits, sensitive-field exclusions, expiry, max uses, and required confirmation levels. Before every concrete Mac or browser step, the executor verifies the token against the normalized step and consumes a nonce; a mismatch hard-stops without dispatch. The relay exposes revoke-all and token-status, while the Mac/browser surfaces return the exact failed predicate. Persist only token hashes and audit metadata, and support an offline revocation cache on the Mac so a stale grant cannot survive relay loss.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate routine authority without handing the system a vague promise or permanent access. A mistaken interpretation becomes a blocked step with a precise explanation, not an accidental purchase, message, deletion, or account change. Revoking authority remains possible even during a network outage.
args.effort: High: policy grammar, signed-token issuance/verification, normalization of Mac and browser actions, nonce/replay protection, revocation distribution/cache, UI for review/revoke, and adversarial boundary tests.
args.risk: Normalization bugs could either over-block useful work or authorize a step that only appears equivalent. Fail closed, use conservative operation grammars, require explicit confirmation for unknown verbs, and ship test vectors for account, amount, recipient, time, and sensitive-field boundaries.
